Some naturalists posit a relationship to the common mudcrab, while one mythic account holds that Emperor Crabs devolved into mudcrabs after forsaking divine pursuits. The species is believed extinct long before the Third Era, though unreliable reports of oceanic sightings persist.
topic_desc_basic: Emperor Crabs were gigantic crustaceans once native to Vvardenfell, described as cathedral-sized. Their immense shells have been repurposed in Dunmer architecture, most notably at Ald'ruhn. House Redoran, whose arms and armor draw from crab imagery, claims to have hunted them to extinction. The species is believed long dead, though some naturalists suggest a relationship to the common mudcrab.

title: False Gods
topic_desc: The term 'False Gods' denotes the Tribunal—Almalexia, Vivec, and Sotha Sil—condemned by dissenting voices as usurpers who stole divine power from the Heart of Lorkhan. Critics, including the Dissident Priests and the Maulborn, argue that the Tribunal's godhood is an abductation rooted in corruption and deceit rather than true divinity. These detractors claim the Three have broken their covenant, misused the tools of the Enemy, and abandoned their people, demanding worship born of fear rather than reverence. The Ashlanders preserve similar accusations, maintaining that the Tribunal's ungodly actions mock the gods and endanger all of Morrowind.
topic_desc_basic: The term 'False Gods' refers to the Tribunal, accused by their critics of stealing divine power rather than earning it. Dissenting groups like the Ashlanders and the Maulborn claim the Three demand worship out of fear, have broken their promises, and threaten Morrowind through their misuse of profane power.

title: Morrowind's economy
topic_desc: Morrowind's economy has historically operated as an agrarian aristocracy, where free farmers, herders, and fishermen were governed by the Great Houses and their noble councils. Since the Imperial occupation, however, a profound transformation has occurred, particularly on Vvardenfell. The Dunmer are increasingly developing a mercantile economy modeled on the Empire. While Imperial authority—embodied by the Emperor, the law, and the legions—provides overarching governance, economic life is now driven by trade in crafts and goods, integrating Morrowind more deeply into broader commercial networks.
topic_desc_basic: Morrowind was traditionally an agrarian aristocracy of free farmers and herders ruled by the Great Houses and their noble councils. Since the Imperial occupation, particularly on Vvardenfell, the Dunmer have been developing a mercantile economy on the Imperial model, driven by trade in crafts and goods rather than agriculture.

title: Oneness
topic_desc: Oneness is the Skaal principle of universal balance, governing the harmony between all natural elements—flora, fauna, stone, and wind. Bestowed by the All-Maker, this equilibrium is the source of the Skaal's spiritual power. When the natural order is maintained, the community draws strength from this unity; when disrupted, their power diminishes. The Skaal attribute such imbalances to outside forces, particularly the Empire, whose presence disrupts the delicate harmony and weakens the tribe's connection to the land.
topic_desc_basic: Oneness is the Skaal concept of natural balance among all living things and the land. Granted by the All-Maker, this harmony gives the Skaal their spiritual power. When this balance is disturbed, their strength fades.

title: slavehunters
topic_desc: Slavehunters are trackers and enforcers employed to capture and return escaped slaves to their owners, operating primarily within Morrowind's legal slave economy. House Dres and other plantation owners rely on them to pursue fugitives. They patrol known escape routes, port towns, and border regions, watching for runaway Khajiit and Argonian laborers. While not a formal guild, their trade is sanctioned by Morrowind law, and they act with legal authority to restrain and return bondsmen. Individual hunters like Anes Hlaren, Garyn Girith, and Sadal Doren exemplify the profession's persistent pursuit of escapees.
topic_desc_basic: Slavehunters are trackers hired to capture and return escaped slaves to their owners in Morrowind. Sanctioned by law, they patrol towns, docks, and escape routes searching for fugitive Khajiit and Argonians. House Dres and other plantation owners depend on them to recover runaway bondsmen.

title: Telvanni tower urban style
topic_desc: The urban style of Telvanni settlements is defined by the wizard's tower, a massive organic structure grown and sculpted from the stems, caps, and root-like holdfasts of giant native mushrooms. These fantastic forms dominate the landscape, serving as the seat of the ruling mage. Below, the village consists of smaller mushroom pods hollowed out to house craftsmen and commoners. Open-air markets frequently feature giant cages where slavemasters display their wares, reflecting the brutal economics underpinning Telvanni society.
topic_desc_basic: Telvanni settlements are dominated by the wizard's tower, a fantastic organic structure grown from giant native mushrooms. Smaller mushroom pods are hollowed out for craftsmen and commoners, and open-air markets often feature giant cages displaying the wares of slavemasters.

title: undead creatures
topic_desc: Undead creatures on Vvardenfell encompass spectral, fleshy, and fleshless revenants. Ghosts include ancestor ghosts, guardian ancestors, wraiths, and dwarven variants such as dwarven ghosts, guardians, and wraiths. Fleshy revenants are known as bonewalkers, appearing in standard and greater forms. Fleshless revenants comprise skeletons, skeleton archers, warriors, and champions, alongside bonelords. Vampires, considered profane undead, have been hunted almost to extinction. These beings are broadly categorized by their animating forces and corporeal states, with ancestral and dwarven spirits often tied to cultural or ruined contexts, while bonewalkers and skeletons serve as mindless guardians or hostile encounters.
topic_desc_basic: Undead creatures on Vvardenfell include ghosts such as ancestor spirits and dwarven spectres, fleshy revenants like bonewalkers, and fleshless skeletons including bonelords. Vampires, considered profane undead, have been hunted almost to extinction.

title: almoners
topic_desc: Almoners serve as the charitable fundraisers within the Imperial Cult, tasked with gathering alms from members and sympathizers of the faith. The Cult relies heavily on these donations to finance its charitable works across Vvardenfell and the broader province. Success in securing generous contributions offers a recognized path for advancement through the ranks of Imperial Cult service. Those seeking to join this vocation are directed to Iulus Truptor at the Imperial Chapels in Ebonheart.
topic_desc_basic: Almoners are members of the Imperial Cult responsible for collecting alms and donations from the faithful. These contributions fund the Cult's charitable endeavors. Aspiring almoners should seek out Iulus Truptor at the Imperial Chapels in Ebonheart.

title: alteration
topic_desc: Alteration is one of the six schools of magic, defined by the manipulation of the physical world and its natural properties. Unlike Illusion, which alters perception, Alteration produces changes recognized by all observers. Its practice demands uncommon sense: the caster imposes their will upon reality, persuading natural forces that the suggested alteration is easier to follow than existing physical law. Subtle changes succeed more readily, and all effects are temporary, as reality inevitably reasserts itself. Practitioners master effects such as water breathing and walking, jumping, levitating, burdening, opening and locking, and creating shield barriers against physical and elemental damage.
topic_desc_basic: Alteration is one of the six schools of magic. It involves manipulating the physical world and its natural properties. Mages of this school cast spells for water breathing and walking, jumping, levitating, opening locks, and creating shield barriers against damage.

title: ancestral burial tombs
topic_desc: Ancestral burial tombs are the consecrated subterranean vaults where House Dunmer inter their dead and honor their forebears. Ancestor worship is a cornerstone of Dunmer culture, and these catacombs serve as both sacred sites of veneration and fortified repositories safeguarded by bound ancestral spirits against desecration. They dot the Morrowind countryside, such as the Ginith and Rethandus tombs near Ald'ruhn. Necromancers and tomb-robbers who violate these sanctuaries face lethal magical retribution from the undead guardians.
topic_desc_basic: Ancestral burial tombs are sacred Dunmer crypts used to inter the dead and venerate forebears. Located throughout Morrowind, examples include the Ginith and Rethandus tombs near Ald'ruhn. These sanctuaries are typically guarded by undead ancestral spirits.

title: Apographa
topic_desc: The Apographa constitute the 'hidden writings' of the Tribunal Temple, comprising secrets restricted to the highest echelons of the priesthood and inquisition. They stand in deliberate contrast to the Heirographa, the Temple's collected priestly writings available to the orthodox faithful. The Temple's suppression of these texts forms a central doctrinal dispute with the Dissident Priests, who accuse the orthodox hierarchy of concealing truths from its followers. In defiance of Temple authority, the Dissident Priests have gathered as much of the Apographa as possible within their sanctuary at Holamayan, preserving censored knowledge that challenges official accounts.
topic_desc_basic: The Apographa are the 'hidden writings' of the Tribunal Temple, secrets known only to the highest levels of priesthood and inquisition. They contrast with the Heirographa, the Temple's public priestly writings. The Dissident Priests consider the Temple's concealment of these texts a hiding of truth from followers, and have gathered what they can of the Apographa at Holamayan.

title: Arena
topic_desc: The Arena Compound sits between the Redoran and Telvanni cantons in Vivec City. The domed structure seats hundreds for public entertainment and combat sports, featuring underground dressing rooms, training facilities, and animal pens. As an ancient venue, it hosts honorable duels, settles feuds, and decides matters of succession. Beneath the public pits, the canton secretly houses the Morag Tong headquarters, offering specialized training to its operatives.
topic_desc_basic: A domed combat venue in Vivec City, situated between the Redoran and Telvanni cantons. It hosts public entertainment, martial competitions, and traditional duels used to settle feuds and questions of succession.

title: Argonian Mission
topic_desc: The Argonian Mission is Black Marsh's diplomatic embassy to the Vvardenfell District, situated in the southwest corner of Ebonheart. Overseen by the Argonian consul Im-Kilaya, the facility represents provincial interests before the Grand Council. Beyond its formal diplomatic role, the mission shelters newly escaped Argonian slaves, a covert function linked to the Twin Lamps. This dual purpose places the mission at the uneasy intersection of Imperial law and Dunmer customs, as harboring fugitives remains illegal under Morrowind's institutions.
topic_desc_basic: The Argonian Mission in Ebonheart serves as Black Marsh's diplomatic embassy to Vvardenfell District. The facility represents provincial interests and provides shelter for Argonians recently escaped from bondage.

title: Ashlander worship
topic_desc: Ashlander worship centers on the ancestor cult, into which every tribe member is born. This foundational practice binds each clan to its revered forebears. Alongside this tradition exists the distinct Nerevarine cult, a small sect of seers and guardians preserving prophecies of the legendary hero's return. The Urshilaku tribe currently sustains this cult, with Ashkhan Sul-Matuul serving as its Warrior-Protector and wise woman Nibani Maesa as its Oracle-Seer.
topic_desc_basic: Ashlander worship revolves around the ancestor cult, a clan-based practice into which all tribe members are born. A separate, smaller Nerevarine cult is maintained by prophetic wise women and their warrior-guardians, who await a legendary hero's return.

title: Ashlanders and foreigners
topic_desc: Ashlanders regard foreigners and their imperial culture as intrusions upon ancestral Morrowind, desiring their expulsion alongside the false gods they represent. At minimum, they seek to be left undisturbed. While they consider attacking the unarmed shameful, armed outsiders who violate clan laws face lethal retribution. Present imperial power prevents open warfare, yet many would willingly sacrifice themselves in a conflict against the Empire if victory seemed achievable.
topic_desc_basic: Ashlanders resent foreign intrusions and wish outsiders would leave Morrowind entirely. They consider attacking the unarmed dishonorable, but will kill armed outsiders who violate clan customs. Though they lack the power to fight the Empire, many would eagerly die in a war against it if victory were possible.

title: Ashlanders in war
topic_desc: Ashlanders wage war differently from settled peoples. Inter-tribal conflict typically takes the form of raids intended to demonstrate strength and secure wealth and respect, while champions settle matters of sport and honor through ritual duels. In full tribal wars, however, hunters and herders fight alongside ashkhans and champions, wielding spear and bow. Such conflicts are inherently cruel and undertaken with great reluctance, as the sparse Ashlander population makes every life too precious to squander.
topic_desc_basic: Ashlanders rarely wage war like settled peoples. They raid other tribes to prove strength and gain respect, and champions duel for honor. In true tribal wars, hunters and herders join ashkhans with spear and bow. These wars are cruel and reluctant, as their few numbers make every life too dear to waste.

title: becoming a lich
topic_desc: Lichdom represents the deliberate transition from mortal life into a state of conscious undeath, typically pursued by powerful mages seeking to escape temporal limitations. The precise rituals for this transformation remain shrouded in speculation and dark lore. One widely circulated—though likely facetious—recipe claims that combining the heart of a lich, a dragon's tongue, and the flesh of a well-ridden horse guarantees the transformation. Genuine accounts of the process are obscure, and the validity of such folk recipes remains highly dubious among serious scholars.
topic_desc_basic: Lichdom is the deliberate transformation into conscious undeath, typically sought by mages wishing to evade mortality. While one popular recipe claims that combining a lich's heart, a dragon's tongue, and well-ridden horse's flesh ensures this transition, such folkloric formulas are widely regarded as unreliable.

title: household slaves
topic_desc: Household slaves in Morrowind serve as personal property bound to domestic service, agricultural labor, or craft production within Dunmer great houses and freeholder estates. The institution persists under Imperial tolerance as an ancient Dunmeri right, with markets openly trading Khajiit, Imperial, Bosmer, Altmer, Breton, and Redguard captives. Slaves are typically marked with branded guar-hide bracers signifying ownership. Abolitionist pressure from the Imperial Cult and sympathetic House Hlaalu has not displaced the practice, which remains entrenched in traditional Telvanni and Dres holdings.
topic_desc_basic: Household slaves in Morrowind are persons held as property for domestic and agricultural labor. Dunmer great houses openly trade Khajiit, Imperial, Bosmer, Altmer, Breton, and Redguard captives in slave markets. The institution persists as an ancient Dunmeri right despite Imperial and abolitionist opposition.

title: literacy
topic_desc: Literacy is fundamental to the Empire. Imperial policy holds that teaching the Dunmer to read and instructing them in a common heritage are essential to maintaining Morrowind within the province. House Hlaalu supporters actively champion this campaign, arguing that widespread literacy binds Morrowind to Imperial civilization. Mages Guild schools participate in these efforts, though they frequently lack sufficient instructional texts. Foundational primers, such as ABCs for Barbarians and The Annotated Anuad, are employed to teach basic reading and shared cultural history. The campaign remains a point of cultural friction, as traditional Dunmer society relies heavily on oral traditions and Temple teachings rather than Imperial literary education.
topic_desc_basic: Imperial policy views literacy as fundamental to keeping Morrowind within the Empire, requiring that the Dunmer be taught to read and learn of their common heritage. House Hlaalu and Mages Guild schools actively support this campaign, though instructional books remain scarce.

title: Master Barelo
topic_desc: Gilvas Barelo serves as abbot of Holamayan Monastery and heads the secret order of Dissident Priests operating within the Tribunal Temple. From this secluded island refuge, Barelo provides spiritual and organizational leadership to those who question Temple orthodoxy while maintaining devotion to the faith. His position requires balancing doctrinal criticism with genuine religious conviction, sheltering dissenting voices against Temple authority. Holamayan's remote location affords some protection from Ordinator enforcement, though Barelo's dual role as both Temple abbot and secret order leader remains precarious.
topic_desc_basic: Gilvas Barelo is the abbot of Holamayan Monastery and heads a secret order of Dissident Priests. He leads those who question Tribunal Temple orthodoxy while maintaining their devotion to the faith from the monastery's secluded refuge.

title: Peace in Black Marsh
topic_desc: The so-called peace currently prevailing in Black Marsh follows the suppression of tribal uprisings by the Imperial Expeditionary Force. Rumors of this pacification, circulating through ports such as Soulrest, suggest that the restoration of order will allow the reconstruction of Argonian plantations and mining operations. Local trading interests anticipate the subsequent resumption of valuable exports, including timber and gold. The stability remains dependent on continued Imperial military occupation and the successful rebuilding of the province's extractive infrastructure.
topic_desc_basic: Imperial forces have reportedly put down tribal uprisings in Black Marsh. Traders in ports like Soulrest expect the pacification will allow plantations and mines to be rebuilt, resuming the region's gold and timber exports.

title: Recall the Legions
topic_desc: Recall the Legions refers to the potential withdrawal of Imperial military forces from the eastern provinces, including Morrowind, to reinforce the heartland amid escalating unrest in Cyrodiil. With the Empire facing internal instability and threats to the Emperor's safety, soldiers stationed abroad may be redeployed to protect the capital. Such a withdrawal would critically weaken the Imperial grip on distant territories, leaving provincial garrisons undermanned and vulnerable to local insurrections or external pressures. The prospect underscores the severe strain on Imperial resources and the fragile state of the Septim dynasty's authority at the close of the Third Era.
topic_desc_basic: Recall the Legions refers to a potential redeployment of Imperial military forces from eastern provinces like Morrowind back to Cyrodiil. Escalating unrest in the heartland threatens the Emperor, and troops may be withdrawn from frontier garrisons to secure the capital, weakening the Empire's hold on its distant territories.

title: restoration
topic_desc: The Restoration discipline governs the spell effects of the College of Restoration, which heals, restores, and fortifies bodily attributes and abilities, cures disease, and protects against malign influences. Its primary spells mend wounds and restore vitality, but the college also augments attributes such as strength, endurance, intelligence, and agility, and can enhance resistance to elements, magic, and disease. Absorption magics are sometimes classed under this discipline, though Mysticism also claims them. Despite its immense utility, the Mages Guild does not consider Restoration one of the great schools. Its benevolent nature makes it highly popular among religious workers. Knowledge of these spells appears to have developed more recently than other schools; as late as the Second Era, even cures for disease were rare.
topic_desc_basic: The College of Restoration encompasses spells that heal wounds, cure disease, restore vitality, and fortify bodily attributes and abilities. It also provides protection against malign influences. Despite its great utility and popularity among religious workers, the Mages Guild does not count it among the great schools.

title: sewers and ruins
topic_desc: Beneath the city of Mournhold lies a vast subterranean network of sewers and ancient ruins. The poor and lawless inhabit these depths, eking out an existence in the shadowy passages. Beyond the sewers lie the ruins of Old Mournhold, a source of treasure and peril. The subterranean network is notoriously dangerous, harboring lethal threats capable of overwhelming the unprepared. Adventurers venture below seeking fortune in the old ruins, though many never return.
topic_desc_basic: Beneath Mournhold lies a vast network of sewers and ancient ruins. The poor and lawless inhabit these depths, while the ruins of Old Mournhold hold treasure for daring adventurers. The passages are notoriously dangerous, harboring lethal threats to the unprepared.

title: study for the priesthood
topic_desc: Study for the priesthood within the Tribunal Temple represents a path of spiritual devotion and communal service dedicated to Almsivi—Almalexia, Sotha Sil, and Vivec. Aspirants typically renounce secular attachments and former transgressions, dedicating their lives and resources to the Temple. This sacred vocation involves rigorous doctrinal instruction alongside practical service, such as teaching or fulfilling administrative duties as directed by the Temple hierarchy. Ordination demands both scholarly understanding of Tribunal dogma and demonstrated commitment through alms and obedience, reflecting the Temple's core principles of compassion and duty.
topic_desc_basic: Study for the priesthood is a Tribunal Temple vocation requiring aspirants to dedicate themselves to Almsivi. Candidates often surrender worldly possessions to the Temple and undergo doctrinal training while serving the community through teaching and other duties as required.

title: suppress the Apographa
topic_desc: The suppression of the Apographa refers to the Tribunal Temple's deliberate concealment of heterodox texts and hidden writings that complicated official doctrine. Vivec acknowledges ordering this suppression, citing the Apographa's volatile mixture of truth, falsehood, and speculation as a threat to the faithful's certainty. The Temple required unwavering belief to power the Ghostfence against Dagoth Ur, making any doctrinal doubt an existential peril. However, Vivec now privately questions whether this policy was a mistake, suggesting that by eliminating doubt, the Temple preserved only the faith of the indifferent while potentially alienating those whose conviction was most vital.
topic_desc_basic: The suppression of the Apographa was the Tribunal Temple's effort to conceal heterodox writings that blended truth, falsehood, and speculation. Vivec ordered this censorship to prevent doubt from weakening the faithful, whose belief was essential to sustain the Ghostfence. Vivec now questions whether this policy mistakenly preserved the faith of the indifferent while losing the devotion of the strong.

title: Ash-chancre
topic_desc: Ash-chancre is an acute blight disease that afflicts the victim's behavior, driving them toward erratic and aggressive outbursts. It is contracted from corprus beasts and other blight monsters roaming the blighted regions of Vvardenfell. Sufferers often experience intense irritability and hostility, sometimes attributing their rage to external provocation rather than the infection. As a blight illness, it resists conventional treatments and requires specific curative magic or potions to remedy. Its behavioral symptoms make infected individuals dangerous, as the afflicted may attack even those offering aid.
topic_desc_basic: Ash-chancre is an acute blight disease that alters a victim's behavior, causing severe irritability and aggression. It is contracted from corprus beasts and other blight monsters.

title: Swamp Fever
topic_desc: Swamp fever is a mild common disease that drains a victim's strength and disrupts normal behavior. Its primary symptoms include elevated body temperature and delirium, though it presents no easily visible external signs. The affliction is known to be contracted from mudcrabs. Standard curative measures include potions of cure disease or restoration spells, and the Temple of the Tribunal typically provides healing to sufferers. Outside settled areas, finding a curative can prove difficult, as wandering priests are not always available.
topic_desc_basic: Swamp fever is a mild common disease that saps a victim's strength and causes high body temperature and delirium. It is contracted from mudcrabs and can be cured with a standard potion of cure disease or a restoration spell.

title: ash ghoul
topic_desc: Ash ghouls are distorted, half-human, half-beast creatures transformed by a mysterious force into powerful magical beings. They are highly intelligent, aggressive, and dangerous, associated in some way with the Devil Dagoth Ur. Found dwelling within Sixth House sanctuaries, these creatures possess formidable magical abilities and represent a disturbing corruption of mortal form. Scholars seek their captured souls to study the unnatural forces that reshape them, though such research carries significant risk given their aggressive nature and the malevolent power behind their existence.
topic_desc_basic: Ash ghouls are distorted, half-human, half-beast creatures transformed by a mysterious force. Highly intelligent and dangerous, they wield powerful magic and are associated with Dagoth Ur. They inhabit Sixth House caves and are greatly feared.

title: Divine Metaphysics
topic_desc: Divine Metaphysics is a Dwemeris text authored by the tonal architect Kagrenac, outlining the theoretical framework behind the construction of Anumidium. The work describes how a new god might be created through the obedience of the Ehlnofey—also called the Earth Bones—and the application of sacred tones upon the Heart of Lorkhan, using Kagrenac's tools. The text remains largely incomprehensible without a translation key such as the Hanging Gardens of Wasten Coridale. Even with partial translation, scholars find its meaning deeply contested: some dismiss it as the ramblings of a lunatic, while others recognize its significance as the essence of Kagrenac's theories. The Dwemer's attempt to enact these principles at Red Mountain ended in their disappearance, suggesting the theories did not work as intended.
topic_desc_basic: Divine Metaphysics is a Dwemeris text describing how the Dwemer attempted to create a new god, Anumidium, using Kagrenac's tools and sacred tones upon the Heart of Lorkhan. Written in Dwemeris, it requires a translation key to interpret, and scholars remain divided on its true meaning and significance.
aliases: Divine Metaphysics Adapted to the Meanest of Intellects

title: Crosier of St. Llothis
topic_desc: The Crosier of St. Llothis is a sacred staff relic of the Tribunal Temple, said to contain the undefeated spirit of Saint Llothis the Pious. Its enchantments adversely affect the wielder, rendering it ill-suited for combat despite its holy significance. The crosier was carried into Red Mountain by Voruse Bethrimo, Captain of the Buoyant Armigers, who fell while protecting his retreating subordinates near Dagoth Ur's citadel. The relic remains lost within the stronghold of Dagoth Ur, awaiting recovery from the forces of the Sixth House.
topic_desc_basic: The Crosier of St. Llothis is a sacred Tribunal Temple staff said to hold the undefeated spirit of Saint Llothis the Pious. Its enchantments harm the wielder, making it unfit for combat. It was lost in Red Mountain when Buoyant Armiger Captain Voruse Bethrimo fell defending his retreating forces near Dagoth Ur's citadel.

title: the Udyrfrykte
topic_desc: The Udyrfrykte is a legendary beast of Nord folklore, long dismissed as a children's tale to frighten the young. The creature is ancient, described as black with glowing eyes and a ravenous taste for human flesh. According to legend, it was sealed within an ice cave on the shore of Lake Fjalding in Solstheim for centuries. The beast recently proved terrifyingly real when mysterious fire melted the ice blocking its lair, freeing it to attack the mead hall of Thirsk. Slaying the Udyrfrykte is considered a feat worthy of the greatest warriors, celebrated in bardic song.
topic_desc_basic: A legendary beast from Nord folklore, long considered merely a children's tale. The Udyrfrykte is an ancient, black creature with glowing eyes and a taste for human flesh, said to have been sealed for centuries in an ice cave near Lake Fjalding on Solstheim.

title: Bloodworm Helm
topic_desc: The Bloodworm Helm is a necromantic crown crafted from trollbone by the lich Mannimarco, the King of Worms. Though beautiful in construction, many find the artifact repulsive due to its morbid nature. It grants the wearer greater skill at Conjuration, the ability to turn undead, drain the essence of living foes, and summon a skeletal minion; if the wearer is undead, their attacks are also made more powerful. Mannimarco left the helm behind when he ascended to godhood during the Warp in the West. The artifact is currently held by the Museum of Artifacts in Mournhold, where it remains a popular yet controversial exhibit.
topic_desc_basic: The Bloodworm Helm is a trollbone necromantic crown crafted by the lich Mannimarco, the King of Worms. Though beautiful, many find it repulsive. It enhances Conjuration, turns undead, drains essence, and summons skeletal minions. Mannimarco left it behind when he ascended during the Warp in the West. It is currently displayed in Mournhold's Museum of Artifacts.

title: Bow of Shadows
topic_desc: The Bow of Shadows is a Daedric artifact forged by Nocturnal. It grants its wielder invisibility and enhanced speed. The ranger Raerlas Ghile once received the bow for a failed mission and reportedly used it to slay many foes before perishing. The Dunmer assassin Dram later wielded it, allegedly using it to kill Prince A'tor at the Battle of Hunding Bay and during the Stros M'Kai rebellion. Yagrum Bagarn lists the bow among artifacts of unimaginable significance in Tamrielic Lore. It currently rests in the Venim Ancestral Tomb in Vvardenfell's Grazelands.
topic_desc_basic: The Bow of Shadows is a Daedric artifact attributed to Nocturnal. It grants invisibility and speed to its wielder. The assassin Dram famously used it during the Stros M'Kai rebellion. It is currently lost somewhere in Vvardenfell.

title: Dragonbone Cuirass
topic_desc: The Dragonbone Cuirass, sometimes called the Dragonbone Mail, is a legendary artifact of extraordinary protective power, rivaling the Lord's Mail and the Ebony Mail in its defensive enchantments. Fashioned from the bones of a dragon, its creation represents a mastery of armoring that contemporary smiths cannot replicate. The cuirass currently rests within a sealed Dwemer closet in the Central Vault of Mudan Grotto, southwest of Ebonheart. Its provenance and the circumstances of its interment alongside Dwemer mechanisms remain uncertain, though its status as a peerless relic is undisputed; curators of Mournhold's Museum of Artifacts recognize it as a defining artifact and value it at thirty thousand gold.
topic_desc_basic: The Dragonbone Cuirass, or Dragonbone Mail, is a legendary armor fashioned from dragon bone. Its craftsmanship surpasses contemporary smithing, and its protective qualities rival those of the Lord's Mail and Ebony Mail. The artifact is currently hidden within the Dwemer vaults of Mudan Grotto near Ebonheart.

title: Eleidon's Ward
topic_desc: Eleidon's Ward is a legendary enchanted tower shield crafted for the Breton knight Eleidon. According to legend, a baron commissioned the shield at great expense to honor Eleidon after he rescued the baron's daughter from a warlord. The shield bears a powerful enchantment that heals the wielder's wounds. In the fifth century of the First Era, the revered warrior Mordrin Hanin was entombed with Eleidon's Ward in the cave of Ibar-Dad on Vvardenfell. Yagrum Bagarn later listed the shield among artifacts of unimaginable significance in Tamrielic Lore, and Divayth Fyr has expressed interest in recovering it. The shield currently remains interred within Mordrin Hanin's crypt.
topic_desc_basic: Eleidon's Ward is a legendary enchanted tower shield crafted for a renowned Breton knight. Legend holds that a grateful baron spent his entire fortune commissioning the shield after Eleidon rescued his daughter. The ward bears a powerful healing enchantment and is currently believed to rest in an ancient tomb on Vvardenfell.

title: Fang of Haynekhtnamet
topic_desc: The Fang of Haynekhtnamet is a dagger carved from a fang of the mythical wamasu Haynekhtnamet, crafted in an exquisite Argonian style. According to legend, a score of Nords fought the beast for seven days in Black Marsh, believing it to be a dragon; a survivor took the fang as a trophy. The blade mysteriously retains the creature's magical properties, allowing its wielder to shock opponents. Conflicting accounts exist regarding its exact origin, with some placing its retrieval in the Shadowfen region during the Second Era, noting the blade inflicted disease upon those it struck. The artifact has surfaced occasionally throughout history.
topic_desc_basic: The Fang of Haynekhtnamet is an Argonian-style dagger carved from the fang of the mythical wamasu Haynekhtnamet. Nords reportedly slew the beast after a seven-day battle, mistakenly believing it a dragon. The blade retains the creature's magical essence, allowing its wielder to shock opponents.

title: Helm of Oreyn Bearclaw
topic_desc: The Helm of Oreyn Bearclaw is an enchanted skull-shaped helmet that fortifies the wearer's agility and endurance. Its cultural attribution is fiercely contested. Bosmeri tradition names it for the legendary Valenwood hunter Oreyn Bearclaw, who purportedly slew the witch-serpent Glenhwyfaunva and performed numerous great deeds before perishing in the Knahaten Flu; his clan eventually fractured and lost the relic. Conversely, Orcish tradition identifies it as the Helm of Kharag gro-Khar, crediting Oreyn's Orc companion with the heroic feats and dismissing the hunter's fame as stolen reputation. Malacath himself has laid claim to the artifact, reinforcing the Orcish perspective. The dispute remains unresolved, with both cultures asserting rightful ownership over the helm and its legacy.
topic_desc_basic: The Helm of Oreyn Bearclaw is an enchanted skull-shaped helmet that bolsters the wearer's agility and endurance. Its origin is disputed: Bosmer claim it belonged to the legendary hunter Oreyn Bearclaw, while Orcs identify it as the Helm of Kharag gro-Khar, crediting an Orcish hero with the famed deeds. Malacath himself claims the relic.

title: Mehra Milo
topic_desc: Mehra Milo is a Dunmer priestess of the Tribunal Temple who serves as a librarian in the Hall of Wisdom and Justice within Vivec's Temple Canton. Recognizable by her copper hair and copper eyes, she is a covert member of the Dissident Priests, a faction that challenges Temple orthodoxy. Her position affords her access to restricted theological texts and suppressed apocrypha, making her a vital conduit for heterodox scholarship. Because the Temple scrutinizes outlanders and suspects dissent within its ranks, Milo must exercise considerable caution; her associations, if discovered, would invite severe censure from the Ordinators. She remains a significant figure for those seeking knowledge of the lost prophecies and alternative interpretations of Tribunal doctrine.
topic_desc_basic: Mehra Milo is a Dunmer priestess and librarian working in the Hall of Wisdom and Justice in Vivec. Distinguished by her copper hair and eyes, she is known as a quiet scholar of Temple doctrine, though rumors suggest she holds sympathies with the Dissident Priests who question official Tribunal teachings.

title: Ring of Phynaster
topic_desc: The Ring of Phynaster was crafted by the Altmer Hero-God Phynaster to protect himself during his adventurous life, granting him heightened resistance to poison, magicka, and shock. These enchantments allowed him to survive for hundreds of years. The ring is inextricably linked to its creator; it will not remain with any other owner indefinitely, inevitably vanishing to a new resting place for another bearer to discover. It is currently reputed to rest within Senim Ancestral Tomb on Vvardenfell.
topic_desc_basic: A legendary artifact created by the Altmer Hero-God Phynaster. It grants its wearer strong resistance to poison, magicka, and shock. The ring is bound to its creator and inevitably vanishes from any subsequent owner to seek a new bearer.

title: Robe of the Lich
topic_desc: The Robe of the Lich is a powerful artifact of necromantic origin. Scholarly accounts offer conflicting theories regarding its creation: some claim it was torn from a destroyed lich, while others posit it was crafted by a wicked mage seeking the power of undeath without its inherent drawbacks. The robe is intrinsically tied to Gedna Relvel, an infamous Mournhold priestess condemned for practicing forbidden magics. Having transformed herself into a lich, Relvel survived for centuries beneath the city. The artifact currently rests with her in the sealed tomb beneath Mournhold's Temple canton, awaiting discovery. Its potent enchantments pose a grave danger to any who wield it without extreme caution.
topic_desc_basic: The Robe of the Lich is a powerful necromantic artifact. Its origins are disputed; some claim it was taken from a destroyed lich, while others believe a wicked mage created it to gain the power of undeath without the usual drawbacks. It remains a dangerous and coveted item.

title: Mantle of Woe
topic_desc: The Mantle of Woe is a powerful enchanted robe steeped in necromantic magic. It greatly augments the wearer's magicka and conjuration, making it coveted by practitioners of the dark arts. However, the Mantle exacts a terrible toll: it renders the wearer perpetually vulnerable to sunlight and weakens their defenses against physical harm. More insidiously, the garment exerts a corruptive influence, amplifying dark ambitions and eroding moral restraint until the wearer becomes a thrall to their own hunger for power. The Mantle was discovered in Rimhull, a cavern system beneath a Skaal village on Solstheim, where it had lain for an unknown period. Its origins remain obscure, though old stories hinted at its presence in those depths.
topic_desc_basic: The Mantle of Woe is a cursed enchanted robe associated with necromancy. It greatly empowers the wearer's magicka and conjuration but inflicts constant sun damage and weakens personal defenses. The Mantle is known for its corruptive influence, slowly dominating those who wear it with hunger for dark power.

title: kagouti
topic_desc: Kagouti are large, aggressive bipedal reptiles native to Morrowind and parts of Black Marsh, closely related to alits, guar, and wormmouths. They are distinguished by thick head crests, huge tusks, and a formidable natural armor. Older individuals may develop multiple pairs of fangs. Kagouti exhibit complex social behaviors, including distinctive vocalizations for mating and territorial disputes, with dominant males leading packs. Their hides are valued for leatherworking, used in clothing and household goods. Travelers and merchants rightly fear them, as kagouti are fiercely territorial and will readily charge perceived threats.
topic_desc_basic: Kagouti are large, aggressive bipedal reptiles native to Morrowind, recognized by their huge tusks and thick head crests. They travel in territorial packs led by dominant males and are known to charge travelers on sight. Their tough hide is harvested for leather goods.

title: Rockjoint
topic_desc: Rockjoint is an acute common disease that markedly impairs a victim's manual dexterity through painful swelling and progressive immobility of all joints. The affliction is known to be contracted from domesticated guar—widely herded throughout Morrowind's settled districts—and the dusky alit, a lesser predatory beast of the ashlands. As a common disease, Rockjoint responds readily to standard temple blessings, curative potions, and restoration magic, though untreated cases can severely hamper a sufferer's capacity to wield weapons or perform delicate labor.
topic_desc_basic: Rockjoint is an acute common disease causing painful swelling and immobility of all joints, significantly reducing manual dexterity. It is contracted from domesticated guar or dusky alit. Standard curative magic and potions are effective against it.

title: Grahl
topic_desc: Grahl, sometimes called ice trolls, are tusked, brutish creatures native to Solstheim's ice caves. The Skaal regard them as the Unholy Beasts, aspects of the Adversary, though whether they are evil spirits or great beasts remains uncertain. They hunt alone or in packs, rending armor and flesh with formidable claws and tusks. Unlike common trolls, grahl possess tails, icy dorsal spikes, and sometimes a third eye. They share their mainland cousins' regeneration and fire vulnerability. Grahl parts hold alchemical and practical value: their eyeballs are used in potions or mummified into carrying pouches, and grated skin brews a tea for curing skin ailments.
topic_desc_basic: Grahl, or ice trolls, are dangerous, tusked creatures inhabiting Solstheim's ice caves. The Skaal call them Unholy Beasts, aspects of the Adversary, though their true nature remains uncertain. They hunt alone or in packs, tearing armor and flesh with powerful claws and tusks.

title: alit
topic_desc: The alit is a tailless, bipedal reptilian predator common to the grasslands and ash wastes of Vvardenfell. Though related to the guar and built like its larger cousin the kagouti, the alit possesses a more vicious temperament and cunning attack instinct. It is distinguished by a large head, protruding jaw, and short, stumpy legs, giving the impression of a mobile toothy mouth. While omnivorous, its aggressive disposition makes it a noteworthy hazard in the wild. Ashlanders regularly hunt the creature, valuing its tough hide as a serviceable multi-purpose leather and trade good.
topic_desc_basic: The alit is a tailless, bipedal predator common to Vvardenfell's grasslands and ash wastes. Resembling its larger relative the kagouti, it has a large head, protruding jaw, and stumpy legs. Ashlanders hunt the alit for its tough hide, which serves as serviceable leather.

title: ancestor ghost
topic_desc: Ancestor ghosts are the translucent spirits of deceased Dunmer forebears, bound to the mortal plane to guard clan tombs and ancestral shrines. Revered in Dunmeri ancestor worship, they are aggressive toward trespassers but pose limited physical threat. Their incorporeal nature renders them immune to mundane weapons; only silvered, enchanted arms or destructive sorcery can harm them. Conjurers may also summon and command these spirits for protection or menial tasks, a practice sometimes viewed with ambivalence by traditionalist Temple faithful.
topic_desc_basic: Ancestor ghosts are spirits of the Dunmer dead that aggressively guard clan tombs. They are incorporeal and immune to mundane weapons, requiring silvered or enchanted arms and sorcery to strike. Sorcerers may also summon and control them.

title: ascended sleeper
topic_desc: Ascended Sleepers are the most powerful and final known stage of the ash creature mutations, transformed from Dunmer cultists of the Sixth House through Dagoth Ur's Divine Disease. These highly intelligent, aggressive beings rank highly within the revived Sixth House, surpassed only by Ash Vampires. They possess formidable magical abilities, unleashing destructive fire, frost, and shock attacks while afflicting foes with deadly Blight diseases. Ascended Sleepers appear as distorted half-mer, half-beast entities with tentacled faces. They exhibit a detached demeanor, acting above petty concerns and holding no fear of death, believing that slaying merely returns them to a dream-state from which they will awaken. When destroyed, their forms dissipate, leaving behind ash salts.
topic_desc_basic: Ascended Sleepers are powerful, highly intelligent ash creatures associated with Dagoth Ur and his Sixth House. Transformed from Dunmer cultists by the Divine Disease, these distorted half-mer, half-beast beings rank among the most dangerous servants of the Devil. They wield destructive magic and deadly Blight diseases.

title: ash slave
topic_desc: Ash slaves are humanoid creatures warped and driven mad by a mysterious corrupting force associated with Dagoth Ur and the Sixth House. Once presumably mortal, they survive as deranged, aggressive beings, their bodies and minds broken by the blight emanating from Red Mountain. They attack any who approach, serving as a terrifying manifestation of Dagoth Ur's spreading influence across the island of Vvardenfell.
topic_desc_basic: Ash slaves are humanoid creatures transformed by a mysterious force into deranged, aggressive beasts. They are dangerous and are associated in some way with the Devil Dagoth Ur.

title: Ash Zombie
topic_desc: Ash Zombies are humanoid creatures warped by Dagoth Ur's corrupting influence into deranged, aggressive beasts. Despite their skulls appearing largely hollow, they retain a disquieting intelligence and pose a significant threat. These unfortunate beings are associated with the Sixth House and share a mysterious connection to the Devil Dagoth Ur, representing the horrifying transformations wrought by his power.
topic_desc_basic: Ash Zombies are aggressive, humanoid beasts transformed by a mysterious force. Though their skulls appear empty, they remain dangerously intelligent. They are connected to the Devil Dagoth Ur.

title: bonelord
topic_desc: Bonelords are revenant guardians that protect the tombs of clan and kin, often found among the undead that haunt ancestral barrows. They command skeleton minions in death as they may have commanded servants in life. The bones of these skeletal attendants yield bonemeal, a finely ground powder with modest magical properties valued in certain alchemical and necromantic practices. Summoning magic can also call forth bonelords to serve.
topic_desc_basic: A bonelord is a revenant that guards the tombs of clan and kin. It commands skeleton minions whose bones yield bonemeal, a ground powder with modest magical properties.

title: clannfear
topic_desc: Clannfear are ferocious reptilian Lesser Daedra resembling muscular bipedal lizards with bony head crests, curved beaks, and spiked tails. They possess a berserk fighting passion and feral intelligence, attacking by biting, clawing, and pouncing. Though of low status among Daedra and incapable of using tools, they are relentless and formidable, sometimes branded to display loyalty. Every Daedric Prince is said to maintain legions of clannfear, though they are often attributed to Mehrunes Dagon. They occasionally linger near Daedric ruins on Nirn and are commonly summoned by conjurers. Their hearts hold modest magical properties valued by alchemists.
topic_desc_basic: The clannfear is a fierce, green, lizardlike bipedal Daedra. These ferocious Lesser Daedra attack through biting, clawing, and pouncing, and are often associated with Mehrunes Dagon despite serving many Princes. They are commonly summoned, and their hearts are prized by alchemists for modest magical properties.

title: daedroth
topic_desc: Daedroths are crocodile-headed, bipedal Daedra most commonly associated with Molag Bal, though they also serve Princes such as Sanguine, Sheogorath, Vaermina, and Mehrunes Dagon. Hulking and reptilian, they possess animalistic tendencies but remain dangerous foes, wielding powerful clawed arms and a vicious bite alongside moderate magical ability, including flame-spitting and poison or shock projection. They roam the wilds of Oblivion as beasts roam Nirn, and some have been observed speaking Tamrielic or wielding simple arms. Linguistically, 'daedroth' is the proper singular form of 'Daedra,' though common parlance reserves the term for these specific creatures, using 'daedroths' for the plural and 'Daedra' as the generic designation. Their hearts hold modest magical properties.
topic_desc_basic: Daedroths are crocodile-headed, bipedal Daedra typically associated with Molag Bal. These hulking, reptilian creatures are dangerous foes, attacking with powerful claws, a vicious bite, and magical abilities such as spitting fire or poison. Their hearts possess modest magical properties valued by alchemists.

title: flame atronach
topic_desc: Flame atronachs are elemental Daedra native to Infernace, a collective Oblivion plane of molten rock and fire. Commonly appearing as feminine floating humanoids composed entirely of flame, they possess some intelligence but remain largely chaotic and unorganized. Conjurers summon them as guardians or laborers, traditionally through Koron's Peremptory Summons. The Direnni clan notably perfected binding them into diverse shapes, including animal forms. When banished or destroyed, their remains yield fire salts, a valuable alchemical compound, and atronite stones. They inhabit numerous Daedric realms and are widely encountered across Tamriel.
topic_desc_basic: Flame atronachs are elemental Daedra associated with fire, often conjured to serve as guardians. They typically appear as floating feminine forms made of flame. When banished, their remains yield fire salts, a useful alchemical substance.

title: Fork of Horripilation
topic_desc: The Fork of Horripilation is a cursed Daedric artifact created by Sheogorath, who affectionately calls it Forky. Outwardly a mundane iron fork that smells faintly of roast beef, it carries a potent enchantment that excites and synergizes surrounding magicka. When wielded as a weapon, it inflicts Fork's Wound, a debilitating curse that drastically drains or stunts the wielder's own magicka reserves while dealing negligible physical damage. Sheogorath delights in forcing mortals to employ the Fork as a weapon, finding horripilation—the standing of hairs on end from cold, fear, or excitement—in their dread and suffering. Accounts of its use often involve impossible or absurd tasks set by the Mad Prince.
topic_desc_basic: The Fork of Horripilation is a cursed Daedric artifact created by Sheogorath. Appearing as a mundane iron fork, it inflicts Fork's Wound on any wielder foolish enough to use it as a weapon, drastically draining their magicka while dealing negligible harm.

title: frost atronach
topic_desc: Frost atronachs are elemental Daedra native to the coldest reaches of Oblivion, sometimes called frost daedra, ice atronachs, or water atronachs. These bulky humanoid constructs of ice possess limited intelligence and are largely unorganized, with many individuals bearing names beginning with the word Nomeg. They can manifest unbound in the wild or be conjured through summoning magic to serve as guards or laborers. When banished or destroyed, their remains yield crystalline frost salts of alchemical value. Conjurers can alter summoning rites to produce varied bestial forms, though such shapes are notoriously difficult to control. The more powerful frost monarchs are distinguished from common frost atronachs.
topic_desc_basic: Frost atronachs are elemental Daedra composed of ice, native to the coldest reaches of Oblivion. They may appear unbound in the wild or be conjured by mages to serve as guardians. When banished, their remains yield valuable frost salts used in alchemy.

title: ogrim
topic_desc: Ogrim are massive, dimly intelligent Daedra resembling fat-faced ogres, chiefly associated with Malacath though they serve other Princes as well, including Molag Bal and Sanguine. Sent into the mortal world to menace mortals for Daedric amusement, they are sturdy, powerful, and cruel, regenerating health by pounding their chests. Despite their limited intellect, they exhibit a crude culture: they play rough games like Ogrim Toss, and higher-ranking individuals wear armor fitted with obsidian belly spoons, along with jewelry such as nipple caps and nose shackles etched with runes signifying obeisance to a Daedric master. Their hearts possess modest magical properties, though extracting one requires considerable effort.
topic_desc_basic: Ogrim are massive, dimly intelligent Daedra that resemble fat-faced ogres. They serve Malacath and other Daedric Princes, often menacing mortals for their masters' amusement. These sturdy, cruel creatures can regenerate by pounding their chests. Their hearts hold modest magical properties, though extracting them requires considerable effort.

title: Plitinius Mero
topic_desc: Plitinius Mero is an author and commoner of notable repute in Mournhold, serving as a close personal friend and trusted informant to Queen Mother Barenziah. Despite her royal station, Barenziah relies on Mero to gauge the shifting sentiments of the populace, as his knowledge and judgment are widely regarded as unparalleled. He is frequently found wandering the Palace Courtyard, accessible to those who seek his insights. His standing affords him a unique position bridging the royal court and the common people, making him a valuable observer of Mournhold's social and political currents.
topic_desc_basic: Plitinius Mero is a well-known author and commoner in Mournhold. He is a close friend and trusted informant of Queen Mother Barenziah, who values his unparalleled knowledge and judgment regarding the common people. He is often found wandering the Palace Courtyard.

title: shalk
topic_desc: Shalk are large, moderately aggressive beetles native to Morrowind and Vvardenfell, commonly found nesting near volcanic vents and active foyadas. They attack by biting and spitting fire, and despite their dangerous temperament, they are herded by Dunmer and Ashlanders for their valuable byproducts. Shalk resin, a tough soluble substance extracted from their hides, serves as a crucial glue and stiffener in manufacturing bonemold and chitin armors. Their carapaces and meat are also prized. While predatory in the wild, shalk raised from pupae can become surprisingly docile and trainable.
topic_desc_basic: Shalk are large, occasionally aggressive beetles that spit fire and inhabit the volcanic regions of Morrowind. Dunmer herd these creatures for their meat, carapaces, and hides. The resin extracted from shalk hides is particularly valuable as a glue and stiffener in crafting bonemold and chitin armors.

title: winged twilight
topic_desc: Winged Twilights are intelligent Daedra with feminine form, bat-like wings, clawed limbs, black horns, and barbed tails. Their scaled bodies range in blue or purple hues with red or blue eyes. Primarily serving Azura as messengers, they also answer Mehrunes Dagon, Molag Bal, and Nocturnal, occasionally deceiving mortals under false allegiances. They organize matriarchically when gathered. Cunning hunters, they stalk prey before striking with talons, tail lashes, shock magic, or debilitating shrieks that stun victims. Resistant to fire, frost, poison, and shock, they can also reflect spells. Some develop obsessive infatuations with mortals, abducting and holding them captive. The grievous twilight is considered a corrupted masculine form. Molag Grunda, a notable winged twilight, is acknowledged as Molag Bal's daughter.
topic_desc_basic: Winged Twilights are female-formed Daedra who primarily serve Azura as messengers. These winged beings possess clawed limbs, horns, spiked tails, and scaled skin in blue or purple hues. Cunning hunters, they attack with talons, barbed tails, and debilitating shrieks. They also serve other Daedric Princes and occasionally deceive mortals.

title: moon sugar
topic_desc: Moon sugar is a grainy powder of small white crystals refined from cane grasses growing along the coasts and estuaries of Elsweyr. The crystals possess a silver sheen and appear to glow from within when struck by light. In its native Elsweyr, moon sugar serves as a common culinary spice, but it also exhibits modest magical properties and functions as a potent narcotic. Humans are notably more susceptible to its effects than the Khajiit. Throughout the Empire, including Morrowind, moon sugar is strictly illegal. The substance is commonly refined into skooma, a more potent and addictive narcotic. Smugglers import moon sugar into Vvardenfell, where it circulates as currency among bandits, though attempts to cultivate its source grasses locally have consistently failed.
topic_desc_basic: Moon sugar is a crystalline powder refined from cane grasses of Elsweyr's coasts. While used as a spice in Khajiiti lands, it is a potent narcotic illegal throughout the Empire. It is commonly refined into the addictive drug skooma. Smugglers bring it into Vvardenfell, though local cultivation has never succeeded.

title: skooma
topic_desc: Skooma is a highly addictive, hallucinatory narcotic refined from moon sugar. The Empire bans it throughout Morrowind, yet it circulates widely as an underworld currency among smugglers and criminals. Users experience fleeting enhancements to speed and strength alongside pronounced clumsiness and mental dullness; sustained consumption leads to delusional euphoria alternating with lethargy, and eventual permanent mental deterioration. The drug is consumed via water pipe or in liquid form. While deeply intertwined with Khajiiti culture and their ceremonial use of moon sugar, skooma itself is universally condemned by Imperial law, and its illicit trade fuels extensive criminal enterprises.
topic_desc_basic: Skooma is an illegal, highly addictive narcotic refined from moon sugar. Banned by the Empire, it circulates as a currency among criminals and smugglers. Users gain temporary speed and strength but suffer clumsiness and mental dullness, with prolonged use causing lasting mental deterioration.

title: Cleaver of St. Felms
topic_desc: The Cleaver of St. Felms the Bold is a holy axe revered by the Tribunal Temple and named for Saint Felms, a celebrated warrior-saint of Temple tradition. The relic was borne by Mendel Eves, a Buoyant Armiger who fell fighting the forces of Dagoth Ur on the slopes of Red Mountain. Its association with Felms and the Armigers gives it importance as both a sacred object and a memorial to the Temple's long defense of Vvardenfell against the Sixth House.
topic_desc_basic: The Cleaver of St. Felms is a holy Tribunal Temple axe named for the warrior-saint. Buoyant Armiger Mendel Eves carried it while fighting the Sixth House at Red Mountain.
aliases: Cleaver of St. Felms the Bold

title: Dagger of Symmachus
topic_desc: The Dagger of Symmachus is the Dunmeri-styled glass ceremonial dagger of General Symmachus, the renowned Dunmer military leader and husband of Queen Barenziah. Because of its association with the late general, it is considered a significant historical treasure to the people of Mournhold. The weapon possesses high durability and is enchanted to enhance the wielder's short blade skill and endurance while reflecting hostile spells cast upon the user.
topic_desc_basic: The Dagger of Symmachus is the Dunmeri-styled glass ceremonial dagger of General Symmachus, the famous husband of Queen Barenziah. It is regarded as a local historical treasure in Mournhold.

title: Darts of Judgement
topic_desc: The Darts of Judgement are exceptionally rare throwing darts crafted in Valenwood from daedric material. They unite Bosmeri expertise in ranged weapons with the lethal resilience associated with daedric arms. Only a small number are known outside their homeland, making them prized by collectors, marksmen, and dealers in unusual weaponry. Their scarcity and craftsmanship distinguish them from ordinary darts and account for their considerable value wherever rare Valenwood arms are traded.
topic_desc_basic: The Darts of Judgement are rare Valenwood throwing weapons made from daedric material. Their Bosmeri craftsmanship, scarcity, and deadly effectiveness make them highly valuable to marksmen and collectors.

title: Egg of Time
topic_desc: A Dwemer treatise authored by the tonal architect Bthuand Mzahnch during the First Era. The work refutes a prevailing contemporary theory among certain Dwemer tones that tapping the power of Lorkhan's Heart entailed unjustifiable risks. Bthuand argues compellingly that no disastrous consequences would result from such use. The text remains largely unreadable without the aid of the companion volume "Hanging Gardens of Sufutta" for translation. Scholars debate its claims fiercely, as the subsequent disappearance of the Dwemer race seemingly contradicts Bthuand's assurances of safety. The book is sought by researchers of the Dwarves for its rare insight into the internal philosophical disputes surrounding Kagrenac's fateful experiments.
topic_desc_basic: A Dwemer text by the tonal architect Bthuand Mzahnch. It argues against the popular contemporary belief among the Dwemer that using Lorkhan's Heart carried unjustifiable risks. The Dwarven disappearance seemingly contradicts Bthuand's assurances of safety, leaving modern scholars divided on the work's conclusions.

title: Hanging Gardens
topic_desc: A surviving Dwemer travel guide to the Hanging Gardens of Wasten Coridale, written in both Dwemeris and Aldmeris. Likely produced during the Resdayn era of peaceful Dwemer-Dunmer cohabitation, its bilingual nature renders it an invaluable cipher for translating other Dwemer texts. Surviving fragments describe Altmer Estrial, quadrangular gardens, and cryptic allusions to defying Earth Bones, concluding with a marginal comment in a different hand warning against misinterpretation.
topic_desc_basic: An old bilingual travel guide written in both Dwemeris and Aldmeris, describing the Hanging Gardens of Wasten Coridale. Because it contains the same text in two languages, scholars consider it a priceless key for translating other Dwemer writings.

title: Ring of Equity
topic_desc: A unique enchanted ring concealed within Master Neloth's treasury in Tel Naga at Sadrith Mora. The ring is reputed as a formidable defense against hostile magic, though its enchantment permits only limited use in a single encounter. Its recovery from the well-guarded tower requires a key to Tel Naga, which Neloth and his retainers carry.
topic_desc_basic: A unique enchanted ring hidden in Master Neloth's treasury in Tel Naga at Sadrith Mora. It is a potent defensive item against spellcasters, though its enchantment allows only limited uses per encounter.

title: Ring of the Wind
topic_desc: The Ring of the Wind is a legendary enchanted ring from Elsweyr, sacred to Kynareth in the best-known tradition, though some accounts associate it with Zenithar. It grants extraordinary speed to its wearer. The artifact is famously linked to the Khajiiti acrobat Kisimba Spring-Snow, celebrated for always landing upon her feet unless she chose otherwise. Yagrum Bagarn's Tamrielic Lore includes the ring among artifacts of exceptional significance, and its movements have inspired competing rumors throughout the Empire.
topic_desc_basic: The Ring of the Wind is a legendary Elsweyr artifact sacred to Kynareth. It grants great speed and is traditionally associated with the nimble Khajiiti acrobat Kisimba Spring-Snow.

title: Shoes of St. Rilms
topic_desc: The Shoes of St. Rilms are a sacred relic of the Tribunal Temple associated with Saint Rilms the Barefooted, patron of pilgrims and the poor. Temple tradition treats objects connected to Rilms as reminders of humility, charity, and service despite the authority carried by senior clergy. Accounts connect the shoes with the Daedric shrine of Ald Sotha and with priestly visions concerning their preservation. Their religious value rests chiefly in their connection to the saint rather than the material worth of the footwear.
topic_desc_basic: The Shoes of St. Rilms are a Tribunal Temple relic associated with Saint Rilms the Barefooted. They symbolize humility, charity, pilgrimage, and service to the poor.

title: berserkers
topic_desc: Berserkers are feral Nords roaming Solstheim's wilderness, driven mad by extreme cold and mead. Called 'bare-sarks' in the Nord tongue for their practice of going bare-chested even in severe blizzards, they possess no respect for life or order, killing any who cross their path. Shunned even from mead halls like Thirsk, they are drawn to death itself, making their homes within the island's ancient burial barrows. Rumors persist of a berserker 'mother' who leads them, though none have reportedly seen her and survived.
topic_desc_basic: Berserkers are feral, half-naked Nords roaming Solstheim, driven mad by the cold and mead. Known as 'bare-sarks' for going bare-chested in blizzards, they kill anyone they encounter and dwell in ancient burial barrows.

title: breeding netch
topic_desc: Breeding netch are mated bull and betty netch whose behavior changes markedly during their reproductive cycle. Netch are ordinarily docile floating creatures valued for hides and other useful products, but breeding pairs become territorial and aggressive when approached. Their size, reach, and persistence can endanger herders, travelers, and settlements near their nesting grounds. Experienced hunters therefore distinguish the behavior of a breeding pair from the calmer habits normally associated with wild or domesticated netch.
topic_desc_basic: A breeding pair of bull and betty netch becomes territorial and aggressive during its reproductive cycle. Although netch are usually docile, breeding pairs can threaten nearby herders and settlements.

title: dragons
topic_desc: Dragons are ancient, immortal creatures of immense power and intelligence, possessing their own language and the capacity to speak those of men and mer. They are not born, hatched, or bred, and have no life cycle in the mortal sense. Their most feared weapon is their breath, which can unleash fire or frost. During the Merethic Era, the Dragon War decimated their numbers. The Akaviri later hunted them extensively during the First Era. By the late Second Era, Tiber Septim reportedly pacted with the few survivors, though their subsequent disappearance remains unexplained; no dragon has been confirmed seen for centuries. Fused skeletal remains embedded in rock provide undeniable proof of their historical existence. Some accounts, including Dragonguard records, suggest individual dragons may yet survive in remote regions, such as Morrowind or the Throat of the World.
topic_desc_basic: Dragons are immortal, intelligent creatures possessing their own language and devastating fire or frost breath. They are not hatched or bred. Their numbers were devastated during the Merethic Era Dragon War and later Akaviri hunts. Tiber Septim reportedly pacted with the last survivors, but they subsequently vanished. No dragon has been confirmed seen for centuries, though their petrified skeletal remains endure.

title: greater bonewalker
topic_desc: Greater bonewalkers are powerful undead guardians that defend the ancestral tombs of Dunmer clans and kin. More formidable than their lesser kin, these aggressive and dangerous revenants arise from the honored dead, bound to protect sacred burial sites from desecration. Their bones yield bonemeal, a finely ground powder valued for its modest magical properties. Summoners of sufficient skill can conjure greater bonewalkers to serve as combat allies. Within Dunmer ancestor worship, such risen dead occupy an ambiguous position—honored protectors, yet unsettling reminders of the boundary between living and dead that the Tribunal Temple's doctrines carefully navigate.
topic_desc_basic: Greater bonewalkers are powerful undead that guard Dunmer ancestral tombs, defending the burial sites of clan and kin. Aggressive and dangerous, these revenants yield bonemeal from their bones, a powder with modest magical properties.

title: kwama forager
topic_desc: The kwama forager is one of the morphs of the kwama, a colonial insect native to Vvardenfell and the broader Morrowind region. It scouts the surface and natural underground passages, searching for suitable locations for new colonies and hunting for prey. While aggressive, foragers are not very dangerous to prepared travelers. They are a common sight near kwama mines, where the creatures are bred for their valuable egg yield. Like all kwama morphs, the forager is susceptible to the Blight disease carried by the recent ash storms, becoming significantly more hostile and threatening when infected.
topic_desc_basic: The kwama forager is a morph of the kwama, a colonial insect of Morrowind. It scouts the surface and underground passages for new colony sites and prey. Aggressive but not very dangerous, it is commonly encountered near kwama mines.

title: kwama warrior
topic_desc: The kwama warrior is the primary defensive caste of the kwama colony, tasked with protecting the nest's tunnels and chambers from intruders. Large, aggressive, and dangerous, warriors patrol the subterranean networks of Vvardenfell's egg mines and natural kwama habitats. They are one of several morphologically distinct forms—alongside workers, foragers, and scribs—that the kwama species produces depending on the colony's needs. While essential to the colony's survival, their hostility poses a significant threat to miners and travelers. Warriors can also fall victim to the Blight, becoming even more ferocious and unpredictable, which further endangers the lucrative egg-mining industry.
topic_desc_basic: The kwama warrior defends the colony's tunnels and chambers from intruders. Large, aggressive, and dangerous, these creatures patrol Vvardenfell's egg mines and pose a significant threat to miners.

title: kwama worker
topic_desc: Kwama workers are the excavators and caretakers of kwama egg mine colonies, responsible for digging tunnels and chambers while tending to the queen and her eggs. Though generally unaggressive, they are not entirely defenseless and will respond to threats against the hive. Alongside foragers and warriors, they constitute one of the three recognized morphs of the worker caste. Kwama workers are vital to the egg mining industry that sustains Morrowind's economy, and their behavior makes them the least dangerous mine inhabitant—unless Blight infection drives them to hostility.
topic_desc_basic: Kwama workers dig their colony's tunnels and chambers and tend the queen and eggs. They are the least aggressive kwama morph but not completely helpless, and can become dangerous if Blighted.

title: Mudcrab
topic_desc: Mudcrabs are small, hard-shelled arthropods found along coastlines, waterways, and caves throughout Tamriel. They typically rely on camouflage, burrowing, and pincers for defense, and are rarely aggressive unless cornered or provoked. However, should a mudcrab taste meat, it becomes a persistent hunter capable of threatening livestock. Swarms can strip a corpse to bone in days. Some naturalists posit a relationship between Morrowind's mudcrabs and the extinct Emperor Crab. Larger species, such as the king mudcrab and mudcrab titan, present genuine danger to travelers. While regarded as vermin by most, their sweet meat is widely edible, and their chitin sees alchemical use. Rare accounts even describe specimens displaying humanoid intelligence and speech.
topic_desc_basic: Mudcrabs are small, hard-shelled arthropods common along shores and waterways across Tamriel. They are rarely aggressive unless provoked, though those that taste meat become hunters. While generally considered vermin, their meat is edible and their chitin has alchemical uses.

title: Reavers
topic_desc: Reavers are Nord raiders from distant northern isles who prey upon Solstheim's remote coasts. Operating in small bands of axemen and archers, they stage hit-and-run attacks against isolated hunting camps and one-hut settlements, deliberately avoiding larger, defended colonies. To protect their vessels from theft or destruction, they refuse to beach their ships, instead anchoring offshore while their raiding parties strike inland. Though a persistent nuisance to solitary trappers and hunters, they pose little threat to fortified positions and are largely dismissed by garrisoned populations as an intermittent hazard of frontier life.
topic_desc_basic: Reavers are Nord raiders from distant northern islands who attack the remote coasts of Solstheim. They strike isolated hunting camps and tiny settlements in small hit-and-run bands of axemen and archers, but avoid larger, defended colonies. They keep their ships offshore rather than beaching them, ensuring a quick escape.

title: skeleton
topic_desc: Skeletons are reanimated undead revenants commonly found guarding ancestral tombs, ruins, and dungeons across Tamriel. They retain a notable resistance to frost magic and edged weapons. While the skeletal structures of Men and Mer are largely identical, Orc and beast-race remains are readily identifiable by their distinct skulls and jaws. Necromancers and conjurers frequently summon or raise these mindless guardians to protect the resting places of clan and kin. Bonemeal, a finely ground powder derived from their bones, possesses modest magical properties valued in alchemical practice.
topic_desc_basic: Skeletons are reanimated undead revenants that commonly guard ancestral tombs and ruins. They resist frost magic and edged weapons. Bonemeal, the powder ground from their bones, holds modest magical properties.

title: slaughterfish
topic_desc: Slaughterfish are large, aggressive fish armed with razor-sharp teeth, inhabiting waters across Tamriel and even subterranean pools. They favor foul waters but thrive in diverse aquatic environments, from deep inland lakes to underground rivers, and are known to swarm unwary prey in lethal groups. While their meat is generally considered mealy and noisome, dried slaughterfish scales are regarded by locals as a crunchy treat when prepared in the native manner. Slaughterfish bites can transmit diseases that induce violent outbursts and dementia in victims.
topic_desc_basic: Slaughterfish are aggressive, sharp-toothed fish found throughout Tamriel's waters and underground pools. They swarm unwary prey in groups. Their meat is unpalatable, but dried scales are a crunchy local delicacy. Their bites can transmit diseases causing dementia.

title: Tusked Bristleback
topic_desc: The Tusked Bristleback is a large, boar-like creature native to Solstheim. Recognized by the Skaal as a natural creation of the All-Maker, it is nevertheless considered a cruel and vicious beast. Bristlebacks roam the island in significant numbers and are sometimes hunted for their meat. Their aggressive temperament makes them difficult to manage, yet the indigenous Rieklings have successfully tamed them, employing the creatures as war mounts and selectively breeding them to amplify their warlike and dangerous tendencies.
topic_desc_basic: The Tusked Bristleback is a large, vicious, boar-like creature native to Solstheim that is sometimes hunted for its meat. The island's Rieklings tame these beasts and employ them as war mounts.

title: wraith
topic_desc: Wraiths are powerful revenant spirits categorized among the returned undead. They arise from souls consumed by profound injustice, unfulfilled purpose, or lives abruptly severed, their anger shaping the darkest expression of a spirit. Necromancers can also forcibly invoke these emotions or employ ensnaring curses to summon and enslave wraiths as guardians, though such hateful specters prove harder to control than common ghosts. Naturally manifesting wraiths often defend ancestral tombs or haunt cursed objects. As ethereal beings, they can perceive invisible foes, cast spells, and suffer harm only from silver or enchanted weapons. Banishing a wraith from the mortal plane leaves behind ectoplasm, a filmy residue with modest magical properties. Distinguished varieties include the weaker faded wraith and the formidable gloom wraith, which wields weapons and projects enfeebling curses.
topic_desc_basic: Wraiths are aggressive revenant spirits that commonly defend ancestral tombs or guard cursed objects. They may also be summoned and bound by sorcerers, though their hateful nature makes them difficult to control. As ethereal undead, they can only be harmed by silver or enchanted weapons. When banished, they leave behind ectoplasm, a filmy residue with modest magical properties.

title: Ashlander challenges
topic_desc: Among the Ashlander tribes, challenges serve as a formal mechanism for resolving disputes and affirming social standing, divided into two distinct categories. Sport challenges are recreational contests of skill or strength; declining such a challenge carries no social stigma. Honor challenges, however, arise from perceived offenses in speech or action, or constitute customary formal challenges of status and ritual. Refusing an honor challenge is considered deeply shameful, as it represents a failure to defend one's reputation or fulfill a ritual obligation within tribal society.
topic_desc_basic: Ashlander custom recognizes two forms of challenges. Sport challenges are recreational contests that may be declined without shame. Honor challenges arise from personal offense, or as formal challenges of status and ritual, and it is shameful to decline them.

title: Imperial neighbors
topic_desc: Native Dunmer regard their Imperial neighbors as uncivilized apes, a common insult reflecting deep cultural disdain. While they grudgingly respect Imperial administrative and military cunning—particularly their ability to forge organized armies from common peasants—and admire their engineering and work ethic, these acknowledgments do not temper broader contempt. Dunmer scorn what they perceive as a fundamental Imperial lack of honor and refinement. Above all, they despise the crass commercialism that drives Imperial enterprise and the tolerance for cultural mongrelization that accompanies it, viewing both as existential threats to Dunmeri identity and tradition.
topic_desc_basic: Native Dunmer commonly regard Imperials as uncivilized apes. While they grudgingly respect Imperial military organization, engineering, and work ethic, they scorn their perceived lack of honor and refinement. Most of all, the Dunmer despise Imperial mercantile greed and tolerance for cultural mongrelization.

title: mabrigash
topic_desc: A mabrigash is an Ashlander witch-warrior, a renegade wise woman who forsakes established Ashlander behavioral rules to master dark magic and the weapons of war.
