The Khajiit deployed multiple morphologies in concert: Cathay-raht and Senche-raht served as ground forces and shield-bearers, Ohmes and Ohmes-raht emerged from concealed tunnels to ambush descending Bosmer infantry, and the arboreal Dagi and Dagi-raht silently climbed into high branches to attack the remaining archers with fire. Callonus expresses skepticism regarding a Bosmer survivor's claim that the small Alfiq Khajiit cast spells, dismissing it as unreliable. The author notes this mixed-unit tactic succeeded twice before a larger Bosmer force with native animal allies prevailed, a confrontation he promises to address in a second volume.
topic_desc_basic: A military treatise by the Imperial observer Codus Callonus, arguing the Legions should study Khajiiti warfare. It details a Five Years War skirmish where Khajiit forces used multiple morphologies in concert—ground troops, concealed tunnel ambushers, and arboreal Dagi attackers—to defeat Bosmer archers. Callonus dismisses Bosmer claims that the small Alfiq Khajiit cast spells as unreliable.
aliases: Mixed Unit Tactics in the Five Years War Volume One

title: Ordo Legionis
topic_desc: Ordo Legionis is an official Imperial instructional tract presenting the Legion as the Empire's paramount disciplined force, preserving peace and the rule of law. It details the five Vvardenfell garrisons—Moonmoth, Buckmoth, Pelagiad, the elite Hawkmoth at Castle Ebonheart, and the under-strength Fort Darius—tasked with supplementing Temple and Great House guards. The text frames Legion service as the model of Imperial citizenship, requiring superior endurance and trustworthy personality. Recruits must master the long blade, spear, and blunt weapons, train with heavy armor and shields, and possess athletics for marching and battlefield maneuver. The account serves as both recruitment propaganda and a civic ideal.
topic_desc_basic: Ordo Legionis is an official tract introducing the Imperial Legion's role and Vvardenfell garrisons. It presents the Legion as history's most disciplined force, preserving Imperial law and supplementing local guards. The text outlines recruitment standards, emphasizing endurance, trustworthy personality, and mastery of long blades, spears, blunt weapons, heavy armor, and athletics.

title: Saryoni's Sermons Manuscript
topic_desc: Saryoni's Sermons Manuscript is the original working text from which Archcanon Tholer Saryoni composed his published sermons. It presents core Tribunal temple doctrine through two sections: Vivec's five maxims on faith and suffering, and the Seven Graces—Valor, Daring, Justice, Courtesy, Pride, Generosity, and Humility—each accompanied by a devotional response. The manuscript frames these virtues as divine gifts from Vivec, instructing the faithful to embody them as religious obligations. As an archcanon's personal manuscript, it carries significant authority within Temple hierarchy and is exceptionally rare and valuable.
topic_desc_basic: This manuscript is the original text Archcanon Tholer Saryoni used to compose his sermons. It outlines Tribunal doctrine through Vivec's five teachings on faith and the Seven Graces—Valor, Daring, Justice, Courtesy, Pride, Generosity, and Humility—each presented as divine virtues the faithful must embody. The work is exceptionally rare and valuable.

title: Sharn's Legions of the Dead
topic_desc: Sharn gra-Muzgob's personal treatise on undead taxonomy, categorizing revenants into spirit, flesh, and fleshless types. It details ancestor ghosts, wraiths, and dwarven ghosts as spirits requiring enchanted or silver weapons, and bonewalkers as preserved flesh revenants vulnerable to normal arms. Fleshless skeletons vary in capability, though the powerful bonelord requires enchanted weapons. The text notes vampires' return to Morrowind after Ordinator and Buoyant Armiger purges, emphasizing their strength. A crucial caveat distinguishes ash vampires from true undead, reporting that anti-undead magic fails against them despite their preserved nature.
topic_desc_basic: A treatise on undead taxonomy categorizing revenants as spirit, flesh, or fleshless. It covers ghosts, bonewalkers, skeletons, and bonelords, detailing their vulnerabilities. It also notes the return of vampires to Morrowind and clarifies that ash vampires are living beings, unaffected by spells targeting the undead.

title: Tal Marog Ker's Researches
topic_desc: Tal Marog Ker's Researches is a scholarly text dated Harvest's End, 3E 172, documenting the tragic fate of the Direnni retainer and sorcerer Chimere Graegyn. It details Chimere's scheme against the Daedra Lord Dagon, whom he tricked into breaking an oath. Protected by Malacath's Armor of the Saviour's Hide, which turns the blows of oathbreakers, Chimere invoked Dagon's Protonymic to drain his power. However, Dagon resisted long enough to twist Chimere's pact, casting Caecilly Island into the void and condemning Chimere to eternal, tormented life. The text also examines the island's Chapel of the Innocent Quarry and the Spear of Bitter Mercy, noting the Hide can protect a bearer from the Spear's maleficent energies.
topic_desc_basic: A scholarly text from 3E 172 by Tal Marog Ker. It chronicles the Direnni sorcerer Chimere Graegyn, who used Malacath's Armor of the Saviour's Hide and Dagon's Protonymic against the Daedra Lord. Dagon twisted Chimere's pact in retaliation, casting his home into the void. The work also discusses the Chapel of the Innocent Quarry and the Spear of Bitter Mercy.

title: Tamrielic Lore
topic_desc: Tamrielic Lore is a substantial catalog of legendary artifacts compiled over centuries by an unknown scholar, widely attributed to the last living Dwemer, Yagrum Bagarn. The text surveys over two dozen items of reputedly unimaginable significance, including Daedric relics like the Ebony Mail and Mace of Molag Bal, and storied arms like Chrysamere and the Ice Blade of the Monarch. The author readily admits that some entries may be myth or hoax, and the work reflects an unreliable viewpoint shaped by centuries of accumulated rumor. Recurring themes emphasize the capricious nature of the artifacts' divine or Daedric creators and the fatal consequences befalling those who possess them. A revised edition exists with corrected grammar, and an alternate version circulates under the title Famed Artifacts of Tamriel.
topic_desc_basic: A centuries-spanning catalog of legendary Tamrielic artifacts, attributed to Yagrum Bagarn. The author surveys renowned items like the Lord's Mail, Spell Breaker, and Mehrunes' Razor, while cautioning that some entries may be myth or hoax. The text emphasizes the capricious nature of the artifacts' creators and the perilous fates of their bearers.

title: The Affairs of Wizards
topic_desc: A recruitment pamphlet by Turedus Talanian, written in the service of Master Aryon, addressing outsiders interested in joining House Telvanni. It systematically refutes common assumptions about Telvanni exclusivity, clarifying that the House accepts candidates of all races and modest magical aptitude, though advancement favors high intelligence, willpower, and proficiency in the magical arts. Talanian explains the Mouth system, whereby councilors are represented by trusted subordinates at the Telvanni Council Hall in Sadrith Mora, and describes the wizard-lords' dependence on skilled retainers and Western mercenaries. The text functions as both practical guide and Telvanni propaganda, presenting the House as more accessible than its reputation suggests while candidly acknowledging that advancement among outsiders is difficult and that the Telvanni casually accept murder and assassination of rivals as legitimate means of progression. Talanian directs the faint-hearted toward the Mages Guild instead.
topic_desc_basic: A pamphlet by Turedus Talanian, in the service of Master Aryon, encouraging outsiders to join House Telvanni. It refutes assumptions about Telvanni racial and intellectual exclusivity, explains the Mouth system of council representation, and candidly notes that advancement accepts murder of rivals as legitimate. The faint-hearted are directed to the Mages Guild.

title: The Alchemists Formulary
topic_desc: A practical alchemical guide divided into three sections addressing healers, travelers, and adventurers. Healers' recipes rely on inexpensive, common ingredients like marshmerrow, saltrice, and wickwheat for health and fatigue restoration, or gravedust and green lichen for curing disease. Travelers' recipes provide affordable mixtures for feather, levitation, and water breathing using accessible flora and fauna. The adventurers' section addresses costlier and more dangerous endeavors, acknowledging that desirable effects like strength fortification and invisibility require rare components such as dreugh wax or crushed diamonds. Beyond recipes, the formulary serves as a regional botanical and harvestable survey of Vvardenfell, cataloging where specific ingredients grow and which creatures yield them.
topic_desc_basic: A widely circulated instructional manual on mixing potions from Vvardenfell's ingredients. It covers affordable healing and fatigue remedies using common plants, travel aids like levitation and water breathing, and costlier adventurer mixtures for strength and invisibility, while noting where various ingredients grow or may be harvested.

title: The Anticipations
topic_desc: This anonymous Temple doctrine outlines the orthodox relationship between the Tribunal and the Daedra. It presents the Tribunal's Apotheosis as a just supersession of the old Chimer worship, categorizing Boethiah, Azura, and Mephala as the Anticipations—ancestor spirits who rightfully submitted to the Tribunal and prefigured its patronage. Boethiah anticipates Almalexia, Mephala anticipates Vivec, and Azura anticipates Sotha Sil. The text frames the Four Corners of the House of Troubles as Rebel Daedra who refused fealty. As Temple propaganda, it asserts that the Daedra are weaker than the Tribunal and omits any suggestion of Daedric resentment toward the Tribunal's ascension.
topic_desc_basic: This Temple text explains the orthodox view that the Daedra Boethiah, Azura, and Mephala are the Anticipations who submitted to the Tribunal and prefigured its divine roles. It also identifies the Rebel Daedra who refused fealty as the House of Troubles.

title: The Book of Dawn and Dusk
topic_desc: The Book of Dawn and Dusk is a collection of aphorisms and sayings attributed to the Tribunal and their saints. These maxims have become everyday clichés throughout Morrowind, distilling the simplest notions of Tribunal doctrine into memorable slogans. The sayings emphasize absolute faith, submission to divine judgment, and the virtues of suffering and service. Recurring themes include the glory of Almsivi—expressed through the triune qualities of Mercy, Mastery, and Mystery—and the rejection of the House of Troubles. The text presents these teachings as unquestionable truth, demanding obedience and reverence while warning of folly and mortal ends.
topic_desc_basic: The Book of Dawn and Dusk collects sayings attributed to the Tribunal and their saints. These aphorisms have become common phrases in Morrowind, expressing core Tribunal beliefs such as absolute faith, the virtues of suffering and service, and devotion to Almsivi's Mercy, Mastery, and Mystery.

record_links.display_name: The Book of Dawn and Dusk

title: The Brothers of Darkness
topic_desc: Pellarne Assi's historical treatise traces the Dark Brotherhood to the Morag Tong, a Second Era religious cult of Mephala worshippers who committed ritual murders. Assi describes how the Night Mother unified the disorganized cult and developed the doctrine that murders born of hate and targeting prominent figures pleased Mephala more. The Morag Tong's 2E 324 assassination of Potentate Versidue-Shaie, publicly claimed in blood, prompted continent-wide outlawing. Assi dates the Brotherhood's emergence to around 2E 360, citing Queen Arlimahera of Hegathe's journals, and distinguishes the Brotherhood from its precursor as a commercial enterprise as much as a cult. He recounts the 2E 430 slaughter of Emperor-Potentate Savirien-Chorak and his heirs, which collapsed the Colovian Dynasty and ushered in four centuries of chaos. Assi acknowledges uncertainties, particularly whether the Night Mother has been one continuous figure.
topic_desc_basic: Pellarne Assi's scholarly history traces the Dark Brotherhood's origins from the Morag Tong, a Second Era Mephala cult. The book describes the Night Mother's rise, the cult's outlawing after assassinating Potentate Versidue-Shaie in 2E 324, and the Brotherhood's later emergence as a commercial assassin's guild. Assi notes key executions and acknowledges uncertainties about the Night Mother's identity.

title: The Common Tongue: Irano's copy
topic_desc: A cheap broadsheet newsletter circulating in Mournhold, this copy discovered beneath Ivulen Irano's pillow. Under a Vivec quotation, it details three individuals—Anhar, Martyrius Arruntius, and Jusole Asciele—who died conveniently after threatening Prince Helseth's interests in Wayrest. Imperial coroners ruled each death natural. The anonymous author disingenuously denies possessing evidence that Helseth is a poisoner while heavily implying his guilt, extending the insinuation to King Athyn Llethan's recent demise. The publication serves as pointed political commentary, using sensationalism and calculated irony to accuse Morrowind's new monarch of assassination while maintaining nominal deniability.
topic_desc_basic: A sensational Mournhold broadsheet, this copy found under Ivulen Irano's pillow. It lists individuals who died conveniently after opposing Prince Helseth in Wayrest. While claiming no evidence exists, the anonymous author heavily implies Helseth is a skilled poisoner and subtly extends the accusation to King Athyn Llethan's recent death.

title: The Consolations of Prayer
topic_desc: A Tribunal Temple prayerbook setting forth the blessings available at three-sided Almsivi shrines. It catalogues cures for disease, poison, and blight granted by all shrines, then enumerates Tribunal-specific blessings such as Almsivi Restoration, Vivec's Mystery, Soul of Sotha Sil, and Lady's Grace. It further lists blessings associated with ten saints, from Aralor's Intervention to Veloth's Indwelling, each tied to a particular fortification or resistance. The text functions as both doctrinal instruction and practical devotional guide, explaining that the faithful receive blessings through prayer and a modest donation, while Temple members of Initiate rank or higher need only pray. It notes that even unbelievers may receive blessings with a generous donation, framing Almsivi's generosity as inclusive. The work presents Temple sacraments as established doctrine rather than disputed tradition.
topic_desc_basic: A Tribunal Temple prayerbook describing blessings granted at Almsivi shrines. It lists cures for disease and poison available at all shrines, plus specific blessings associated with Vivec, Almalexia, Sotha Sil, and ten saints. The faithful pray and donate; Temple initiates need only pray. Unbelievers may also receive blessings with a generous donation.

title: The Eastern Provinces...
topic_desc: A political treatise arguing that the Empire's occupation of Morrowind and Black Marsh is morally corrupt, militarily indefensible, and economically ruinous. The anonymous author contends that bureaucratic and garrison costs exceed provincial revenues, that idle Eastern legions pose a domestic threat to Imperial succession, and that the Empire hypocritically tolerates and protects Dunmer slavery to enrich monopolists. The tract advocates complete withdrawal from the Eastern provinces to preserve Western civilization, reflecting an anti-imperial viewpoint that frames the occupation as a corrupt scheme benefiting only the Imperial family's cronies.
topic_desc_basic: A political treatise arguing that the Empire should withdraw from Morrowind and Black Marsh. The author claims the occupation is economically ruinous, militarily unnecessary, and morally compromised by Imperial tolerance of Dunmer slavery, serving only to enrich monopolists rather than the Empire as a whole.

title: The Firmament
topic_desc: Ffoulke's astrological treatise catalogues Tamriel's thirteen constellations, detailing their seasonal alignments and the birthsigns they bestow. The text organizes the heavens into three Guardian constellations—the Warrior, the Mage, and the Thief—each shielding three Charges from the wandering, seasonless Serpent. Every sign receives a designated month and is said to confer specific traits: martial skill and irritability under the Warrior, magical aptitude and arrogance under the Mage, or fortune and restlessness under the Thief. The Serpent's influence is presented as uniquely contradictory, rendering those born beneath it both blessed and cursed. While the work serves as a foundational reference for astrological doctrine, its deterministic claims regarding personality and fate reflect cultural belief rather than verified natural law.
topic_desc_basic: Ffoulke's treatise describes Tamriel's thirteen constellations and their associated birthsigns. It explains how the three Guardians—the Warrior, the Mage, and the Thief—each protect three Charges from the wandering Serpent. The text assigns each constellation a seasonal month and claims those born under specific signs possess corresponding traits and aptitudes.

title: The Madness of Pelagius
topic_desc: A historical study by Tsathenes chronicling the life and mental decline of Emperor Pelagius III. The narrative traces his unremarkable childhood during the War of the Red Diamond, his burgeoning eccentricities as King of Solitude, and his total incapacitation after ascending to the Ruby Throne. The author attributes his limited public incidents to the careful management of his Dunmer consort, Katariah Ra'athim, who assumed regency when his violence required institutionalization. Tsathenes writes from a loyalist perspective, explicitly dismissing rumors of torture in asylums and questioning Katariah's fidelity, while openly acknowledging that many infamous Pelagius anecdotes are unverified or apocryphal.
topic_desc_basic: A historical account by Tsathenes detailing the life and mental deterioration of Emperor Pelagius III. It covers his youth, his growing madness as king, and his eventual confinement after Katariah Ra'athim assumed regency. The author adopts a loyalist stance, dismissing rumors of asylum torture and imperial conspiracy as traitorous lies.

title: The Pig Children
topic_desc: Tyston Bane's vehement anti-Orcish pamphlet presents the Orsimer as Daedric conjurations and perpetual blights upon civilization. Employing crude caricatures of Orcish appearance, intellect, and hygiene, it argues that only their ferocity and tribal loyalty prevented their eradication. To substantiate these claims, Bane cites the historian Jastyaga's account of the siege of Orsinium in 1E 950, when the Order of Diagna joined the armies of Daggerfall and Sentinel to destroy the Orcish kingdom. The subsequent scattering of survivors and the death of heroes like Gaiden Shinji are framed as righteous necessity against a savage foe. The tract serves as unvarnished propaganda, reinforcing cultural prejudice by depicting Orcs as irredeemable monsters while celebrating their displacement.
topic_desc_basic: Tyston Bane's inflammatory pamphlet denounces Orcs as foul Daedric conjurations and savage pests. It cites the first-era siege and destruction of Orsinium by Daggerfall, Sentinel, and the Order of Diagna as a righteous victory against a monstrous race. The text serves as blunt anti-Orcish propaganda.

title: The Pilgrim's Path
topic_desc: A Tribunal Temple doctrinal guide detailing the Shrines of the Seven Graces and the essential Vvardenfell pilgrimage. Each entry recounts a legendary episode from Vivec's life—displaying humility at the Fields of Kummu, halting Baar Dau through daring, honoring all war dead with generosity, showing courtesy to Mehrunes Dagon's Dremora, weeping to save blighted refugees at Gnisis, defeating Ruddy Man with valor at Koal Cave, and demonstrating pride through the Ghostfence. The text serves as both devotional narrative and practical travel manual, prescribing customary offerings and route advice. As official Temple doctrine, it presents these accounts as historical truth and reverent parable, omitting alternative theological perspectives while emphasizing the living presence and authority of ALMSIVI.
topic_desc_basic: A Tribunal Temple guide instructing faithful on the Vvardenfell pilgrimage to the Shrines of the Seven Graces. Each shrine commemorates a legendary act of Vivec and requires a customary offering. The text provides both devotional stories and travel directions, serving as an essential practical and religious manual for Temple followers.

title: The Posting of the Hunt
topic_desc: A hasty transcription of the laws and rites governing the Ritual of the Innocent Quarry, commonly called the Wild Hunt. The document describes a Daedric ceremony wherein all-powerful Huntsmen and their hounds pursue a doomed mortal, the Hare. The ritual mandates four stages—the Drag, the Chase, the Call, and the View—culminating in a kill by the Spear of Bitter Mercy. The text emphasizes an aesthetic balance between the Huntsman's ecstasy and the Hare's despair. Crucially, the Law requires giving the Hare a genuine, if impossibly slim, chance of escape via six keys in the Temple of Daedric Rites. The ritual shields Huntsmen from all attacks, yet the Spear remains lethal to participant and quarry alike, and its removal from the grounds is forbidden. The document's hasty transcription suggests an incomplete or secondhand account of these ancient Daedric practices.
topic_desc_basic: A transcribed document detailing the laws of the Wild Hunt, a Daedric ritual where Huntsmen pursue a mortal Hare using the Spear of Bitter Mercy. It describes the four stages of the hunt and the requirement that the Hare receive a genuine chance to escape, however slim. The account appears hastily copied from a longer work.

title: The Real Barenziah v I
topic_desc: This unauthorized biographical volume traces Queen Barenziah's early life and the origins of Symmachus, presenting events through a dramatic, potentially unreliable narrative. It depicts Symmachus as a Mournhold miner who, after his mother dies because callous nobility denied her healing during Barenziah's naming rite, vows vengeance and accidentally kills a priest before fleeing. The account then shifts to Barenziah's childhood, portraying her parents riding to war against Tiber Septim, her chaotic evacuation amid a terrifying omen, and her grim upbringing under the contemptuous Count Sven and Lady Inga in Skyrim. The narrative emphasizes her innate royal disdain for her poseur guardians and concludes with her sixteenth-year flight alongside the stable-boy Straw. As propaganda or sensationalized legend, the work's anonymous authorship and melodramatic framing render its specific dialogues and private motivations uncertain.
topic_desc_basic: This unauthorized biographical volume dramatizes Queen Barenziah's early life. It recounts Symmachus's origins as a Mournhold miner who swore vengeance against the ruling family after his mother's neglected death, then depicts Barenziah's evacuation from Mournhold during Tiber Septim's invasion and her cold upbringing in Skyrim, culminating in her flight at age sixteen. The anonymous account's sensationalized nature makes its reliability uncertain.

title: The Real Barenziah v II
topic_desc: This unauthorized second volume of the biography of Queen Barenziah recounts her teenage years in Rifton alongside her companion Straw. The narrative depicts her induction into the Thieves Guild through a Khajiit sponsor named Therris, her training in stealth and magic under a Nord woman named Katisha, and a disastrous burglary that leads to her capture by General Symmachus of the Imperial Army. Symmachus reveals that the Empire has long intended to restore her as Queen of Mournhold under Imperial guidance. The text includes passages censored by order of the Temple and presents Barenziah's youth in a sensationalized manner, depicting promiscuity and criminal activity. As an unattributed and unauthorized work, its reliability is questionable, and its portrayal of the Queen Mother's early life should be treated with considerable skepticism.
topic_desc_basic: This unauthorized second volume of Queen Barenziah's biography covers her youth in Rifton, her involvement with the Thieves Guild, and her eventual capture by General Symmachus, who reveals Imperial plans to restore her as Queen of Mournhold. The text contains Temple-censored passages and its anonymous authorship makes its sensationalized account unreliable.

title: The Real Barenziah v III
topic_desc: This unauthorized biographical volume covers Barenziah's arrival at the Imperial City and her initial encounters with Tiber Septim. General Symmachus instructs her on the dignity and obedience expected of an Imperial appointee, reminding her that she rules Mournhold solely at the Emperor's pleasure. The narrative depicts Septim as surprisingly genial and vulnerable, sharing his vision of a united Tamriel under the Temple of the One. The account culminates in an intimate moment between the young queen and the aging Emperor, casting their relationship in a romantic light that sharply contradicts the official Imperial biography. As an unauthorised text, its portrayal of the Emperor's private confidences and Barenziah's past is likely sensationalized or unreliable.
topic_desc_basic: This unauthorized volume recounts Barenziah's journey to the Imperial City and her first meetings with Tiber Septim. It portrays a growing intimacy between the young queen and the Emperor, contradicting the official biography. The account is considered unreliable and potentially sensationalized.

title: The Real Barenziah v IV
topic_desc: The fourth volume of this unauthorized biography chronicles Queen Barenziah's return to Morrowind for her coronation, a ceremony blending ancient Dark Elven tradition with Imperial decree. She navigates the tensions between native elders and Imperial advisors while immersing herself in Dark Elven history. Following Tiber Septim's death decades later, Symmachus proposes, and Barenziah accepts, valuing his steadfast loyalty. Their politically successful marriage proves childless, however, prompting secretive and ultimately fruitless consultations with healers. The narrative concludes with Barenziah encountering a mysterious bard called the Nightingale, whose subversive songs hint at Morrowindish nationalism. As an anonymous and unauthorized account, the work presents a dramatized and potentially unreliable perspective on the Queen's private life and political struggles.
topic_desc_basic: The fourth volume of this unauthorized biography covers Queen Barenziah's coronation in Mournhold, her marriage to Symmachus following Tiber Septim's death, and their struggles with a childless union. It also introduces the mysterious bard called the Nightingale. As an anonymous account, its dramatized claims are potentially unreliable.

title: The Real Barenziah v V
topic_desc: This unauthorized biographical volume covers Queen Barenziah's life after the Staff of Chaos theft, detailing the births of Helseth and Morgiah and the subsequent deterioration of Mournhold's relations with the Empire. As Imperial levies escalate, Symmachus sends his family to the Imperial City, vowing he can destroy the Empire he helped build if they are harmed. The narrative climaxes with Barenziah's tense audience before Emperor Uriel Septim, during which she detects potent illusion magic veiling his true identity—a revelation implying Jagar Tharn's usurpation. As an anonymous, unsanctioned account, the work blends intimate domestic detail with explosive political accusations of treachery at the Imperial throne's highest level.
topic_desc_basic: The fifth volume of an unauthorized biography of Queen Barenziah. It recounts the births of her children Helseth and Morgiah, Mournhold's declining Imperial relations, Symmachus's threats against the Empire, and Barenziah's discovery of powerful illusion magic concealing the true identity of Emperor Uriel Septim during an audience at the Imperial City.

title: The Ruins of Kemel-Ze
topic_desc: Rolard Nordssen of the Imperial Society recounts his excavation of Kemel-Ze, the Dwemer 'Cliff City' on the mainland shore of the Vvardenfell Rift. Writing with undisguised Imperial arrogance, Nordssen describes the site's geography, centuries of looting by local villagers, and his discovery of carvings possibly depicting a Dwemer religious ritual—figures bowing before a giant emerging from a smoking mountain—which he claims are unique in the archaeological record. He also identifies a domed observatory and notes that the ruin's original surface level now lies hundreds of feet below present ground, a consequence of Red Mountain's eruption. The narrative reveals that most 'Dwarven armor' in circulation is merely stripped casing from Dwemer animunculi. Nordssen's account is marked by cultural contempt toward Dunmer, dismissiveness toward Tribunal religious taboos, and harsh treatment of hired laborers, making it an unreliable but informative first-person record of Imperial archaeological practice in Morrowind.
topic_desc_basic: A travel and excavation account by Imperial archaeologist Rolard Nordssen, describing his exploration of Kemel-Ze, a Dwemer cliff-side ruin on the mainland near the Vvardenfell Rift. The work notes the site's long history of looting, possible Dwemer religious carvings, and the true nature of Dwarven armor as repurposed animunculus casing.

title: The Story of Aevar Stone-Singer
topic_desc: A traditional Skaal myth recounting the journey of Aevar, a young man who volunteers to recover the six Gifts of the All-Maker—Water, Earth, Beasts, Trees, Sun, and Winds—after the Adversary, known as the Greedy Man, steals them from a complacent people. Framed as an oral lesson passed from grandfather to child, the narrative emphasizes humility and duty: Aevar succeeds precisely because he holds no formal rank. The tale identifies the Adversary with multiple aspects, including Thartaag the World-Devourer, and casts the Falmer as servants of this force. Notably, the story ends abruptly upon Aevar's return, deliberately refusing to reveal whether he received any reward or status, reinforcing the Skaal teaching that acting according to one's nature is its own fulfillment.
topic_desc_basic: A foundational Skaal myth about a youth named Aevar who reclaims the All-Maker's stolen gifts from the Greedy Man, an aspect of the Adversary. Framed as an oral lesson, the tale teaches that even the humblest member of the community can restore balance through perseverance and by acting according to their nature.

title: The True Noble's Code
topic_desc: Serjo Athyn Sarethi's doctrinal treatise outlining the principles governing Great House Redoran. It defines Redoran nobility through the triune virtues of duty, gravity, and piety. Duty is hierarchically owed to the Tribunal Temple, then House Redoran, and finally family and clan. Gravity demands solemnity and forbids rumor, while piety requires reverence for Aedra and Daedra. The text frames martial proficiency—long blade, spear, bow, athletics, and armor maintenance—as practical necessities for fulfilling duty rather than intrinsically honorable pursuits. It characterizes House Telvanni as scheming and House Hlaalu as untrustworthy, reflecting partisan rivalry. Prospective retainers must demonstrate suitable skills before the Redoran Council, and advancement requires proven service and obedience. The work serves as both ideological instruction and recruitment guidance for the House.
topic_desc_basic: A treatise by Serjo Athyn Sarethi defining the principles of Great House Redoran. It establishes the triune virtues of duty, gravity, and piety as essential for Redoran nobility, prioritizing duty to the Tribunal Temple, then the House, and finally family. It also outlines the martial skills required to fulfill one's obligations and the expectations for those seeking to join or advance within the House.

title: The Wild Elves
topic_desc: Kier-jo Chorvak's treatise examines the Ayleids, or Wild Elves, reclusive descendants of Tamriel's original inhabitants who persist across provincial wilds. Unlike assimilated Mer, the Ayleids shun Tamrielic, speaking a variation of Old Cyrodilic and dismissing outsiders as Pellani. The author acknowledges that prevailing stereotypes of their dark temperament stem from foreign bias, citing the civilized Ayleid sage Tjurhane Fyrre, whose writings reveal a vibrant, diverse tribal culture. Ultimately, Chorvak concedes that filtering legend from fact yields almost nothing; the Ayleids remain an enigmatic presence, vanishing from recorded history as swiftly as they appear.
topic_desc_basic: Kier-jo Chorvak's treatise surveys the Ayleids, or Wild Elves, reclusive Mer dwelling across Tamriel's wilds. Unlike their assimilated cousins, they shun outsiders—termed Pellani—and speak Old Cyrodilic. While commonly stereotyped as taciturn, the Ayleid sage Tjurhane Fyrre suggested a vibrant, diverse tribal culture. Ultimately, Chorvak concedes the Ayleids remain historical enigmas, with legend yielding almost no verifiable fact.

title: Vampires of Vvardenfell, v I
topic_desc: A scholarly overview of vampirism in Morrowind. The author argues that despite the Temple's violent antipathy toward necromancy making vampires seemingly rare, Dunmer authorities are experienced in handling them, and large communities could easily escape detection in remote wastelands or abandoned subterranean labyrinths. The text distinguishes the legendary Ash vampire from true undead, noting no specimen has been examined and anti-undead magic reportedly fails against them. It details Vvardenfell's three bloodlines: the frenzied, strong Quarra; the hypnotic, spellcasting Aundae; and the stealthy, agile Berne. The author outlines the poorly understood contraction process and the critical incubation period, during which the disease remains curable for up to 72 hours before becoming irreversible.
topic_desc_basic: A scholarly study of vampirism in Morrowind. It claims vampires may hide undetected in remote wastelands, distinguishes the legendary Ash vampire from true undead, and profiles Vvardenfell's three bloodlines: the strong Quarra, spellcasting Aundae, and stealthy Berne. It notes the vampirism disease is curable during a 72-hour incubation period.

title: Vampires of Vvardenfell, v II
topic_desc: This scholarly excerpt contrasts Western and Eastern traditions regarding vampirism and its cure. In the West, a legendary fraternity of vampire hunters allegedly consists of cured former vampires who conceal the remedy. In Morrowind, the Temple declares vampirism incurable; any cured vampire would be destroyed as an abomination, and failing to treat the disease within three days proves depravity. The text examines a peculiarly Dunmer tradition attributing the first vampire to Molag Bal spawning it upon a defeated foe, though the victim's identity varies across accounts. The author laments that the Temple discourages inquiry and restricts historical records. Notably, the account highlights Galur Rithari, a Buoyant Armiger formerly stationed at Bal Ur who claimed to be cured. The Temple imprisoned him for heresy until he recanted, after which he served out his years as a Vivec librarian.
topic_desc_basic: This volume contrasts Western legends of cured vampire hunters with the Temple of the Tribunal's doctrine that vampirism is incurable. It details the Dunmer belief that Molag Bal created the first vampire and notes the case of Galur Rithari, a Buoyant Armiger who claimed he was cured but later recanted.

title: Where Were You ... Dragon Broke
topic_desc: A compilation of four contradictory testimonies regarding the Middle Dawn, the Dragon Break caused by the Maruhkati Selectives' ritual on White-Gold Tower. Corax of the Elder Council admits Imperial accounts conflict, noting only universal agreement on eight falling stars. Mehra Nabisi offers orthodox Tribunal doctrine, framing the event as Lorkhan's iniquity and claiming the Tribunal alone shielded the Dunmer. R'leyt-harhr, a Khajiit, asserts the Mane tracked time via the moons, crediting Khajiit for the era's recorded duration and accusing Cyrodiil of repeating the fracture. Mannimarco, speaking as the God of Worms, treats the temporal chaos as a revelation of Dawn-era principles. Each account reflects its speaker's cultural bias and theological agenda, leaving the true nature of the catastrophe uncertain.
topic_desc_basic: A book collecting four conflicting accounts of the Middle Dawn, a Dragon Break caused by the Maruhkati Selectives. An Imperial bureaucrat, a Dunmer theologian, a Khajiit keeper, and the necromancer Mannimarco each explain the temporal catastrophe according to their own cultural biases and religious doctrines, offering no consensus on what truly occurred.

title: Yellow Book of 3E 426
topic_desc: The Yellow Book of 3E 426 is an official register of Great House Hlaalu, documenting the councilors of its Vvardenfell District alongside a summary of notable council affairs for that year. It formally lists Mistress Velanda Omani, Master Dram Bero, Master Crassius Curio, Master Yngling Half-Troll, and Mistress Nevena Ules, styling each by the grace of Almsivi and noting their residences and trading titles. The appended council affairs present the house's perspective on provincial events: praising reduced crime attributed to Imperial vigilance, lamenting violent clashes between the Thieves Guild and the Camonna Tong over black markets, noting the suppression of a minor Balmora tax revolt, and recording deputations to the Duke protesting high tariffs and taxes. The document serves as Hlaalu propaganda, projecting an image of orderly Imperial governance while subtly acknowledging widespread illicit trade and local unrest.
topic_desc_basic: The Yellow Book of 3E 426 is an official register of Great House Hlaalu listing its five Vvardenfell councilors and summarizing notable house affairs. It records the suppression of a Balmora tax revolt, violent competition between the Thieves Guild and the Camonna Tong, and council protests to the Duke over high tariffs, presenting the house's perspective on district governance.
aliases: Yellow Book of Great House Hlaalu

title: Mournhold Temple
topic_desc: The principal religious edifice of Mournhold, also called the Tribunal Palace or High Temple, this complex serves as both the traditional center of Tribunal worship and the administrative heart of the Temple hierarchy. Situated within a grand courtyard at the northern end of the city of Almalexia, it encompasses the Reception Area, the Hall of Ministry, an Infirmary, the Office of the Lord Archcanon, and the High Chapel. Historically, it served as the home of Almalexia. The complex connects to the subterranean ruins of Old Mournhold via the temple sewers. As the seat of the Lord Archcanon, it directs Temple affairs across Morrowind, while the High Chapel remains the focal point for veneration of the Tribunal within the ancient Indoril capital.
topic_desc_basic: The great religious and administrative center of the Tribunal Temple in Mournhold, also known as the High Temple or Tribunal Palace. Located in the city of Almalexia, it houses the High Chapel, Hall of Ministry, Infirmary, and the Lord Archcanon's offices. It historically served as the home of Almalexia and connects to the buried ruins of Old Mournhold.
aliases: Mournhold Temple: Office of the Lord Archcanon

title: Buckmoth Legion Fort
topic_desc: Buckmoth Legion Fort is an Imperial Legion garrison situated in the Ashlands region, due south of Ald'ruhn and west of the Daedric shrine at Ramimilk. The fort straddles the main road leading toward Ghostgate, serving as a strategic outpost for Imperial forces operating in the volcanic interior of Vvardenfell. Its architecture follows standard Imperial military construction, featuring distinct interior halls, prison holdings, and watchtowers. The compound provides extensive services typical of a major Legion installation, including facilities for enchanting, trade, apothecary work, healing, and smithing, alongside a drillmaster, a battlemage, and an Imperial Cult altar, cementing its role as a vital logistical and spiritual hub for Imperial personnel in the region.
topic_desc_basic: Buckmoth Legion Fort is an Imperial military garrison in the Ashlands, located south of Ald'ruhn along the road to Ghostgate. The walled compound includes interior halls, prison cells, and watchtowers. It serves as a major logistical and spiritual hub for the Imperial Legion, offering extensive services and an Imperial Cult altar.

title: Rethan Manor
topic_desc: Rethan Manor is a House Hlaalu stronghold situated on the Odai Plateau, southwest of Balmora and east of Hla Oad, on the northeast coast of the River Odai. The compound consists of a stone wall encircling a central manor house and three supporting residences. It represents the Hlaalu Great House's program of establishing fortified landholdings on Vvardenfell, constructed under legal land charter issued through the Hlaalu treasury. The surrounding region connects to Balmora's silt strider and Mages Guild services and to Hla Oad's boat traffic, placing the manor within the settled corridor of the Bitter Coast and the Odai River valley.
topic_desc_basic: Rethan Manor is a House Hlaalu stronghold on the Odai Plateau, southwest of Balmora and east of Hla Oad along the River Odai. A stone wall encloses a central manor and several support buildings. It serves as a Hlaalu landholding on Vvardenfell, accessible from both Balmora and the Bitter Coast.

title: Skaal Village
topic_desc: Skaal Village is the northernmost settlement in Tamriel, situated on the Felsaad Coast of Solstheim. It serves as the cultural and spiritual heart of the Skaal, a reclusive Nordic tribe devoted to the All-Maker and harmonious coexistence with nature. The settlement is built around a central Greathall used for communal feasts and gatherings, flanked by small, sturdy wooden dwellings. Skaal Honor Guards clad in traditional Nordic mail patrol the paths, reflecting the tribe's longstanding wariness of outsiders and their determination to protect their ancestral ways from external intrusion.
topic_desc_basic: Skaal Village is the northernmost settlement in Tamriel, located on Solstheim's Felsaad Coast. It is home to the Skaal, a reclusive Nordic tribe that reveres the All-Maker. The settlement consists of sturdy wooden huts arranged around a central Greathall and is heavily guarded against outsiders.

title: Arvel Manor
topic_desc: Arvel Manor is the plantation estate of the Arvel family, situated north of Vivec's Foreign Quarter and above Dren Plantation within the Ascadian Isles. Lacking a direct overland road, the manor is commonly reached by swimming the intervening lakes. The complex reflects the Hlaalu plantation economy, which relies on legally sanctioned slave labor within the Empire. Its architecture comprises a main manor house alongside several outbuildings, including a slavemaster's shack, slave quarters, and a storage shack, illustrating the organized infrastructure supporting the estate's operations.
topic_desc_basic: Arvel Manor is a plantation estate located north of Vivec's Foreign Quarter and above Dren Plantation. With no direct road, travelers typically swim the lakes to reach it. The Hlaalu-run estate operates under Imperial law, legally maintaining slaves housed in dedicated outbuildings like the Slave Shack and Slavemaster's Shack.

title: Bamz-Amschend
topic_desc: Bamz-Amschend is a vast Dwemer ruin lying deep beneath the city of Mournhold. Before their disappearance, its halls hosted a Dwemer Council Meet, marking it as a significant center of Dwarven governance. The city's notable districts include the Hall of Wails, Hall of Winds, Hearthfire Hall, King's Walk, Passage of the Walker, and Passage of Whispers. Its Skybreak Gallery housed the Karstangz-Bcharn, a colossal machine engineered to control surface weather. The ruin also includes Radac's Forge, the workshop of the weaponsmith Radac Stungnthumz. Subterranean passages connect Bamz-Amschend to the Daedric ruin Norenen-dur.
topic_desc_basic: Bamz-Amschend is a vast Dwemer ruin located beneath Mournhold. It once hosted a Dwemer Council Meet and housed the Karstangz-Bcharn, a giant weather-controlling machine within its Skybreak Gallery. The site includes Radac's Forge and connects to the Daedric ruin Norenen-dur.

title: Hlormaren
topic_desc: Hlormaren is one of the ancient Dunmer strongholds of Vvardenfell, situated on the central Bitter Coast just west of Balmora. Like the other old forts, it dates to a brighter age of Dunmer civilization and now stands largely abandoned, its halls prone to attracting whatever faction feels strong enough to claim them. The stronghold is notably extensive, comprising five levels: sewers, underground passages, a keep with bottom and top floors, and a rooftop dome. Unusually among the strongholds, Hlormaren possesses a sewer system with a direct outlet to the sea to the west. A propylon chamber within the fortress provides magical transit links to the strongholds of Marandus and Andasreth. Travelers are advised that these ruins, while architecturally fascinating, should be approached with considerable caution.
topic_desc_basic: Hlormaren is an ancient Dunmer stronghold on the Bitter Coast, west of Balmora. Built in an earlier age of Dunmer civilization, it now stands largely abandoned. The fortress spans five levels including sewers, underground passages, a multi-story keep, and a rooftop dome. A propylon chamber links it to Marandus and Andasreth. Travelers should approach with caution.

title: Indarys Manor
topic_desc: Indarys Manor is a House Redoran stronghold situated at the site of Bal Isra within the Ashlands region of Vvardenfell. The compound follows traditional Dunmer defensive architecture, featuring a central manor house and three auxiliary buildings enclosed by a sturdy stone wall. The Manor Services building functions as a Redoran tradehouse. Positioned along the rugged corridor between Ald'ruhn and Maar Gan, the manor sits in proximity to the ancient Dunmer strongholds of Andasreth, Falasmaryon, and Kogoruhn. Its strategic location provides regional access to nearby Propylon Chambers and the transport networks of the surrounding settlements.
topic_desc_basic: Indarys Manor is a House Redoran stronghold located at Bal Isra in the Ashlands region. The walled compound consists of a central manor and three surrounding buildings, including a tradehouse for Redoran services. It lies between Ald'ruhn and Maar Gan, near several ancient Dunmer strongholds.

title: Moonmoth Legion Fort
topic_desc: Moonmoth Legion Fort is an Imperial military installation situated southeast of Balmora in the West Gash region. It functions as the primary center for Imperial control in the surrounding district. The fortress features typical Imperial architectural design and includes interior facilities supporting the garrison, such as an Imperial Cult altar, apothecary, enchanter, smith, and trader. The compound's Prison Towers house the regional jail and an evidence chest, reflecting the fort's administrative and judicial role in maintaining Imperial law. Moonmoth anchors the Imperial presence along the western road network near Balmora.
topic_desc_basic: Moonmoth Legion Fort is an Imperial military fortress located southeast of Balmora in the West Gash. It serves as the primary center for Imperial control in the region, housing a garrison, an Imperial Cult altar, various services, and the Prison Towers containing the regional jail and evidence chest.

title: Old Mournhold
topic_desc: Old Mournhold comprises the subterranean ruins of the First Era city destroyed when Mehrunes Dagon invaded at the end of the First Era, before Almalexia and Sotha Sil banished him. The present-day Mournhold Sewers weave through these ruins, though their expansiveness means whole sections—such as forgotten sewers and abandoned passageways—remain lost to city administrators. The underground retains the architectural footprint of the ancient settlement, encompassing ruined manor districts, armories, crypts, and city gates, all bearing the scars of the Daedric devastation. These depths serve as a lasting monument to the conflict that reshaped Mournhold.
topic_desc_basic: Old Mournhold is the underground ruin of the city destroyed by Mehrunes Dagon at the end of the First Era, before Almalexia and Sotha Sil banished him. The modern Mournhold Sewers wind through these remains, though vast sections remain entirely forgotten by administrators.

title: Valenvaryon
topic_desc: Valenvaryon is an ancient Dunmer stronghold situated at the northern edge of the Ashlands, east of the Urshilaku Camp and north of Falasmaryon. Constructed during a brighter era of Dunmer history, the fortress has long lacked internal access, its original entrance stones broken down and repurposed into crude dwellings. Like other such strongholds, its remote ruins have attracted groups capable of holding them. The site's magical Propylon Chamber, linking to Rotheran and Falasmaryon, has escaped the physical degradation affecting the rest of the structure.
topic_desc_basic: An ancient Dunmer stronghold in the northern Ashlands. Its original entrance stones have been broken down and repurposed into crude dwellings, though the magical Propylon Chamber linking to Rotheran and Falasmaryon remains intact.

title: Falasmaryon
topic_desc: Falasmaryon is a Dunmer stronghold situated in the northern Ashlands, across the Foyada Bani-Dad from Maar Gan. Like other ancient Velothi fortresses, its multi-level architecture includes an upper level, a lower level, a propylon chamber linking it to Valenvaryon and Berandas, and one of the few sewer systems found in such strongholds. These structures have long been abandoned by their original builders, leaving them to be claimed by whatever faction can hold them. A small hut crowns the stronghold's exterior. The remote fortress stands as a formidable landmark along the foyada routes of the ash-covered region.
topic_desc_basic: Falasmaryon is an ancient Dunmer stronghold in the northern Ashlands, across the Foyada Bani-Dad from Maar Gan. It features multiple interior levels, a sewer system, and a propylon chamber linking it to Valenvaryon and Berandas. Long abandoned, such fortresses typically attract groups capable of claiming them.

title: Shulk Egg Mine
topic_desc: Shulk Egg Mine is a substantial House Hlaalu kwama egg mine situated in the bluffs west of the Odai River, a short distance southwest of Balmora. An old suspension bridge spanning the Odai lies just southeast of the entrance. The interior consists of a mining camp and a queen's lair. Reputedly the largest single source of kwama eggs on Vvardenfell, the mine represents a significant economic asset for House Hlaalu. The site can be reached via an unmarked mountain path from the Pelagiad-Balmora road or by following the river south from Balmora's silt strider port.
topic_desc_basic: Shulk Egg Mine is a large House Hlaalu kwama egg mine located in the bluffs west of the Odai River, a short distance southwest of Balmora. An old suspension bridge crosses the Odai just southeast of the entrance. The mine is a major source of kwama eggs on Vvardenfell.

title: Tel Uvirith
topic_desc: A Telvanni tower settlement in the Molag Amur region, built upon the site historically known as Uvirith's Grave. Unlike the walled strongholds of other Great Houses, Tel Uvirith consists of a central wizard's tower surrounded by organic fungal pods serving as dwellings, eschewing conventional defensive walls in favor of Dwemer Centurion constructs. The complex extends into subterranean dungeon levels beneath the tower proper. Situated in the rugged volcanic interior of Vvardenfell, the tower is isolated from major trade routes, with the nearest services located at Sadrith Mora to the east and Molag Mar to the west.
topic_desc_basic: A Telvanni tower settlement in Molag Amur, erected at the site of Uvirith's Grave. It features a central tower with surrounding fungal pod dwellings and relies on Dwemer Centurions for defense rather than walls. The isolated stronghold lies far from major travel routes in Vvardenfell's volcanic interior.

title: Ules Manor
topic_desc: Ules Manor is a Hlaalu plantation estate situated just west of Suran in the Ascadian Isles. The manor serves as the seat of Councilor Nevena Ules, a prominent figure within House Hlaalu. The complex includes the main residence and separate outbuildings designated as the Slave Shack and the Slavemaster's Shack, reflecting the typical Dunmer agricultural estate structure that relies on enslaved labor. Like many Hlaalu country estates, the manor combines mercantile agricultural purpose with political significance, its proximity to Suran ensuring easy access to regional trade routes while maintaining the insulated authority of a councilor's rural seat.
topic_desc_basic: A Hlaalu plantation estate located west of Suran in the Ascadian Isles. The manor belongs to House Hlaalu Councilor Nevena Ules and includes a main residence alongside separate slave and slavemaster's quarters, reflecting the typical layout of Dunmer agricultural plantations.

title: Urshilaku
topic_desc: The Urshilaku are an Ashlander tribe inhabiting the northern Ashlands and West Gash along the Sea of Ghosts. Renowned as lore-keepers and mystics, they serve as guardians of the Nerevarine prophecies. Their nomadic camp migrates with guar herds but remains anchored to the northern coast. East of their territory lie the Urshilaku Burial Caverns, a network of ancestral tombs comprising the Astral, Fragile, Juno, Kakuna, Karma, Kefka, and Laterus Burials. These caverns hold the remains of generations, reflecting a tradition where guar bones are preserved for spiritual guidance. Despite their conservatism, the Urshilaku uniquely extend Clanfriend status to outsiders.
topic_desc_basic: The Urshilaku are an Ashlander tribe roaming the northern Ashlands and West Gash near the Sea of Ghosts. Known as traditionalist lore-keepers and guardians of the Nerevarine prophecies, they maintain ancestral burial caverns east of their territory, comprising seven named tomb chambers.

title: Arvel Plantation
topic_desc: Arvel Plantation is a large agricultural estate situated in the Ascadian Isles between Pelagiad and Suran. It exemplifies the wealthy Hlaalu plantation economy, with slave labor working the fields to cultivate cash crops such as corkbulb root. The estate's prosperity is evident in the opulent lifestyle of its noble residents, whose influence and wealth derive directly from this lucrative agricultural enterprise.
topic_desc_basic: A large agricultural estate in the Ascadian Isles between Pelagiad and Suran. It exemplifies the wealthy Hlaalu plantation economy, where slave labor cultivates cash crops such as corkbulb root, generating significant prosperity and influence for its noble residents.

title: Ashimanu Egg Mine
topic_desc: Ashimanu Egg Mine is an isolated kwama egg mine situated in the West Gash region, positioned between Ald'ruhn, Andasreth, and Gnisis. The site consists of a main tunnel network and a distinct interior chamber designated as the Queen's Lair. As a typical kwama egg operation, the mine's architecture follows natural cavern formations adapted for egg harvesting. The remote location makes it one of the less accessible mining sites in the region, relying on the kwama colony's natural productivity to sustain its output.
topic_desc_basic: An isolated kwama egg mine in the West Gash region, located between Ald'ruhn, Gnisis, and Andasreth. The site features standard cavern workings and a designated Queen's Lair chamber for the colony's egg production.

title: Berandas
topic_desc: Berandas is an ancient Dunmer stronghold situated in the West Gash, south of Gnisis and east of Koal Cave. Like other strongholds of the early Dunmer, it has been long abandoned by its original builders, subsequently attracting various groups seeking a defensible position. The fortress is built with a multi-level keep and features a functioning Propylon Chamber linking it to Falasmaryon and Andasreth. Beneath the main structure lies an extensive underground cave system extending deep into the earth. Though nominally ruinous, Berandas remains a significant landmark of Velothi military architecture and a notable waypoint in the regional Propylon network.
topic_desc_basic: An old Dunmer stronghold in the West Gash region, south of Gnisis. It features a multi-story keep and a functional Propylon Chamber connecting to Falasmaryon and Andasreth. Beneath the fort, deep underground tunnels honeycomb the earth.

title: Hairat-Vassamsi Egg Mine
topic_desc: Hairat-Vassamsi Egg Mine is a kwama egg mine situated west-northwest of Maar Gan in the Ashlands of Vvardenfell. The complex consists of tunneled passages worked into the surrounding terrain, with a deeper chamber designated the Queen's Lair where the colony's kwama queen is housed. Kwama workers and warriors form the mine's biological population, as is typical of functioning egg operations. The Blight has spread to the colony, reflecting the broader affliction affecting Vvardenfell's kwama populations across the island. Egg mines such as this one serve as important economic resources for nearby settlements, yielding kwama eggs as both food staple and trade commodity. The mine's proximity to Maar Gan ties it to that township's commercial and subsistence network.
topic_desc_basic: Hairat-Vassamsi Egg Mine is a kwama egg mine located west-northwest of Maar Gan in Vvardenfell's Ashlands. The complex features worked tunnels and a deeper Queen's Lair chamber. Like other egg mines on the island, it forms part of the local economy centered on kwama egg harvesting.

title: Koal Cave Entrance
topic_desc: Koal Cave Entrance marks the surface opening of Koal Cave, a natural cavern system situated in the West Gash region of Vvardenfell. The entrance lies near the settlement of Gnisis, set among the region's characteristic rocky slopes and lush vegetation. As a stable geographic feature, the cave mouth provides access to the subterranean interior. The West Gash's winding foyada and river corridors make such caves notable waypoints, and Koal Cave holds cultural significance for local Dunmer, traditionally associated with the shrine to Vivec within its depths.
topic_desc_basic: Koal Cave Entrance is the surface opening of Koal Cave, located in the West Gash region of Vvardenfell near Gnisis. The cave mouth provides access to a natural cavern system that holds cultural importance for the Dunmer, containing a shrine to Vivec within its depths.

title: Marandus
topic_desc: Marandus is an ancient Dunmer stronghold situated on the shore of Lake Nabia within the Molag Amur region, northwest of Suran. Like other surviving strongholds of that earlier era, its architecture features a multi-level interior comprising upper and lower halls, a central dome, and an integral Propylon Chamber. This chamber provides teleportation links to the strongholds of Telasero and Hlormaren. Though such fortresses were largely abandoned after their golden age, their defensible isolation continues to attract underworld elements and rogue factions.
topic_desc_basic: Marandus is an ancient Dunmer stronghold on the shore of Lake Nabia in the Molag Amur region, northwest of Suran. The fortress contains upper and lower levels, a dome, and a Propylon Chamber linking to Telasero and Hlormaren. Like many such strongholds, it has fallen into abandonment.

title: Matus-Akin Egg Mine
topic_desc: Matus-Akin Egg Mine is a kwama egg mine situated west of Holamayan and northeast of Molag Mar along the Azura's Coast region. Like many of Vvardenfell's egg mines, it serves as a traditional site for kwama egg harvesting, a staple of Dunmer diet and trade. The mine's architecture consists of natural caverns adapted with minimal structural supports typical of such operations.
topic_desc_basic: Matus-Akin Egg Mine is a kwama egg mine located west of Holamayan and northeast of Molag Mar. It consists of mining tunnels and a Queen's Lair chamber. Kwama egg mines are traditional sources of food and trade goods in Vvardenfell.

title: Mount Assarnibibi
topic_desc: Mount Assarnibibi is a mountain peak north of Molag Mar in the Molag Amur region of Vvardenfell. Its summit holds a Tribunal Temple shrine that draws pilgrims alongside nearby Mount Kand. Temple lore holds that Molag Bal here oversaw the ninety-nine lovers of Boethiah, who gave birth to Almalexia. The mountain's full extent is uncertain; the cave of Dubdilla runs beneath it, with an entrance as far north as the southern outskirts of Vos. The shrine's association with Almalexia's divine origin makes it one of the more doctrinally significant pilgrimage destinations on Vvardenfell, reached after completing the Pilgrimage of the Four Corners.
topic_desc_basic: Mount Assarnibibi is a mountain peak north of Molag Mar in Vvardenfell's Molag Amur region. A Tribunal Temple shrine crowns its summit and attracts pilgrims. Temple lore teaches that Molag Bal here oversaw the ninety-nine lovers of Boethiah, who gave birth to Almalexia.

title: Mzahnch Ruin
topic_desc: Mzahnch is a Dwemer ruin situated along the rocky southeastern shoreline of Azura's Coast. Like other settlements of the vanished Deep Elves, it consists of weathered stone corridors, domed chambers, and animaculorian workshops built in the distinctive Dwemer architectural style. The site overlooks the Azura's Coast waters, isolated from major Imperial settlements. Its historical purpose likely mirrored other Dwemer strongholds, serving as a center for arcane study and engineering before the race's disappearance. The ruin's remote coastal placement makes it a landmark for navigators traversing the southeastern island chains.
topic_desc_basic: Mzahnch is a Dwemer ruin on Azura's Coast in southeastern Vvardenfell. Built by the vanished Deep Elves, its weathered stone corridors and domed chambers follow typical Dwemer architecture. The remote coastal site stands isolated along the rocky shoreline, a landmark for those navigating the region's waters.

title: Mzuleft Ruin
topic_desc: Mzuleft is a Dwemer ruin situated in the Sheogorad region of Vvardenfell. Like other abandoned Dwemer strongholds, it exhibits the characteristic blend of surface structures and deep subterranean chambers built from massive stone blocks and adorned with arcane steam pipes and machinery. The isolated Sheogorad archipelago hosts several such sites, and Mzuleft stands as a testament to the Dwemer presence in these remote northern islands long before their disappearance. The ruin's architecture reflects standard Dwemer construction principles, with domed halls and angular buttresses. Its remote island location shields it from easy access, leaving its deeper vaults largely undisturbed by Imperial colonization and settlement.
topic_desc_basic: Mzuleft is a Dwemer ruin located in the Sheogorad region of Vvardenfell. It features characteristic Dwemer stone architecture and subterranean chambers, reflecting the ancient Deep Elf presence in the remote northern islands before their mysterious disappearance.

title: Nchuleft Ruin
topic_desc: Nchuleft is a Dwemer ruin situated in the Grazelands of Vvardenfell. Like other sites of the vanished Deep Elves, it exhibits their characteristic stonework and arcane machinery, preserving the inscrutable architectural and engineering legacy of a civilization that disappeared millennia ago. The Grazelands' open terrain makes the ruin relatively accessible compared to more remote island sites, attracting scholarly interest in its structural layout and mechanical remnants. As with all Dwemer strongholds, its original purpose remains debated among scholars of Tamrielic antiquity, though its design follows the standardized subterranean and surface compound patterns typical of Dwemer settlement across Morrowind.
topic_desc_basic: Nchuleft is a Dwemer ruin located in the Grazelands region of Vvardenfell. It contains the characteristic stone architecture and arcane machinery left behind by the vanished Deep Elves. The site stands as a typical example of Dwemer construction, its original purpose lost to history alongside its builders.

title: Norenen-dur
topic_desc: Norenen-dur is an extensive cavern network lying deep beneath Mournhold, accessed through the city's subterranean depths. Its named sectors—the Basilica of Divine Whispers, the Citadel of Myn Dhrur, the Grand Stair, the Teeth that Gnash, and the Wailingdelve—suggest a site of considerable age, bearing architectural remnants and nomenclature that evoke both sacred and martial purposes. The sprawling grottoes, carved passages, and natural caverns form a layered subterranean complex. Water flows through its lowest reaches, while the stone halls above retain the character of ancient construction. The site remains a notable fixture of the region's underground geography, its original builders and purpose lost to obscurity.
topic_desc_basic: Norenen-dur is a vast cavern complex deep beneath Mournhold, reachable through the city's underground passages. Its distinct areas include the Basilica of Divine Whispers, the Citadel of Myn Dhrur, the Grand Stair, the Teeth that Gnash, and the Wailingdelve. These stone halls and natural grottoes form one of the region's most extensive subterranean sites.

title: Pudai Egg Mine
topic_desc: Pudai Egg Mine is a kwama egg mine located in the Sheogorad region, west-southwest of Dagon Fel and west of Mzuleft. Long lost and absent from most maps, the mine is the subject of persistent legends claiming it harbors extraordinary treasure: seven golden kwama eggs produced by its queen. The subterranean complex consists of a main tunnel network and a submerged Queen's Lair. The surrounding Sheogorad wilderness is notoriously labyrinthine, contributing to the mine's obscurity and the failure of prior expeditions to locate it.
topic_desc_basic: Pudai Egg Mine is a lost kwama egg mine in the Sheogorad region, west-southwest of Dagon Fel. Legends claim the mine's queen produces seven extraordinary golden eggs, though its remote location has kept it hidden from most mapmakers and travelers.

title: Salit Camp
topic_desc: Salit Camp is a medium-sized outcast Ashlander settlement situated just inland from the Azura's Coast waterfront, southwest of Tel Mora. The camp comprises traditional Ashlander yurts, including those designated as Zalit's Yurt and Zelay's Yurt, which provide shelter from the hostile daedra roaming the adjacent Grazelands. Like other outcast camps, it stands apart from the settled Great House territories, maintaining the nomadic Ashlander way of life on Vvardenfell's rugged northeastern coast.
topic_desc_basic: An outcast Ashlander camp on Azura's Coast, southwest of Tel Mora. Its traditional yurts shelter the inhabitants from dangerous daedra roaming the nearby Grazelands.

title: Sanctus Shrine
topic_desc: The Sanctus Shrine is a Tribunal Temple holy site situated on a medium-sized island in the Sheogorad region, due west of Dagon Fel. The site consists of a modest shack accompanied by a triolith shrine. It holds particular significance for the faithful as the secluded retreat where Archcanon Tholer Saryoni composed his widely read sermons. Reaching the shrine requires navigating the dangerous coastal waters of the Sheogorad archipelago. The Sanctus Shrine is notably the destination of the Silent Pilgrimage, a rigorous Temple trial requiring devotees to travel to the site under a strict vow of silence.
topic_desc_basic: The Sanctus Shrine is a Tribunal Temple holy site on an island west of Dagon Fel in the Sheogorad region. It consists of a modest shack and a triolith. The shrine is revered as the place where Archcanon Tholer Saryoni wrote his famous sermons, and it serves as the destination for the Temple's rigorous Silent Pilgrimage.

title: Sarimisun-Assa Egg Mine
topic_desc: Sarimisun-Assa Egg Mine is a medium-sized kwama egg mine located just north of Andasreth Stronghold. Typical of such operations, it consists of worked tunnels and a distinct Queen's Lair chamber housing the colony's kwama queen. Consequently, the operation has been abandoned by its Dunmer miners, who left behind little of value. The subterranean architecture follows standard Imperial and Dunmer mining practices for kwama colonies, with the Queen's Lair serving as the colony's heart.
topic_desc_basic: Sarimisun-Assa Egg Mine is a medium-sized kwama egg mine north of Andasreth Stronghold. The Blight has afflicted the colony, including the kwama queen in her lair, forcing miners to abandon the tunnels.

title: Tower of Tel Fyr
topic_desc: Tel Fyr is a Telvanni wizard tower on a small island off the south-central coast of Vvardenfell, within the Azura's Coast region near the Molag Amur badlands. The tower complex consists of a central fungal growth rising above subterranean halls carved into the rock, including the Hall of Fyr and the deeper Onyx Hall. Unlike most Telvanni settlements, the tower incorporates ancient Daedric structural elements, suggesting the site predates the Telvanni occupation. The tower is remote and intentionally isolated, reachable only by water or levitation across its vertical interior. It serves as a private arcane retreat rather than a populated Telvanni council seat, reflecting the Telvanni tradition of powerful magisters building towers in solitude. The surrounding waters and rugged coastline keep the site inaccessible to ordinary travelers.
topic_desc_basic: Tel Fyr is an isolated Telvanni wizard tower on a small island off Vvardenfell's south-central coast, near the Molag Amur badlands. The tower's interior halls, including the Hall of Fyr and Onyx Hall, are built vertically and require levitation to navigate fully. The site incorporates ancient Daedric stonework, suggesting it predates Telvanni settlement. It serves as a private arcane retreat rather than a populated settlement.

title: Tureynulal
topic_desc: Tureynulal is a ruined Dwemer citadel within the Ghostfence in the Red Mountain region, situated northeast of the Dagoth Ur facility. Like other strongholds of the interior, it reflects the architectural and arcane sophistication of the Deep Elves before their disappearance. The citadel is divided into four distinct sections: the Bladder of Clovis, the Eye of Duggan, the Eye of Thom Wye, and Kagrenac's Library. The latter chamber indicates the site's historical role as a repository for Dwemer knowledge, likely associated with the Tonal Architect Kagrenac and his studies of the Heart of Lorkhan. The citadel's proximity to the Red Mountain core underscores its significance in the ancient Dwemer infrastructure of the region.
topic_desc_basic: Tureynulal is a ruined Dwemer citadel within the Ghostfence in the Red Mountain region, northeast of Dagoth Ur. The fortress comprises four interior sections: the Bladder of Clovis, the Eye of Duggan, the Eye of Thom Wye, and Kagrenac's Library. Its name and layout reflect its ancient Dwemer origin.

title: Vor Lair
topic_desc: Vor Lair is a subterranean complex on the island of Solstheim, situated in the rocky terrain of the Brodir Grove region. The site comprises two distinct areas: the outer Chambers of Alta Vor and an inner interior section, suggesting a layered construction of considerable depth. The architecture bears the hallmarks of ancient Nordic tomb-building, with carved stone passages and burial chambers cut into the island's basalt substrate. Such sites dot Solstheim's landscape, remnants of early Nord settlers who established holds and interred their dead in elaborate underground complexes. The lair's remote location and substantial construction indicate it once served as a significant burial or ceremonial site, though its original builders and occupants have long since passed from memory.
topic_desc_basic: Vor Lair is an underground complex on Solstheim, located in the Brodir Grove region. It consists of the Chambers of Alta Vor and an inner interior section. The site follows the pattern of ancient Nordic tombs found across the island, featuring carved stone passages and burial chambers built into the rocky terrain by early Nord settlers.

title: Wolverine Hall
topic_desc: Wolverine Hall is an Imperial fort situated on Azura's Coast immediately south of Sadrith Mora. It represents the Empire's effort to project authority in a region dominated by House Telvanni, who tolerate the garrison largely out of indifference rather than acceptance. The fort's architecture conceals organizations forbidden within the Telvanni city itself, specifically the local Fighters Guild, Mages Guild, and an Imperial Cult shrine, all operating under lease from the Telvanni Council. A Nord-style tavern, Dirty Muriel's Cornerclub, occupies the causeway between the Hall and Sadrith Mora, serving as the local Thieves Guild headquarters and occasionally facilitating discreet arrangements with the Hall's mages.
topic_desc_basic: An Imperial fort south of Sadrith Mora on Azura's Coast, built to project Imperial influence into Telvanni territory. The Hall houses the local Fighters Guild, Mages Guild, and Imperial Cult shrine, organizations not permitted within the Telvanni town itself. Dirty Muriel's Cornerclub, a Nord tavern hosting the Thieves Guild, sits between the fort and the city.

title: Abaelun Mine
topic_desc: Abaelun Mine is Vvardenfell's sole operational diamond mine, situated just beyond the hills northeast of Caldera. The site represents a collaborative venture between the Empire and House Hlaalu, blending Imperial oversight with Dunmer labor to extract the island's most precious gemstones. While modest in size, the mine yields a rich supply of diamonds, making it a notable point of resource extraction and economic cooperation in the region.
topic_desc_basic: Abaelun Mine is Vvardenfell's only operational diamond mine, located in the hills northeast of Caldera. The small excavation operates as a joint venture between the Empire and House Hlaalu to extract precious gemstones.

title: Abaesen-Pulu Egg Mine
topic_desc: Abaesen-Pulu Egg Mine sits on the Bitter Coast roughly halfway between Seyda Neen and Vivec, just north of the main road. It is a kwama egg mine that has fallen to blight, rendering it nonoperational. The typical architecture of such a site consists of excavated tunnels and chambers carved into the hillside to follow kwama nests. Owing to the blighted infestation, no miners work the tunnels, and the site yields no productive output.
topic_desc_basic: Abaesen-Pulu Egg Mine is a blighted kwama egg mine on the Bitter Coast, approximately halfway between Seyda Neen and Vivec, just north of the road. The mine is nonoperational and unworked due to the blight infestation.

title: Abebaal Egg Mine
topic_desc: Abebaal Egg Mine is a Telvanni-operated kwama egg mine on the northern coast of a small island northwest of Tel Branora, in southeastern Vvardenfell's Azura's Coast region. The mine lies between Tel Branora and Molag Mar across the scattered archipelago. Like other kwama mines on Vvardenfell, it functions as a source of kwama eggs, a staple food and trade good throughout Morrowind. Its remote island setting makes it reachable primarily by water from Tel Branora or overland routes toward Molag Mar, reflecting the Telvanni practice of establishing economic holdings across their coastal territories.
topic_desc_basic: Abebaal Egg Mine lies on an island northwest of Tel Branora along Azura's Coast. Operated by House Telvanni, it produces kwama eggs for trade and sustenance across southeastern Vvardenfell. Its island location requires sea travel from nearby Telvanni settlements.

title: Ahallaraddon Egg Mine
topic_desc: Ahallaraddon Egg Mine is a small kwama egg mine situated on the southeastern corner of the Morrowind mainland, north of the Shrine of Azura. The workings include a partially submerged section, consistent with the low coastal wetlands characterizing that remote stretch of shore. Like other kwama mines across Morrowind, it functions as a local source of eggs, a dietary staple and modest trade good. Its distance from major settlements places it among the quieter economic outposts of the southeastern hinterland.
topic_desc_basic: Ahallaraddon Egg Mine is a small kwama egg mine on the southeastern mainland of Morrowind, north of the Shrine of Azura. Its workings include a partially submerged section reflecting the surrounding coastal lowlands. It serves as a local source of kwama eggs.

title: Ahanibi-Malmus Egg Mine
topic_desc: Ahanibi-Malmus Egg Mine is situated in the Ashlands southeast of Kogoruhn, just north of the Ghostfence and south of Kora-Dur. Once a kwama egg harvesting operation, the mine is now blighted and entirely abandoned. The diseased kwama within preclude any continued industry, leaving the tunnels devoid of workers or resources. Its proximity to the Ghostfence places it firmly within the dangerous, blighted interior of the Ashlands.
topic_desc_basic: An abandoned kwama egg mine in the Ashlands, located southeast of Kogoruhn and just north of the Ghostfence. Blighted kwama have overrun the tunnels, halting all operations.

title: Aharasaplit Camp
topic_desc: Aharasaplit Camp is an outcast Ashlander settlement on the southern shoreline of Sheogorad island, situated southwest of Dagon Fel village. The camp consists of a yurt erected on the beach, characteristic of the portable felt-and-frame dwellings used by nomadic Ashlander kindreds across Vvardenfell. Its coastal placement reflects the practical needs of small groups living beyond the authority of both Great House settlements and mainstream Ashlander clans. Sheogorad's rugged, island-dotted geography isolates the camp, reachable only by footpaths threading through the archipelago's rocky terrain. The designation 'outcast' marks its inhabitants as separated from the four recognized Ashlander tribes of the Ashlands and Grazelands, existing on the social periphery of Vvardenfell's indigenous Dunmer culture.
topic_desc_basic: Travelers on Sheogorad island may encounter Aharasaplit Camp on the southern coast, southwest of Dagon Fel. It is a small Ashlander yurt settlement whose inhabitants live as outcasts, separated from the recognized tribal clans of Vvardenfell. The remote, beachside location reflects the marginal existence such groups endure.

title: Aidanat Camp
topic_desc: Aidanat Camp, also called Abassel's Yurt, is a small Ashlander encampment situated on the coastal slopes just south of the Redoran settlement of Ald Velothi in the West Gash region. The camp consists of a single traditional yurt of the sort used by nomadic Ashlander bands, though its occupants are outcasts rather than a recognized tribal community. Its isolation on the wind-swept bluffs above the Bitter Coast reflects the marginal status of those who dwell apart from the four main Ashlander tribes of Vvardenfell.
