Indoranyon appears in the historical fiction Poison Song by Bristin Xel, attesting to its cultural recognition. Over the centuries the ruin has attracted various parties strong enough to claim it, including rogue battlemages and sorcerers drawn to its defensible architecture and remote coastal position.
topic_desc_basic: Indoranyon is an ancient Dunmer stronghold on Vvardenfell's eastern coast, south-southeast of Vos near the Grazelands. Like other pre-Empire strongholds, it dates from an older era of Dunmer civilization and now stands as a ruin. It retains a propylon chamber linking to Falensarano and Rotheran. The name means 'Blessed Greenland' in the Dunmeri tongue.

title: Khartag Point
topic_desc: Khartag Point is a prominent coastal rock formation along Vvardenfell's Bitter Coast, situated northwest of Gnaar Mok. The site holds cultural significance for Orcs, named after the warrior Khartag, who perished there following a battle. The towering boulder subsequently gained notoriety as a site where another Orc leapt to his death on a dare. Recently, a large Daedric statue has been carved directly into the rock face by an Orc sculptor, transforming the landmark's appearance and adding a new layer of reverence to the location.
topic_desc_basic: A towering coastal rock on Vvardenfell's Bitter Coast, northwest of Gnaar Mok. It is named after a famed Orc warrior who died there after a battle, and is known among Orcs for a fatal dare leap from its heights. A newly carved Daedric statue now marks the stone.

title: Minabi
topic_desc: Minabi is a medium-sized natural cave on Azura's Coast, situated directly south of the Telasero stronghold and southeast of Suran. The coastal entrance lies where the road from Telasero meets the shore and curves around steep hills. The layout reflects typical smuggler and bandit occupation of remote coastal caverns throughout the Ascadian Isles and Azura's Coast frontier.
topic_desc_basic: Minabi is a coastal cave complex on Azura's Coast, located south of the Telasero stronghold and southeast of Suran. The cavern features multiple levels with natural rock formations adapted into a remote hideout, typical of the region's shoreline geology. Its coastal position and multi-chamber layout make it representative of the secluded caves found throughout this stretch of Morrowind's eastern coast.

title: Odai Plateau
topic_desc: The Odai Plateau is a raised landform on the west bank of the Odai River within the Bitter Coast region. Situated southwest of Balmora and east of Hla Oad, it lies along the river path past the Shulk Egg Mine. The plateau serves as the site for the House Hlaalu stronghold, Rethan Manor, strategically positioned to secure Hlaalu interests along this vital waterway.
topic_desc_basic: A raised landform on the Bitter Coast, the Odai Plateau occupies the west bank of the Odai River southwest of Balmora. It hosts Rethan Manor, the fortified stronghold of House Hlaalu.

title: Salmantu
topic_desc: Salmantu is a Sixth House cave sanctuary occupying a peninsula north of Holamayan in the Azura's Coast region of southeastern Vvardenfell. The complex consists of natural caverns fitted with a dedicated shrine, ash statues, and corprus growths characteristic of House Dagoth's scattered coastal bases. A Sixth House bell hammer denotes the site's ritual function. These caverns serve as gathering points where the cult's dreamers and ash-bound servants congregate under Dagoth Ur's spreading influence. Salmantu's proximity to Holamayan, the Dissident Priests' secluded monastery, places a center of heretical worship near one of the Temple's most contentious theological rivals, reflecting the broader spiritual contest playing out across Vvardenfell's remote southeastern shores.
topic_desc_basic: Salmantu is a Sixth House cave complex on a peninsula north of Holamayan in southeastern Vvardenfell's Azura's Coast region. The caverns house a shrine to Dagoth Ur amid ash statues and corprus growths, serving as one of House Dagoth's scattered coastal sanctuaries where the cult's followers gather.

title: Sanit
topic_desc: Sanit is a Sixth House shrine occupying a coastal cave on the northwestern edge of the Grazelands, situated southwest of the Ahemmusa Ashlander camp. Its strategic position threatens both the Ahemmusa and the settlements of Vos and Tel Vos. The interior features a typical Sixth House shrine, complete with ash statues and a bell hammer, alongside a trough holding a copy of The Wolf Queen, Book III and a secured chest of gems.
topic_desc_basic: Sanit is a Sixth House shrine located in a coastal cave on the northwestern Grazelands, southwest of the Ahemmusa camp. Its position threatens nearby settlements like Vos and Tel Vos.

title: Shashpilamat
topic_desc: Shashpilamat is a Daedric shrine dedicated to Malacath, situated on the Azura's Coast mainland west of the Holamayan monastery. The site consists of two unconnected interior areas: an antechamber and the main sanctuary. The antechamber provides sparse lodging and storage, while the main shrine chamber houses an altar of offerings and a side passage terminating at a collapsed doorway. Like many remote Daedric ruins dotting the Vvardenfell coast, Shashpilamat serves as an isolated place of veneration for Malacath's Orcish followers, its crumbling architecture reflecting the harsh, neglected state of such remote wilderness sanctuaries.
topic_desc_basic: Shashpilamat is a Daedric shrine to Malacath located on the Azura's Coast mainland, west of Holamayan. The ruin consists of two unconnected interior chambers: an antechamber and a main sanctuary with an altar. It serves as an isolated site of veneration for Orcish worshippers of Malacath.

title: Subdun
topic_desc: Subdun is a Sixth House cave complex situated on a small island in the Sea of Ghosts, just south across the water from Koal Cave in the West Gash region of Vvardenfell. The entrance opens into a crescent-shaped bay on the island's shore. The interior consists of natural volcanic caverns with a lava chamber accessible only by levitation, alongside a dedicated shrine area. As a Sixth House site, Subdun serves as a remote cultic installation devoted to Dagoth Ur, reflecting the growing reach of the Sixth House across Vvardenfell. Its island location provides isolation from mainland settlements while remaining within sight of the prominent Koal Cave landmark.
topic_desc_basic: Subdun is a Sixth House cave shrine on a small island south of Koal Cave in the West Gash region of Vvardenfell. The entrance sits in a crescent-shaped bay. The interior contains natural caverns with lava formations and a dedicated shrine area devoted to Dagoth Ur, reflecting the Sixth House's presence in the region.

title: Tukushapal
topic_desc: Tukushapal is a hidden cavern network within the Marvani Ancestral Tomb in the Molag Amur region. Its outer chamber forms a maze-like passage terminating at a sealed door that leads to the inner Sepulcher. This vast subterranean hall contains a pool where a ship is moored, serving as the ceremonial burial vessel for Olmgerd the Outlaw, a First Age Nord prince. The cavern architecture merges natural rock formations with carved tomb structures, and the ceiling conceals a high hidden ledge. The site stands as a significant example of ancient Nordic ship burial practices transplanted to Morrowind.
topic_desc_basic: Tukushapal is a hidden cavern within the Marvani Ancestral Tomb in the Molag Amur region. Its maze-like outer passages lead to a Sepulcher housing an ancient Nordic ship burial for Olmgerd the Outlaw, a First Age Nord prince. The cavern ceiling conceals a high hidden ledge above the burial chamber.

title: Yakin
topic_desc: Yakin is a natural cavern on the mainland coast of the Grazelands, northwest of Tel Aruhn across a narrow strait. The entrance lies just steps from the waterline, sheltered among a small rock formation and facing southeast toward the sea. The cave extends inland to a Sixth House shrine chamber, a characteristic arrangement of cultic architecture adapted to natural cavern geometry. A bell chamber adjoins the shrine area, marking the site as a functioning Sixth House base rather than a mere lair. Its coastal position makes it accessible by water or levitation from Tel Aruhn, though the surrounding Grazelands shoreline can easily conceal the entrance from those traveling along the coast. The presence of Sixth House occupation indicates Dagoth Ur's influence has extended to the mainland near Zainab territory.
topic_desc_basic: Yakin is a cavern on the mainland coast of the Grazelands, northwest of Tel Aruhn. The entrance sits close to the waterline among rocks. The cave contains a Sixth House shrine and is an active cult site. It can be reached by swimming or flying northwest from Tel Aruhn and crossing one island.

title: Abanabi
topic_desc: Abanabi is a cave network beneath Zafirbel Bay in the Azura's Coast region. Its surface entrance sits on an island southwest of Sadrith Mora and northeast of Tel Fyr, marked by three large Emperor Parasols. The caves are notable as one of the few locations in Vvardenfell where diamonds naturally occur, alongside raw ebony and other mineral deposits, some submerged. A deeper section of the system connects directly to Tel Fyr. The caves provide a remote and defensible refuge, attracting sorcerers who claim isolated platforms within the caverns.
topic_desc_basic: A cave system on an island in Zafirbel Bay, northeast of Tel Fyr and southwest of Sadrith Mora. The caverns are known as one of the few diamond-bearing sites in Vvardenfell and feature underwater passages and mineral deposits.

title: Abernanit
topic_desc: Abernanit is a cave on the Bitter Coast peninsula southeast of Gnaar Mok. In the mid-Second Era, it was a Daedric ruin and shrine to Mehrunes Dagon, housing Sixth House cultists under the supposed heir Dagoth Thras. Circa 3E 150, Tribunal forces under Rangidil Ketil besieged the shrine. Though greatly outnumbered, Rangidil slew Thras through cunning, an event immortalized in the Temple text "The Death Blow of Abernanit." By 3E 427, the Daedric architecture has vanished entirely, leaving only a natural cavern.
topic_desc_basic: Abernanit is a cave on the Bitter Coast peninsula southeast of Gnaar Mok. It was once a Daedric shrine to Mehrunes Dagon and site of a famed Tribunal victory over the Sixth House cultist Dagoth Thras, but its Daedric architecture has long since vanished.

title: Abinabi
topic_desc: Abinabi is an unremarkable cavern situated in the northwestern Ashlands, positioned south of the Urshilaku Camp between the Dwemer ruin of Bthungthumz and the Urshilaku Burial Caverns. It lies along the road west of Falasmaryon. The cave serves as a Sixth House shrine, a site of Corprus cult devotion dedicated to Dagoth Ur. Its architecture is typical of such hidden sanctums, housing a great bell and ash statues central to the cult's rituals. The surrounding region is sparsely populated, dominated by the encroaching Blight and the territorial reach of the Urshilaku Ashlander camp, making the shrine's presence a localized threat to travelers and nomads alike.
topic_desc_basic: Abinabi is an unremarkable cave in the northwestern Ashlands, located south of the Urshilaku Camp between Bthungthumz and the Urshilaku Burial Caverns. The cavern serves as a Sixth House shrine devoted to Dagoth Ur, marked by its ritual bell and ash statues.

title: Adanumuran
topic_desc: Adanumuran is a cave system situated against the hills along the northwestern shore of Lake Amaya, reachable via the road leading north from Pelagiad. Nestled at the boundary of the Ascadian Isles, its rocky interior provides natural shelter that historically attracts those dwelling outside mainstream settlement. Like many such caverns in the region, its remote yet accessible location makes it a practical lair for outlaws and displaced Dunmer. The surrounding hillside and lakeshore geography offer concealment while maintaining proximity to regional travel routes.
topic_desc_basic: Adanumuran is a cave located against the hills on the northwestern shore of Lake Amaya, north of Pelagiad. Its secluded yet accessible position in the Ascadian Isles region makes it a natural refuge for outlaws and bandits seeking shelter near traveled roads.

title: Addadshashanammu
topic_desc: Addadshashanammu is a Daedric ruin dedicated to Sheogorath, situated on an island northwest of Hlormaren along the Bitter Coast. The shrine's entrance faces northwest toward the sea. Built in the standard Daedric architectural style, the structure features the iconic stonework and menacing statuary typical of such sites. Like many isolated Daedric shrines scattered across the Morrowind wilderness, it serves as a persistent place of worship for the Madgod's followers, its remote island location offering seclusion for cultic rites away from Tribunal scrutiny.
topic_desc_basic: A Daedric shrine to Sheogorath located on an island northwest of Hlormaren on the Bitter Coast. The ruin's entrance faces the sea, and its remote island setting provides seclusion for the Madgod's worshippers.

title: Addamasartus
topic_desc: Addamasartus is a small coastal cave situated northeast of Seyda Neen along the Bitter Coast. Its architecture consists of natural cavern formations partially flooded by the sea, requiring underwater navigation to access certain chambers. The cave serves as a base for smugglers and slavers operating in the region, a persistent issue that local authorities in Seyda Neen have historically neglected. The site's proximity to the Imperial town makes it a notable landmark for travelers exploring the swampy coastline.
topic_desc_basic: Addamasartus is a small coastal cave northeast of Seyda Neen on the Bitter Coast. Partially flooded by the sea, it requires some underwater exploration to navigate fully. The cave is known as a haunt for smugglers and slavers operating in the area.

title: Aharnabi
topic_desc: Aharnabi is a small coastal cave situated just south of the Shrine of Azura, on the far southeastern tip of Vvardenfell's mainland. The cavern features a partially submerged interior, with flooded passages that host slaughterfish, and an entrance area noted for its fungal growths. Beyond the entry, the cave extends into a network of stairs and intersections, with deeper chambers containing alchemical apparatus, scholarly texts, and secured chests. Its remote location makes it a suitable refuge for those seeking to evade Imperial authority.
topic_desc_basic: Aharnabi is a small coastal cave located just south of the Shrine of Azura, on the far southeastern tip of Vvardenfell. Its partially submerged passages host slaughterfish, and its remote location provides a secluded refuge from Imperial authority.

title: Aharunartus
topic_desc: Aharunartus is a small coastal cave on a remote island west of the Bitter Coast peninsula, beyond Seyda Neen. The cavern serves as a secluded outpost for the Morrowind slave trade, offering slavers a hidden anchorage away from Imperial patrols. Its architecture is typical of natural Bitter Coast sea caves, adapted with crude holding pens and storage areas to confine captives and shelter illicit operations.
topic_desc_basic: A small sea cave on a remote island west of the Bitter Coast peninsula. The cavern serves as a secluded slaver outpost, providing a hidden anchorage for the region's illicit slave trade away from settled areas.

title: Ahinipalit
topic_desc: Ahinipalit is a coastal cavern on the peninsula northwest of Tel Fyr, carved into the rocky shoreline of the Azura's Coast region. The cave features a typical natural layout of subterranean chambers, with its southern reaches accessible only via elevated passages that require levitation or significant athletic ability to traverse. Such remote coastal caves frequently serve as refuges for outlaws and smugglers operating away from Imperial and Great House authority.
topic_desc_basic: Ahinipalit is a coastal cave on the peninsula northwest of Tel Fyr, along the Azura's Coast shoreline. Its natural chambers include elevated southern passages reachable only by levitation. Remote caves like this commonly shelter outlaws.

title: Ainat
topic_desc: Ainat is a small coastal cave on the eastern shore of the Morrowind mainland, situated directly west of the Holamayan Monastery and just north of Shashpilamat. Carved into the rugged Ascadian coastline, its modest chambers serve as a secluded hideout for outlaws. The cave's remote location and defensible interior make it a natural refuge for those seeking to avoid the reach of nearby monastic settlements and mainland authorities.
topic_desc_basic: A small cave on the eastern mainland coast, directly west of Holamayan Monastery and north of Shashpilamat. Its remote coastal setting provides a natural refuge for outlaws operating far from settled areas.

title: Akimaes Grotto
topic_desc: Akimaes Grotto is a small coastal cavern situated among the islands southeast of Seyda Neen, in the Azura's Coast region. The grotto's interior is partially submerged, with brackish pools and rocky passages shaped by tidal erosion. Kollop beds cling to the submerged ledges, and the cave's sheltered waters provide a typical habitat for the region's aquatic life. An abandoned rowboat rests near the entrance, suggesting the grotto has seen occasional use by foragers and pearl divers. The site holds no known historical or cultural significance beyond its natural geography.
topic_desc_basic: Akimaes Grotto is a small, partially submerged coastal cave located among the islands southeast of Seyda Neen. Tidal erosion has shaped its rocky passages and brackish pools. Kollop beds grow along the submerged ledges, making the grotto a natural feature of the Bitter Coast's shoreline environment.

title: Aleft
topic_desc: Aleft is a small Dwemer ruin situated southeast of Gnaar Mok and northwest of Hlormaren, notable as the only known Dwemer site within the Bitter Coast region. The complex is architecturally modest, comprising merely two interior chambers. Like other such sites, it retains active Dwemer Centurions, the autonomous constructs that typically populate these ancient strongholds. The ruin yields standard Dwemer artifacts and scrap metal rather than any unique relics, reflecting its limited scope compared to grander strongholds like Arkngthand. Its isolated Bitter Coast placement distinguishes it from the more concentrated Dwemer activity in the island's interior highlands.
topic_desc_basic: Aleft is a minor Dwemer ruin in the Bitter Coast region, lying southeast of Gnaar Mok and northwest of Hlormaren. It stands as the only Dwemer site in this coastal region. The structure consists of just two chambers containing standard Dwemer artifacts and the autonomous centurion constructs common to such ruins.

title: Almurbalarammi
topic_desc: Almurbalarammi is a Daedric shrine dedicated to Sheogorath, the Prince of Madness, situated near the center of the peninsula east of Molag Mar. The ruin follows the conventional layout of Morrowind's Daedric shrines, with a subterranean chamber housing a profane altar. The site reflects the enduring presence of Daedric worship in the region, where cultists gather to honor the Madgod despite the Tribunal Temple's condemnation of such practices. Its remote peninsular location places it among the scattered Daedric ruins of Azura's Coast, a region long associated with outsider faiths and the veneration of Daedric Princes outside mainstream Dunmer Temple doctrine.
topic_desc_basic: Almurbalarammi is a Daedric shrine to Sheogorath located on the peninsula east of Molag Mar. Like other Daedric ruins in Morrowind, it consists of a subterranean chamber with a profane altar. The site serves as a place of worship for followers of the Madgod, reflecting the persistence of Daedric cults in the remote coastal regions despite Tribunal Temple opposition.

title: An Abandoned Shack
topic_desc: An Abandoned Shack stands on the marshy Bitter Coast near Seyda Neen, a humble single-room structure of timber and thatch typical of the modest vernacular architecture found across the Imperial-occupied southwest coast of Vvardenfell. Such dwellings are often left vacant when fisherfolk or smugglers move on, the region's mists, swamps, and isolation making marginal habitation precarious. The shack reflects the scattered, impermanent settlement pattern of the coast.
topic_desc_basic: A derelict timber shack on the Bitter Coast near Seyda Neen. Such modest dwellings dot the foggy marshlands of southwestern Vvardenfell, often abandoned when their occupants move on. The region's wet climate and isolation make marginal coastal habitation precarious.

title: Ansi
topic_desc: Ansi is a natural cave system serving as a bandit hideout on the large island directly east of the Palace of Vivec, in the Azura's Coast region. The entrance sits just inland from the western shoreline at the island's southern tip, accessible over a low rise from the coast. The interior consists of interconnected chambers carved into the volcanic rock, with at least one elevated platform reachable only by levitation, climbing, or a circuitous rock formation. Such caves dot the islands surrounding Vivec City, providing concealed refuges for outlaws and smugglers who exploit the archipelago's rugged terrain and proximity to the city's wealth.
topic_desc_basic: Ansi is a bandit cave on the large island directly east of the Palace of Vivec. The entrance lies just above the western shoreline at the island's southern tip. The volcanic rock interior contains multiple chambers, including elevated platforms difficult to reach on foot. It is one of many such hideouts scattered across the Azura's Coast islands near Vivec City.

title: Arkngthunch-Sturdumz
topic_desc: Arkngthunch-Sturdumz is a Dwemer ruin on the northern coast of Vvardenfell, west of Ald Velothi and northwest of Gnisis. The site is carved into the hillside with a barrel-vaulted roof jutting from the southern slope. Its interior consists of three levels across four rooms connected by halls, built in the characteristic Dwemer style of fused stone and metalwork. Like other Dwemer sites across the island, it retains operational centurions and spectres guarding its chambers, along with scattered Dwemer artifacts and containers. The ruin exemplifies the dispersed network of Dwemer settlements that once dotted Vvardenfell before the race's disappearance.
topic_desc_basic: A Dwemer ruin on Vvardenfell's northern coast, reachable by following the shoreline west from Ald Velothi. It is one of several ancient Dwemer sites scattered across the island, built in the characteristic stone-and-metal style of that vanished civilization.
aliases: Dwemer ruin west of Ald Velothi

title: Ashalmimilkala
topic_desc: Ashalmimilkala is a ruined Daedric temple on a large offshore island along the western coast of Vvardenfell, situated in the Bitter Coast region. The island lies south of Gnaar Mok and west of the Imperial stronghold of Hlormaren, connected to the mainland by a thin strand of land and bridges. The site is dedicated to Mehrunes Dagon, Daedric Prince of Destruction and one of the Four Corners of the House of Troubles, whose veneration is proscribed among the Dunmer Temple faithful. The ruin retains the characteristic architecture of Daedric shrines, with dark stone construction and an altar precinct. Its remote island setting amid coastal swamps makes it one of the more isolated Daedric sites on Vvardenfell.
topic_desc_basic: Ashalmimilkala is a Daedric ruin on an island off the western coast of Vvardenfell in the Bitter Coast region. It lies south of Gnaar Mok and west of the stronghold of Hlormaren, reachable by bridges connecting the island to the mainland. The shrine is dedicated to Mehrunes Dagon of the House of Troubles.

title: Ashanammu
topic_desc: Ashanammu is a small cave situated just off the road outside the Caldera Mine in the West Gash region. The cavern features a modest interior layout that descends to a subterranean pool. Its proximity to Imperial mining operations makes it a notable landmark along the route, though its isolated chambers have historically attracted rogue Telvanni seeking seclusion. The architecture is typical of natural Vvardenfell caverns, with a staircase leading down to the water level.
topic_desc_basic: Ashanammu is a small cave located just off the road outside the Caldera Mine in the West Gash. The cavern descends to a subterranean pool and is known to occasionally shelter rogue Telvanni mages seeking seclusion near the Imperial mining route.

title: Ashir-Dan
topic_desc: Ashir-Dan is a coastal cave situated east of Khuul in the Ashlands region. Its modest chambers serve as a smugglers' hideout, historically utilized by criminal networks to cache contraband and illicit substances bound for or distributed from the remote northern coast. The cave's geography provides natural concealment for such operations, away from the scrutiny of major settlements and Imperial trade routes.
topic_desc_basic: Ashir-Dan is a small cave located east of Khuul. Its secluded coastal setting makes it a natural refuge for smugglers operating along the remote northern Ashlands coast.

title: Ashirbadon
topic_desc: Ashirbadon is a small coastal cave situated on the first island east of Bal Fell along Azura's Coast. Its initial passage opens into a broad cavern that appears to be a dead end at ground level. However, the cavern ceiling contains two elevated offshoots accessible only through levitation. One ascending niche holds an ancient chest, while the other leads deeper into the cave system. The site's architectural layout is entirely natural, defined by its vertical complexity and reliance on magical traversal to navigate its upper chambers.
topic_desc_basic: Ashirbadon is a small coastal cave on the first island east of Bal Fell along Azura's Coast. Its initial passage opens into a broad cavern with two elevated offshoots in the ceiling, reachable only through levitation, making the cave's deeper chambers inaccessible to those lacking magical means of flight.

title: Ashmelech
topic_desc: Ashmelech is an isolated catacomb complex situated on a small island in the Sheogorad archipelago, northwest of Vvardenfell's mainland. It lies between the main Sheogorad landmass—near the Velothi tower of Shara—and the coast near the ancient Chimer stronghold of Valenvaryon. The site serves as the seat of the Aundae Clan, one of the three vampire bloodlines of Vvardenfell, who favor its remote and defensible position. The catacombs are of old construction, consistent with Velothi-era tomb architecture, and their seclusion has long sheltered the clan from mortal intrusion and rival bloodlines alike. The Aundae bind their members to this refuge through magical recall, ensuring that even those scattered across the island can return swiftly to safety.
topic_desc_basic: This remote catacomb occupies a tiny island in the Sheogorad archipelago, between the main Sheogorad landmass and the Vvardenfell mainland. It serves as the stronghold of the Aundae Clan, one of three vampire bloodlines native to Vvardenfell, prized for its isolation and natural defensibility.

title: Ashunartes
topic_desc: Ashunartes is a small Daedric shrine dedicated to Malacath, situated west of Marandus near the shores of Lake Nabia in the Molag Amur region. The site features typical Daedric architecture and is constructed with two distinct entryways: a main entrance and a secondary, concealed passage leading directly to the upper level. As a shrine to Malacath, it naturally attracts Orcish adherents drawn to the Daedric Prince's pariah patronage. The surrounding landscape is marked by the rugged, volcanic terrain characteristic of the region, and the shrine's proximity to Lake Nabia provides a notable landmark for travelers navigating the hostile interior of Morrowind.
topic_desc_basic: Ashunartes is a small Daedric shrine dedicated to Malacath, located west of Marandus near the shores of Lake Nabia. Built in the standard Daedric style, the structure features both a main entrance and a hidden upper-level passage. The shrine serves as a gathering place for Orcish worshippers of Malacath.

title: Assalkushalit
topic_desc: Assalkushalit, also called Kushalit Sanctuary, is a Daedric ruin housing a shrine to Sheogorath. It sits on the northern slopes of Red Mountain within the Ghostfence, southeast of Maar Gan. The complex features a statue of the Mad God and numerous portal connections between its chambers. Following its Second Era abandonment, the Ghostfence's construction isolated the site deep within the blighted quarantine zone, cutting it off from the surrounding Ashlands.
topic_desc_basic: Assalkushalit is a Daedric ruin and Sheogorath shrine on Red Mountain's northern slopes, southeast of Maar Gan. It lies within the Ghostfence, isolated from the surrounding Ashlands by the blight quarantine.

title: Assarnatamat
topic_desc: Assarnatamat is a Daedric shrine dedicated to Mehrunes Dagon, situated along the Foyada Mamaea southeast of Caldera and northeast of Balmora, just within the Ashlands region. The structure exemplifies the stark, angular architecture typical of Daedric ruins, serving as an enduring monument to the Prince of Destruction. Daedra maintain a persistent presence at the site, and the altar bears a cursed piece of raw ebony, reflecting the inherent danger of such profane places of worship.
topic_desc_basic: Assarnatamat is a Daedric shrine to Mehrunes Dagon located on the Foyada Mamaea southeast of Caldera, just inside the Ashlands region. Daedra are commonly present at this remote site, and its altar holds a cursed piece of raw ebony.

title: Assarnud
topic_desc: Assarnud is a cave complex situated east of Gnisis, near the waters of the local lake. Its strategic significance lies in its dual entrances: one opens onto the lakeside, while the second lies just beyond Fort Darius's eastern arch, providing discreet access. The interior features flooded chambers with submerged pools, diamond deposits, and kollop beds. The cave's architecture is notably partitioned, containing secured slave pens protected by traps and reinforced locks, reflecting its established use as a holding site by regional slavers operating near the Imperial garrison.
topic_desc_basic: Assarnud is a cave located east of Gnisis, near a lakeshore. It features two entrances—one on the lake and another close to Fort Darius. The interior contains flooded chambers with underwater pools and is known as a slaver holding site with secured, trap-guarded slave pens.

title: Assu
topic_desc: Assu is a small cavern situated in the rugged Molag Amur region, near the slopes of Mount Kand. The cave's interior features distinct chambers connected by watery passages, some requiring magical levitation to navigate fully. Culturally, Assu serves as a secluded refuge for sorcerers who maintain daedric guardians within its depths. The cavern holds notable historical significance as the provenance of the Staff of Magnus, a renowned artifact of considerable arcane power that has attracted the attention of the Mages Guild.
topic_desc_basic: Assu is a small cave near Mount Kand in the Molag Amur region. The cavern serves as a secluded refuge for sorcerers and their daedric guardians. It is historically significant as the provenance of the Staff of Magnus, a renowned arcane artifact.

title: Assumanu
topic_desc: Assumanu is a cavern complex situated on the northern coast of Vvardenfell, southeast of Ald Redaynia and northeast of the Urshilaku Camp. Carved into the region's rugged volcanic terrain, the cave features distinct interior chambers connected by natural rock bridges and pillars. The site serves as a secluded retreat for rogue House Telvanni mages and their retainers, who favor such remote, defensible locations to pursue their studies and schemes beyond the scrutiny of Great House authorities. Its isolated Ashlands position makes it a notable landmark for travelers navigating the harsh northern coastline.
topic_desc_basic: Assumanu is a cave on the northern coast of Vvardenfell, southeast of Ald Redaynia and northeast of the Urshilaku Camp. Its remote and defensible interior provides a secluded refuge for rogue House Telvanni mages and their retainers, characteristic of the isolated dwellings favored by the sorcerous house.

title: Bensamsi
topic_desc: Bensamsi is a cavern system situated in the northern Ashlands, northeast of Kogoruhn. Carved into the region's rugged volcanic terrain, the cave's dark chambers and winding passages have been repurposed as a Sixth House shrine. The architecture reflects the cult's distinctive biomorphic and corprus-stained modifications, transforming the natural stone into a ritual space dedicated to Dagoth Ur. The site's remote Ashlands location provides isolation for the Sixth House's secretive ceremonies and gatherings.
topic_desc_basic: Bensamsi is a cave in the northern Ashlands, northeast of Kogoruhn. Its natural volcanic chambers serve as a Sixth House shrine, featuring the cult's distinctive corprus-stained architecture and ritual spaces.

title: Beshara
topic_desc: Beshara is a natural cave system situated east of the Telvanni Canton of Vivec, along the rocky shores of Azura's Coast. The cavern consists of a main tunnel network branching into several chambers, including a deep western pool. An underwater passage tunnels beneath the primary hallways, connecting portions of the cave. The site's defensible interior and relative isolation from nearby settlements make it a typical refuge for bandit groups operating along the southeastern coast of Vvardenfell.
topic_desc_basic: Beshara is a cave east of Vivec's Telvanni Canton on the Azura's Coast region of Vvardenfell. Its natural tunnels branch into several chambers, including a deep western pool and an underwater passage. The cave's isolated, defensible interior makes it a common refuge for bandits along the southeastern coast.

title: Bthanchend
topic_desc: Bthanchend is a Dwemer ruin situated just within the Ghostfence near the Maar Gan region. Unlike other Dwemer sites enclosed by the barrier, it is not associated with the Sixth House. The site is relatively small, comprising four chambers across three levels. Several caved-in passageways indicate that the complex was once significantly larger before structural collapse. Bthanchend retains active Dwemer constructs and typical Deep Elf engineering remnants, serving as a hazardous but notable landmark for travelers navigating the blighted perimeter of the Ghostfence.
topic_desc_basic: Bthanchend is a small Dwemer ruin located just inside the Ghostfence near Maar Gan. Unlike other Dwemer sites within the barrier, it has no Sixth House presence. Collapsed passageways suggest the complex was once larger, though only four chambers across three levels remain accessible today.

title: Bthuand
topic_desc: Bthuand is a Dwemer ruin situated in the north-central Ashlands of Vvardenfell, lying west of the Daedric shrine Zergonipal. Like other Dwemer strongholds, it was abruptly abandoned in 1E 700 following the disappearance of the Deep Folk. The site retains typical Dwemer architectural and mechanical features; Dwarven Centurions still function within its halls, and the ghosts of ancient Dwemer are occasionally encountered. The ruin's interior has suffered structural collapses over the centuries, sealing off some passages and trapping past explorers beneath rubble. Bthuand is historically noted as a place where significant Dwemer artifacts have been lost, including the renowned Daedric shield Spellbreaker, which rests beside the remains of a previous owner killed by a cave-in.
topic_desc_basic: Bthuand is an ancient Dwemer ruin in the north-central Ashlands of Vvardenfell, west of the Zergonipal Daedric shrine. Abandoned in 1E 700 during the Dwemer disappearance, the site still contains functioning Dwarven Centurions and occasional Dwemer ghosts. The ruin has suffered cave-ins over the centuries, trapping previous explorers.

title: Bthungthumz
topic_desc: Bthungthumz, also known as Ald Carac, is a Dwemer ruin in the northwestern Ashlands of Vvardenfell, situated near the Urshilaku Camp and the vampire stronghold of Druscashti. Constructed as a fortified village during the War of the First Council in the early First Era, its halls feature standard Dwemer architectural and engineering designs. In the Second Era, the site briefly served as a bloodsport arena for the Circle of Champions. Local legends associate the ruin with the specter of Dahrk Mezalf, a smith said to have served under Kagrenac.
topic_desc_basic: Bthungthumz, also called Ald Carac, is a Dwemer ruin in northwestern Vvardenfell near the Urshilaku Camp. Built as a fortified village during the War of the First Council in the early First Era, it features typical Dwemer architecture and is locally associated with the specter of Dahrk Mezalf, a smith of Kagrenac.

title: Corprusarium Bowels
topic_desc: The deepest subterranean chambers beneath Divayth Fyr's tower at Tel Fyr, serving as the containment ward for the Corprusarium's most severely afflicted corprus victims. Carved into the volcanic rock of Azura's Coast, these lightless, cavernous bowels reflect the Telvanni wizard's approach to studying the divine disease: isolated, secure, and largely forgotten by the outside world. The architecture is purely functional, consisting of rough-hewn passages and chambers designed to house those warped by corprus indefinitely, far from the upper levels where the less monstrous cases reside.
topic_desc_basic: The deepest chambers beneath Tel Fyr's Corprusarium. These dark, subterranean passages serve as the containment area for the most severely deformed victims of corprus disease, kept isolated within Divayth Fyr's remote infirmary complex.

title: Dun-Ahhe
topic_desc: Dun-Ahhe is a medium-sized cavern situated in the northeastern Ashlands, directly over the hills north of the Cavern of the Incarnate. The interior features multiple ledges, sheer drops, and waterways, making levitation the most practical means of traversing its depths. Raw diamond ore deposits line the walls, and slaughterfish inhabit the subterranean pools. The cavern's remote and defensible character has historically attracted renegade mages and summoned Daedra, who claim such isolated sites for their studies.
topic_desc_basic: Dun-Ahhe is a medium-sized cavern in the northeastern Ashlands, just north of the Cavern of the Incarnate. Its interior features deep waterways, sheer drops, and diamond ore deposits, with levitation often required to traverse its uneven passages.

title: Dushariran
topic_desc: Dushariran is a Daedric shrine dedicated to Malacath, situated along the West Gash road east of the Berandas stronghold. The site features a long interior corridor and staircase leading to an underground altar chamber, a typical architectural layout for such remote sanctuaries. As a recognized place of Malacath worship, the shrine reflects the Orcish association with the Daedric Prince, serving as a spiritual waypoint in the rugged West Gash region.
topic_desc_basic: Dushariran is a Daedric shrine to Malacath located on the West Gash road east of Berandas. The site consists of a long interior corridor and staircase leading to an underground altar chamber, serving as a remote sanctuary for the Daedric Prince's followers.

title: Ebernanit
topic_desc: Ebernanit is a Daedric shrine dedicated to Mehrunes Dagon, situated in the Ashlands southeast of the Dunmer stronghold of Valenvaryon. Like many such remote sites, it consists of a typical subterranean chamber featuring the Prince's altar, reflecting the forbidden veneration of a destructive Daedric power in the harsh volcanic wasteland. These isolated shrines historically serve as destinations for committed cultists seeking communion with their patron, far from settled areas.
topic_desc_basic: Ebernanit is a shrine to Mehrunes Dagon located in the Ashlands, southeast of Valenvaryon. It is a remote Daedric site where cultists venerate the Prince of Destruction.

title: Eluba-Addon Grotto
topic_desc: Eluba-Addon Grotto is a submerged coastal cavern situated in the waters just offshore from the Ahemmusa Camp in the Azura's Coast region. The cave system consists of typical volcanic rock formations shaped by the sea, providing a habitat for kollop colonies and various marine life. Its name reflects the Ahemmusa Ashlander naming tradition, though the grotto holds no known cultural or historical significance for the tribe. The sheltered underwater passages offer little beyond the natural pearls harvestable from the resident kollops.
topic_desc_basic: Eluba-Addon Grotto is a small underwater cave located just offshore from the Ahemmusa Camp along Azura's Coast. The submerged cavern hosts kollop colonies and common sea creatures, offering little else of note to passing travelers.

title: Endusal
topic_desc: Endusal, traditionally known as Kagrenac's Study, is a Dwemer citadel situated within the Ghostfence in the Red Mountain region. It served as the workshop and study of the Dwemer Tonal Architect Kagrenac during the construction of the Numidium. The facility retains its ancient Dwemer architectural character, housing the architect's original journal among its ruins. Like the other citadels of Red Mountain, it has become a site of corrupting blight and malevolent influence, deeply tied to the mythopoeic forces that shaped the Dwemer disappearance and the mountain's current dangers.
topic_desc_basic: Endusal, known as Kagrenac's Study, is a Dwemer citadel within the Ghostfence in the Red Mountain region. It historically served as the workshop of the Dwemer Tonal Architect Kagrenac and still contains his journal among its ancient ruins.

title: Esutanamus
topic_desc: Esutanamus is a Daedric shrine dedicated to Molag Bal, situated south of Tel Mora along Vvardenfell's northeastern coast. The ruin follows the conventional plan of remote Daedric cult sites: a small antechamber gives way to a central shrine chamber where offerings are placed upon the altar. As a site venerating the Lord of Domination, Esutanamus reflects the enduring presence of Daedric worship on Vvardenfell, maintained far from the administrative reach of the Tribunal Temple and Imperial governance. Its isolated coastal placement underscores the clandestine nature of such devotion, typical of shrines erected to the Four Corners of the House of Troubles.
topic_desc_basic: Esutanamus is a Daedric shrine to Molag Bal located south of Tel Mora on Vvardenfell's northeastern coast. The ruin consists of an antechamber leading to a central altar chamber. Like other remote Daedric sites, it serves as a place of worship beyond the reach of Tribunal Temple authority.

title: Forgotten Vaults of Anudnabia
topic_desc: The Forgotten Vaults of Anudnabia are ancient Dwemer ruins situated in the remote Azura's Coast region. The complex incorporates the Forge of Hilbongard, a renowned smithy reflecting the Dwemer mastery of metalwork. Built from monumental stone and brass architecture, the vaults descend into cavernous halls and submerged passages typical of Dwemer construction. Their isolation and structural decay have left them largely unexplored, preserving the architectural and mechanical legacy of the vanished Deep Folk.
topic_desc_basic: The Forgotten Vaults of Anudnabia are remote Dwemer ruins in Azura's Coast. The complex includes the Forge of Hilbongard, an ancient smithy. Built of monumental stone and brass, the deteriorated halls reflect the vanished Deep Folk's architectural and metallurgical legacy.
aliases: Forgotten Vaults of Anudnabia, Forge of Hilbongard

title: Habinbaes
topic_desc: Habinbaes is a small sea cave situated on the northern edge of the island of Sheogorad, west of Dagon Fel and across a narrow river channel near the Azura's Arch coastline. Its secluded position makes it a favored refuge for smugglers operating in the remote island archipelago, far from Imperial authority. The cavern interior provides shelter and hidden storage for contraband routed through the Sheogorad region.
topic_desc_basic: Habinbaes is a small sea cave on the northern coast of Sheogorad, west of Dagon Fel and across a river. Its isolated location makes it a natural refuge for smugglers operating far from Imperial patrols.

title: Hinnabi
topic_desc: Hinnabi is a coastal cave situated on the island north-northwest of Bal Fell, east of Vivec. Serving as a slaver hideout, it provides a secluded base for the region's illicit trade. The interior consists of typical rocky cavern chambers adapted for holding captives and storing contraband. Its remote island location offers natural concealment from mainland authorities, making it a strategic outpost for those operating outside Imperial law in the Azura's Coast region.
topic_desc_basic: Hinnabi is a cave on an island north-northwest of Bal Fell, east of Vivec. It serves as a remote slaver hideout, its rocky chambers providing a secluded base for the region's illicit trade away from mainland authorities.

title: Ibar-Dad
topic_desc: Ibar-Dad is a small cave situated west of the Assurnabitashpi Daedric shrine in the Ashlands region, not far from the Urshilaku Camp. The cavern serves as an excavation site for Daedra-worshipping sorcerers exploring a submerged Velothi tomb. Submerged passages lead to the burial chamber of Mordrin Hanin, an ancient figure of Dark Elven history. Powerful Daedra inhabit the deeper reaches, reflecting the site's significance as both a revered tomb and a place of Daedric veneration.
topic_desc_basic: Ibar-Dad is a small cave west of the Assurnabitashpi shrine near the Urshilaku Camp. Daedra-worshipping sorcerers excavate the site, which contains submerged passages leading to the ancient Tomb of Mordrin Hanin. Powerful Daedra occupy the deeper reaches.

title: Ibishammus
topic_desc: Ibishammus is a Daedric shrine dedicated to Malacath, situated in the subterranean waterways beneath Vivec City's Foreign Quarter. This secluded sanctuary reflects the typical architectural austerity of such cult sites, centered around a venerated altar. The shrine serves as a place of worship for Malacath's followers, who maintain the hidden sanctum within the sprawling canton underworks. Its location in the sewers underscores the marginalized status of Malacath veneration in urban Morrowind, requiring devotees to practice their faith far from the city's prominent Tribunal temples.
topic_desc_basic: Ibishammus is a hidden shrine to Malacath located in the sewers beneath Vivec's Foreign Quarter. This secluded sanctuary serves as a place of worship for the Daedric Prince's followers, who maintain the site within the canton's subterranean waterways away from the city's mainstream Tribunal temples.

title: Ilanipu Grotto
topic_desc: Ilanipu Grotto is a partially submerged coastal cave situated off an island south of Rotheran and Dagon Fel in the Sheogorad region. The grotto transitions from a flooded sea entrance into dry subterranean chambers. Like many such caverns in the remote archipelago, it provides shelter for local fauna and the occasional ill-fated traveler drawn to the rugged island coastlines.
topic_desc_basic: Ilanipu Grotto is a partially flooded coastal cave located off an island south of Rotheran and Dagon Fel in the Sheogorad region. Its sea entrance transitions into dry underground chambers typical of the remote archipelago's rugged coastline.

title: Imperial Prison Ship
topic_desc: An Imperial transport vessel employed to convey prisoners and deportees to Vvardenfell. The ship features a secure lower hold designed for confinement during long voyages across the Inner Sea. Upon reaching its destination, it anchors at the Seyda Neen docks, where the Census and Excise Office processes arrivals. Such vessels represent the logistical reach of Imperial law, enabling the relocation of convicts and outlanders to Morrowind's administrative centers.
topic_desc_basic: An Imperial transport vessel used to convey prisoners and deportees to Vvardenfell. The ship features a secure lower hold for confinement during voyages. It anchors at the Seyda Neen docks, where arrivals are processed by the Census and Excise Office.

title: Kaushtarari
topic_desc: Kaushtarari is a small Daedric shrine dedicated to Malacath, situated on an isolated island in the Azura's Coast region, south-southeast of Sadrith Mora and east of the Erabenimsun Camp. The site reflects the typical remote placement of Malacath's cult centers, far from major settlements. Orcish adherents maintain the shrine, guarding both its exterior approaches and interior sanctum. The architecture conforms to the standard Daedric style found across similar remote shrines in Morrowind, serving as a place of veneration for the Daedric Prince of the Spurned and Ostracized.
topic_desc_basic: Kaushtarari is a small shrine to Malacath located on an island south-southeast of Sadrith Mora and east of the Erabenimsun Camp. The remote site is maintained by Orcish adherents who guard the shrine's exterior and interior, serving as a place of worship for the Daedric Prince of the Spurned and Ostracized.

title: Kora-Dur
topic_desc: Kora-Dur is a cavern system situated in the northern Ashlands, just east of the Sixth House stronghold Kogoruhn. The cave serves as a lair for powerful Daedra, predominantly daedroths accompanied by storm atronachs. It is notably the refuge of the unique daedroth Menta Na. According to Molag Bal's own doctrine, the Daedric Prince harbors a longstanding grudge against Menta Na, a dispute known to those who visit the shrine of Yansirramus on the western edge of Zafirbel Bay. The site's concentration of formidable Daedra makes it a hazardous landmark in the rugged ashland terrain.
topic_desc_basic: Kora-Dur is a cave in the northern Ashlands, located east of Kogoruhn. It serves as a lair for powerful Daedra, primarily daedroths and storm atronachs. The cavern is known as the refuge of the unique daedroth Menta Na, who is despised by his master, the Daedric Prince Molag Bal.

title: Kudanat
topic_desc: Kudanat is a cavern hideout situated west of Caldera, beyond the Caldera Mine entrance. The cave serves as a base for slavers and bandits, reflecting the persistent illegal trade in the region. Its interior contains a small pool and typical encampment features. The presence of captive labor and illicit goods such as skooma underscores its role as a refuge for those operating outside Imperial law. The site exemplifies the remote caverns exploited throughout the West Gash by criminal elements.
topic_desc_basic: Kudanat is a cavern west of Caldera, past the Caldera Mine. The cave functions as a slaver and bandit hideout, a common type of remote refuge in the West Gash region exploited by those operating outside Imperial law.

title: Kumarahaz
topic_desc: Kumarahaz is a sizeable natural cave formation situated on the mainland northeast of Tel Branora and slightly east of the Abebaal Egg Mine. The cavern features an extensive network of passages, including concealed tunnels. Its remote Azura's Coast location makes it a natural refuge for outlaws and smugglers operating beyond the reach of House Telvanni authority.
topic_desc_basic: Kumarahaz is a large cave on the mainland northeast of Tel Branora, just east of the Abebaal Egg Mine. Its remote Azura's Coast location and hidden tunnels make it a natural refuge for outlaws.

title: Kunirai
topic_desc: Kunirai is a cave situated in the Molag Amur region, north of Telasero and east-northeast of Suran. Carved into the rugged volcanic hills, its interior features multiple chambers connected by natural passages, including areas with wooden platforms and a forge. The cave's defensible layout and isolated location make it a suitable hideout for those wishing to avoid the main roads. The surrounding terrain is characteristic of Molag Amur: harsh, rocky, and sparsely vegetated, offering natural concealment from the nearby Dunmer strongholds and Imperial settlements.
topic_desc_basic: Kunirai is a cave in the Molag Amur region, located north of Telasero and east-northeast of Suran. Its isolated position within the rugged volcanic landscape makes it a natural refuge away from the main travel routes.

title: Kushtashpi
topic_desc: Kushtashpi is a Daedric shrine dedicated to Molag Bal, situated in the hilly terrain of the Grazelands west of the Ahemmusa Camp. The entrance sits atop a stone plateau, leading into a subterranean passage complicated by a broken bridge over a chasm. Beyond this obstacle lies the shrine chamber, which is partially submerged. The site exemplifies the remote and hazardous Molag Bal cult sanctuaries scattered across Morrowind, blending natural cave formations with Daedric architectural elements and an altar area.
topic_desc_basic: Kushtashpi is a Daedric shrine to Molag Bal located in the Grazelands, west of the Ahemmusa Camp. Built atop a stone plateau, the subterranean sanctuary features a partially submerged shrine chamber accessed via a cave passage with a broken bridge.

title: Maba-Ilu
topic_desc: Maba-Ilu is a small, secluded cave situated on the southern shore of the peninsula east of Molag Mar, within the Azura's Coast region. Known as a refuge for rogue sorcerers, its isolated geography makes it a suitable lair for reclusive necromancers and their Daedric servants. The cave's natural formations yield rare raw ebony, glass, and diamonds, alongside scattered magical paraphernalia, potions, and scrolls. A copy of Feyfolgen III, a treatise on Conjuration, is among the notable texts left within. The site exemplifies the remote, perilous dens that dot the rugged Azura's Coast, where practitioners of forbidden arts seek solitude away from Tribunal and Imperial oversight.
topic_desc_basic: Maba-Ilu is a small, isolated cave on the southern shore of the peninsula east of Molag Mar in the Azura's Coast region. It serves as a remote refuge for rogue sorcerers and necromancers. The cave contains rare natural deposits of raw ebony, glass, and diamonds, along with scattered magical supplies and scrolls.

title: Mababi
topic_desc: Mababi is a Velothi tower situated within the harsh wastelands of the Molag Amur region. Originally constructed as a traditional Dunmer stronghold, the site has since been claimed by House Telvanni, who adapted the architecture to suit their distinctive wizardly needs. The remote and inhospitable surrounding terrain provides natural isolation, a quality valued by the Telvanni mage-lords. The interior houses a modest collection of potions and scholarly texts, reflecting its current function as a secluded magical retreat rather than a grand seat of power.
topic_desc_basic: Mababi is a Velothi tower in the Molag Amur wastelands. Claimed by House Telvanni, the remote stronghold serves as a secluded retreat for the wizard-lords, its harsh surroundings providing natural isolation.

title: Madas Grotto
topic_desc: Madas Grotto is a submerged sea cave along Vvardenfell's rocky north coast, northeast of the Urshilaku Camp. Its entrance sits just below the waterline, opening into a largely flooded interior. The grotto is a natural formation with no architectural development, serving as habitat for aquatic fauna such as slaughterfish, dreugh, and kollops. The submerged chambers offer little shelter for surface dwellers, making the site primarily a navigational hazard for coastal travelers rather than a habitation.
topic_desc_basic: Madas Grotto is a largely submerged sea cave along Vvardenfell's north coast, northeast of the Urshilaku Camp. Its entrance lies just below the waterline, and the flooded interior hosts aquatic life. The site offers little shelter and remains primarily a navigational feature for coastal travelers.

title: Magas Volar
topic_desc: Magas Volar is a Daedric shrine wholly disconnected from the mainland of Morrowind, reachable only through magical transport rather than overland travel. The site consists of a compact Daedric ruin of standard Oblivion-derived architecture, featuring carved stone and the angular construction typical of Daedric sanctuaries. No physical road, waterway, or cavern passage connects it to any settlement or region. Access is achieved solely by equipping a Daedric Sanctuary Amulet, which instantly conveys the wearer to the shrine's interior. The shrine is culturally significant as an isolated pocket of Daedric presence, housing a powerful Dremora guardian armed with the Daedric Crescent, a rare and storied artifact weapon of Daedric manufacture. Its seclusion and the magical means of entry mark it as an exceptional site, distinct from the more accessible Daedric ruins scattered across the Vvardenfell landscape.
topic_desc_basic: Magas Volar is an isolated Daedric shrine with no physical connection to any location in Morrowind. It is reachable only through magical transport via a Daedric Sanctuary Amulet. The shrine features standard Daedric architecture and houses a powerful Dremora guardian. Its complete seclusion from overland routes distinguishes it from other Daedric ruins across Vvardenfell.

title: Mallapi
topic_desc: Mallapi is a cave situated a short distance northeast of the fishing village of Gnaar Mok along the Bitter Coast. Its interior architecture suggests a former Dunmer habitation or shrine, now abandoned to the region's encroaching wilderness. The site is known to attract conjurers and their summoned Daedric guardians, indicating lingering esoteric or cultic significance. Its relative isolation within the coastal swamplands makes it a noted landmark for travelers navigating the roadless terrain between Gnaar Mok and the broader Azura's Coast region.
topic_desc_basic: Mallapi is a cave located northeast of Gnaar Mok on the Bitter Coast. The site is known to harbor conjurers and Daedric entities, suggesting a history of esoteric practice. It serves as a landmark for travelers in the surrounding wilderness.

title: Malmus Grotto
topic_desc: Malmus Grotto is a coastal cavern situated on a small island in the Sheogorad region, northwest of Dagon Fel. Unlike many flooded sea caves in the archipelago, its interior remains largely dry. A natural land bridge spans an interior channel, connecting the main chamber to a secluded alcove. The grotto supports a modest population of kollop beds along its damp margins. The isolated alcove holds the remains of a long-dead figure impaled by an iron claymore, a grim testament to some forgotten violence in the region's distant past.
topic_desc_basic: Malmus Grotto is a largely dry coastal cave on a small island in the Sheogorad region, northwest of Dagon Fel. A natural land bridge connects the main chamber to a separate alcove. Kollop beds line the damp interior margins.

title: Mannammu
topic_desc: Mannammu is a sizable cave complex carved into the hills along the southwestern shore of Lake Hairan, just south of the village of Pelagiad and accessible via stepping stones across the lake's narrows. The interior is extensive and vertically varied, with rope bridges and ladders spanning deep chambers and a submerged passage connecting separate sections. Its proximity to Pelagiad and the well-traveled roads between Balmora and the Ascadian Isles has long made such caves attractive to smugglers and bandits seeking refuge near settled areas. The natural formation creates a multi-level den with both dry and flooded passages.
topic_desc_basic: Mannammu is a large cave complex on the southwestern shore of Lake Hairan, just south of Pelagiad. Reached by stepping stones across the lake, the cave features rope bridges, ladders, and an underwater passage through its multi-level chambers. Its location near Pelagiad's trade routes has long attracted smuggler activity.

title: Maran-Adon
topic_desc: Maran-Adon is a cave situated in the northeastern Ashlands, directly south of the Cavern of the Incarnate and west of the Nchuleft Dwemer ruin. Its remote and difficult-to-reach location makes it a natural redoubt for the Sixth House, serving as a shrine and haven for Dreamers and ash creatures. The cavern's architecture reflects its cultic purpose, dominated by a Sixth House bell and its accompanying hammer rather than any substantial material wealth. The site's proximity to the sacred Cavern of the Incarnate underscores the deep ideological conflict between the Tribunal and the Sixth House in this desolate region.
topic_desc_basic: Maran-Adon is a remote cave in the northeastern Ashlands, located south of the Cavern of the Incarnate and west of Nchuleft. It serves as a Sixth House shrine and refuge for ash creatures and Dreamers, distinguished by its cultic bell rather than material wealth.

title: Masseranit
topic_desc: Masseranit is a coastal cave situated on the first large island southwest of Molag Mar. Its entrance faces southeast along the eastern shoreline. The cavern serves as a smuggler's den, characterized by an extensive accumulation of storage crates and barrels that fill much of its modest chambers. The site's substantial contraband stores include skooma, moon sugar, ash statues, and soul gems, alongside assorted smuggled goods, potions, and weaponry. A copy of the Destruction text The Horror of Castle Xyr rests within its southeast room. The den's remote island placement provides a secluded staging ground for illicit trade operating in the waters between the mainland and the Azura's Coast archipelago.
topic_desc_basic: Masseranit is a coastal cave on the first large island southwest of Molag Mar, with its entrance facing southeast along the eastern shore. The cavern functions as a smuggler's den, densely packed with crates and barrels holding substantial contraband, including skooma, moon sugar, and ash statues. Its remote island location offers a secluded refuge for illicit regional trade.

title: Mat
topic_desc: Mat is a small natural cave situated in the hills just north of the village of Gnisis in northwestern Vvardenfell. The terrain surrounding Gnisis is rugged, with rocky slopes rising from the West Gash region toward the Ashlands, and Mat occupies one of these elevated pockets. The cave itself is unremarkable in scale and shows no evidence of permanent habitation or structured architecture. Like many such caverns scattered across the Vvardenfell frontier, it serves primarily as a sheltered hollow in an otherwise exposed landscape, occasionally drawing those who wish to avoid the roads and settlements of the region.
topic_desc_basic: Mat is a small cave in the hills north of Gnisis, in northwestern Vvardenfell. It is an unremarkable natural cavern with no notable architecture or permanent settlement, typical of the many scattered shelters found throughout the rugged terrain surrounding the West Gash region.

title: Mawia
topic_desc: Mawia is a Velothi tower standing on a small island just off the coast southeast of Molag Mar. The structure exemplifies traditional Dunmer Velothi architecture, with a domed upper chamber reached by interior stairways ascending through several levels. Its island setting isolates it from the mainland, reachable only by water or magical transport. Velothi towers of this type are scattered across Vvardenfell, often serving as private retreats or dwellings removed from major settlements. Mawia's proximity to Molag Mar places it within the rugged southeastern coastal region, where the terrain descends from the slopes of Mount Kand toward the Padomaic waters. The tower's remote location and enduring construction reflect the dispersed pattern of Velothi settlement throughout the island.
topic_desc_basic: Mawia is a Velothi tower on a small island off the southeastern coast near Molag Mar. Built in the traditional Dunmer style with a domed upper chamber and interior stairs spanning multiple levels, it stands isolated from mainland settlements, accessible only by water. Like many Velothi towers across Vvardenfell, it occupies a remote coastal site far from major population centers.

title: Mila-Nipal
topic_desc: Mila-Nipal is an Ashlander yurt situated at the foothills of the Ashlands, northeast of the Daedric shrine Dushariran and east of Salothan Ancestral Tomb. A Dwemer ruin, Bthanchend, lies to its east. The site consists of a single traditional felt tent, characteristic of nomadic Ashlander encampments, positioned where the Ashlands meet the surrounding terrain. Mila-Nipal serves as a modest outpost in this sparsely inhabited region, reflecting the scattered and mobile settlement patterns of the Ashlander clans.
topic_desc_basic: Mila-Nipal is an Ashlander yurt located at the foothills of the Ashlands, northeast of Dushariran and east of Salothan Ancestral Tomb. The traditional felt tent reflects the nomadic lifestyle of the region's Ashlander clans.

title: Milk
topic_desc: Milk is a cave situated west of Ald'ruhn's northern reaches and south of Bal Isra, along the road toward Maar Gan. The cavern has gained regional notoriety as the stronghold of a fallen Redoran noble whose descent into madness transformed the location into a bandit den. From this cave, the rogue lord and his retainers demand tribute from travelers passing through the Ashlands corridor. The site's infamy has earned it the colloquial epithet linking its name to its mad inhabitant, marking it as a hazard for caravans and pilgrims navigating the routes north of Ald'ruhn.
topic_desc_basic: Milk is a cave located west of Ald'ruhn and south of Bal Isra, along the road toward Maar Gan. The cavern serves as the stronghold of a mad former Redoran noble and his retainers, who demand tribute from travelers passing through the Ashlands.

title: Missamsi
topic_desc: Missamsi is a Sixth House cave complex situated in the rugged terrain northeast of Moonmoth Legion Fort, along the mountainous route toward Assarnatamat. The cavern's dark passages feature lava channels and contain a corrupted shrine typical of Dagoth Ur's influence. Ash creatures and corprus horrors infest the tunnels, marking the site as a significant localized base for the Sixth House cult. The southwestern chambers harbor a crude shrine area with metal troughs holding ritual offerings and discarded equipment, reflecting the cult's degenerate practices in the region.
topic_desc_basic: Missamsi is a cave in the hills northeast of Moonmoth Legion Fort. It serves as a Sixth House base, its tunnels corrupted by lava flows and a foul shrine. Ash creatures wander the passages, making the site dangerous for travelers traversing the area between the fort and Assarnatamat.

title: Mudan Grotto
topic_desc: Mudan Grotto is a submerged Dwemer site located in the waters southwest of Ebonheart. The complex consists of four distinct areas: the surface grotto, the Lost Dwemer Checkpoint, the Right Tower, and the Central Vault. As an underwater ruin, it reflects the typical Dwemer architectural propensity for subterranean construction, now entirely flooded and hidden beneath the sea. The presence of a designated checkpoint and central vault suggests the site originally served a guarded logistical or storage function within the broader Dwemer infrastructure of the region, though its exact historical purpose remains uncertain.
topic_desc_basic: Mudan Grotto is a flooded Dwemer ruin hidden underwater southwest of Ebonheart. The complex comprises four areas: the Grotto, the Lost Dwemer Checkpoint, the Right Tower, and the Central Vault. Its original purpose remains unclear.

title: Mul Grotto
topic_desc: Mul Grotto is a small, submerged coastal cave situated on the first large island southwest of Molag Mar, east of Mzahnch. Its entrance lies underwater among the rocks on the island's western shore. Inside, the grotto consists of flooded tunnels leading to a southeast chamber centered around a large rock spire rising from the water. The cavern provides a habitat for aquatic life and kollops. A submerged rock shelf jutting from the central spire holds the remains of a skeleton, suggesting the grotto occasionally shelters those traversing the Azura's Coast waterways, though its hidden, flooded nature makes it an easily overlooked landmark.
topic_desc_basic: Mul Grotto is a small, flooded cave on an island southwest of Molag Mar along the Azura's Coast. Its underwater entrance is concealed among western shoreline rocks. The interior is largely submerged and home to aquatic creatures and kollops, offering little shelter for travelers.

title: Mzahnch
topic_desc: Mzahnch is a Dwemer ruin situated on a small island in the Ascadian Isles, east of Ald Sotha. Like all Dwemer strongholds, it was abandoned in 1E 700 following the mysterious disappearance of its inhabitants. The site retains classic Dwemer subterranean architecture, extending into a main area and a lower level. Two large bipedal ballista siege weapons stand in its exterior. The island and ruin grounds support kresh fiber, gold kanet, and black lichen. Active Dwarven Centurions still patrol the interior halls.
topic_desc_basic: Mzahnch is a Dwemer ruin on a small island in the Ascadian Isles, east of Ald Sotha. Abandoned in 1E 700 during the Dwemer disappearance, the site retains typical Dwarven architecture, exterior siege ballistae, and active Centurion guardians within its two-level interior.

title: Mzahnch Lower Level
topic_desc: Mzahnch Lower Level comprises the deeper subterranean chambers of the Mzahnch Dwemer complex, situated in Vvardenfell's rugged Molag Amur region. This section features characteristic Dwemer architecture with steam conduits, massive metal doors, and carved stone halls extending beneath the upper citadel. Like other lower works of Dwemer strongholds, these depths historically housed machinery, storage, and residential quarters for the clan. The lower level remains largely intact, preserving the enigmatic architectural and engineering legacy of the vanished Dwemer.
topic_desc_basic: Mzahnch Lower Level is the deeper underground section of the Mzahnch Dwemer ruin in Vvardenfell's Molag Amur region. It features standard Dwemer stone and metal architecture, extending the complex beneath the surface citadel. These depths historically served the vanished Dwemer clan's residential and mechanical needs.

title: Mzanchend
topic_desc: Mzanchend is a Dwemer fortress situated in the volcanic wasteland of Molag Amur, in close proximity to the Dwemer ruin of Galom Daeus. Like other settlements of the lost Deep Elves, it consists of labyrinthine stone corridors and grand chambers built around subterranean steamworks, now prowled by dormant automata. The site holds particular interest for scholars of Dwemer engineering, as its interior preserves a rare Dwemer schematic. The ruin's architecture features multi-level junctions and secured vaults typical of Dwemer strongholds, though its remote and hazardous location amidst the ash and lava of Molag Amur keeps it largely inaccessible to all but the most determined explorers.
topic_desc_basic: Mzanchend is a remote Dwemer fortress in the Molag Amur region. Its ancient stone corridors and chambers still house active Dwemer automata and preserve rare Dwemer engineering schematics within its vaults.

title: Mzuleft
topic_desc: Mzuleft is a substantial Dwemer ruin situated in the Sheogorad region, southwest of Dagon Fel on northern Vvardenfell. The site exemplifies classic Dwemer architectural principles, featuring deep subterranean halls, heavy metallic construction, and intricate steam-work mechanisms. Among its notable contents are Dwemer Scarab Plans and a copy of The Egg of Time, indicating the site's historical role in both Dwemer engineering and theological discourse. The ruin's remote island location renders it isolated from settled regions, accessible primarily by sea or arduous overland routes through the rugged archipelago.
topic_desc_basic: Mzuleft is a large Dwemer ruin located in the Sheogorad region, southwest of Dagon Fel on northern Vvardenfell. The site features characteristic Dwemer architecture and contains notable Dwemer schematics and texts. Its remote island setting makes it difficult to reach.

title: Nallit
topic_desc: Nallit is a small cavern situated on an island in the Grazelands, northwest of Tel Aruhn. The island's isolation in the waters of Azura's Coast makes the cave accessible mainly by water or levitation. The cavern's interior is typical of the region's volcanic geology, with rough stone passages and natural chambers. Its remote location has historically attracted those seeking seclusion from mainland authorities, including practitioners of the magical arts who wish to conduct their affairs undisturbed. The presence of summoned Daedra within such retreats is consistent with the practices of independent mages throughout the Grazelands and the broader Telvanni-controlled eastern coast.
topic_desc_basic: Nallit is a small cavern on an island in the Grazelands, northwest of Tel Aruhn. The cave's remote island location makes it accessible primarily by water travel or levitation. Like many such isolated caverns along Azura's Coast, it has historically served as a retreat for those seeking seclusion from mainland settlements.

title: Nammu
topic_desc: Nammu is a cave system in the Grazelands, situated west of Tel Aruhn and roughly midway between the Dunmer stronghold of Falensarano and the Daedric shrine of Yansirramus. The interior features a natural rock bridge spanning a subterranean pool, with passages branching into deeper chambers and an upper level reached by staircase. The cave's remote location amid the ashlands and pastoral Grazelands terrain makes it a natural refuge for those wishing to avoid the authority of nearby Telvanni settlements or Imperial patrols. Its proximity to both a Dunmer stronghold and a Daedric shrine places it within a region long marked by diverse powers and contested access.
topic_desc_basic: Nammu is a cave in the Grazelands west of Tel Aruhn, roughly halfway between the Dunmer stronghold Falensarano and the Daedric shrine Yansirramus. Its interior contains a natural bridge over water and passages leading to deeper chambers. The cave's remote location makes it a natural refuge from nearby Telvanni and Imperial authority.

title: Nchardahrk
topic_desc: Nchardahrk is a Dwemer ruin situated on the island of Sheogorad, southeast of Dagon Fel and the Mzuleft stronghold. Like other surviving sites of the vanished Deep Folk, its architecture reflects classical Dwemer subterranean construction, though its specific historical purpose remains uncertain. The ruin's interior mechanisms remain active, sustained by enduring steam power that drives the automated centurions still patrolling its halls. The site contains substantial remnants of Dwemer engineering, including a notable concentration of cogs and coinage alongside typical artifacts, suggesting it may have served a significant industrial or administrative role within the ancient Dwemer holdings of the Sheogorad archipelago.
topic_desc_basic: Nchardahrk is a Dwemer ruin on Sheogorad island, southeast of Dagon Fel and the Mzuleft site. The remote complex features classical subterranean architecture and extensive mechanical infrastructure. Automated centurion constructs defend its sprawling halls.

title: Nchardumz
topic_desc: Nchardumz is a Dwemer ruin situated northeast of Molag Mar, far east of Mount Kand between two mountain ridges. Like other surviving strongholds of the vanished Deep Folk, its architecture reflects the advanced stonework and mechanical ingenuity characteristic of Dwemer construction. The site consists of a main level and a lower level, typical of the vertical stratification found in Dwemer city-planning. Its remote, rugged placement amid the Molag Mar highlands underscores the Dwemer preference for defensible, mineral-rich terrain. The original purpose and fate of its builders remain obscure, consistent with the broader mysteries of the Dwemer disappearance.
topic_desc_basic: Nchardumz is a Dwemer ruin northeast of Molag Mar, located far east of Mount Kand between two mountain ridges. The stronghold features a main area and a lower level, displaying the characteristic stonework of the vanished Deep Folk.

title: Nchardumz Lower Level
topic_desc: Nchardumz Lower Level comprises the deeper chambers of the Dwemer ruin Nchardumz. Typical of subterranean Dwemer construction, the passages feature massive stone masonry, rusted metal fixtures, and steam-driven mechanisms extending into the volcanic rock. These lower depths historically housed industrial machinery and storage, sustaining the complex's operations above. Like many such sites, the lower level remains isolated and hazardous, its original purpose lost with the Dwemer's disappearance.
topic_desc_basic: The deeper chambers of the Dwemer ruin Nchardumz. Built from heavy stone and rusted metal, the lower level contains the remnants of ancient Dwemer machinery and storage halls. Its original function ended with the Dwemer's disappearance, leaving the passages dark and hazardous.

title: Nimawia Grotto
topic_desc: Nimawia Grotto is a submerged sea cave along the Bitter Coast, lying northwest of Seyda Neen with its entrance facing south just off the shore. The cavern network extends beneath the coastal waters, featuring chambers where air pockets are scarce, making submerged exploration hazardous without preparation. The grotto exemplifies the treacherous, flood-prone cave systems common to the regional coastline, where mineral deposits and aquatic life occasionally attract foragers despite the drowning risks posed by the prolonged underwater passages.
topic_desc_basic: Nimawia Grotto is a small, partially submerged sea cave on the Bitter Coast, situated northwest of Seyda Neen. Its south-facing entrance lies just off the shore. The underwater passages within are hazardous due to scarce air pockets, characteristic of the region's treacherous flooded coastal caves.

title: Nissintu
topic_desc: Nissintu is a small cave situated in the Molag Amur region of Vvardenfell, east of Moonmoth Legion Fort and north of the Fields of Kummu. The volcanic terrain surrounding it is characteristically rugged and inhospitable, marked by lava flows and ash. The cave itself is a modest subterranean space typical of the many smugglers' dens scattered across the island, offering concealed shelter for those seeking to avoid Imperial authority. Its proximity to both the Legion fort and the pilgrim road near the Fields of Kummu makes it a strategically positioned hideout for contraband activity.
topic_desc_basic: Nissintu is a small cave in the Molag Amur region of Vvardenfell, located east of Moonmoth Legion Fort and north of the Fields of Kummu. Like many caves across the island, it serves as a hidden refuge for smugglers operating beyond the reach of Imperial law.

title: Nund
topic_desc: Nund is a small cavern situated just east of Vivec's St. Olms Canton and west of Omani Manor. The cave serves as a smugglers' hideout, reportedly relocated from the vicinity of Ebonheart under the direction of a rumored leader. Its isolated yet accessible position near the canton makes it a convenient coastal stash for contraband moving through the Vivec region.
topic_desc_basic: Nund is a small smugglers' cave located just east of the St. Olms Canton in Vivec, near Omani Manor. The cavern serves as a hidden waystation for moving illicit goods through the region.

title: Odaishah
topic_desc: Odaishah is a small, isolated cave situated in the Ashlands region of Vvardenfell.
