It lies along the roads leading south from the Ghostgate, east of Ald'ruhn, within a stretch of barren terrain largely devoid of notable landmarks. The cave's remote location and challenging surrounding environment make it a secluded refuge far from typical travel routes. Known to attract practitioners of conjuration and Daedric summoning, the site occasionally holds volumes of arcane significance, such as the conjuration text Feyfolgen III. Its distance from settled areas ensures it remains a quiet and obscure corner of the Ashlands.
topic_desc_basic: Odaishah is a small, isolated cave in the Ashlands region of Vvardenfell. Located south of the Ghostgate and east of Ald'ruhn, it sits in a barren area with few nearby landmarks. Its remote position keeps it far from common travel routes.

title: Morrowind shipwrecks
topic_desc: The coastal waters around Vvardenfell hold numerous wrecked vessels, their broken hulls scattered along the shores and shallows of the Inner Sea and the Azurian coast. At least four distinct wrecks are charted by Imperial maritime records—designated Abandoned, Ancient, Derelict, and Deserted—each preserving a multi-deck interior of cabin, upper, and lower levels. Their construction follows standard merchant and Imperial naval framing: timber hulls with planked decking, cargo holds, and stern cabins, now half-flooded and structurally compromised. The distribution reflects the hazards of navigating Vvardenfell's waters: submerged rocks, sudden storms, strong currents, and the navigational difficulties posed by the island's jagged coastline. Some wrecks appear old enough to predate the Imperial charter, suggesting earlier Dunmer or even Nordic merchant losses. Mariners treat these sites with caution, as collapsed decking and standing water make interior exploration dangerous.
topic_desc_basic: Several wrecked ships lie along Vvardenfell's coasts, victims of submerged rocks, storms, and treacherous currents. At least four distinct wrecks are known, each preserving flooded multi-level interiors including cabins and cargo holds. Their broken hulls serve as grim markers of the dangers faced by vessels navigating the island's waters.

title: Adamantium Ore
topic_desc: A dense, irregularly shaped lump of raw adamantium ore exhibiting a dark metallic luster. This exceptionally heavy and valuable mineral is found only in hard-to-come-at and dangerous places beneath Mournhold, where adventurers occasionally retrieve small loads for smithing purposes. In alchemical practice, adamantium ore yields the effects Burden, Restore Magicka, Poison, and Reflect. Its extreme weight makes the Burden effect a natural expression of its properties, while its arcane metallic nature enables the restoration of magicka and the reflection of harmful magic, alongside a potent toxic quality.
topic_desc_basic: A dense, dark metallic lump of raw adamantium ore. This exceptionally heavy and valuable mineral is found in dangerous places beneath Mournhold. Alchemists value it for its varied properties, which include both restorative and harmful qualities.

title: Alit Hide
topic_desc: A rough, mottled patch of tanned hide stripped from an alit, bearing a thick leathery texture and sparse bristly hairs. Ashlanders hunt the wild alit and prepare these durable skins as serviceable multi-purpose leather and regional trade goods. In alchemical practice, the hide yields four distinct properties: Drain Intelligence, Resist Poison, Telekinesis, and Detect Animal. Its combination of sensory and manipulative effects makes it a valued, if intellectually hazardous, reagent.
topic_desc_basic: A rough, mottled patch of thick, leathery hide with sparse bristly hairs, stripped from an alit. Ashlanders hunt the creatures and trade the tanned skins as serviceable leather. Alchemists value the hide for its four properties: Drain Intelligence, Resist Poison, Telekinesis, and Detect Animal.

title: Ampoule Pod
topic_desc: A small, bulbous organic pod with a tapered stem, its pale surface stretched taut over rounded seed chambers. The ampoule pod is the immature fruiting body of the primitive draggle-tail plant, which grows abundantly in the Bitter Coast region. Prized by alchemists for its modest magical properties, the pod yields the effects Water Walking, Paralyze, Detect Animal, and Drain Willpower.
topic_desc_basic: The ampoule pod is the immature fruiting body of the draggle-tail plant, found throughout the Bitter Coast. Alchemists value it for its modest magical properties.

title: Ash Salts
topic_desc: Ash salts are hard grey crystalline deposits formed from ash storms across Morrowind's ash wastes and lava fields. These pale, gritty, ash-colored granules carry a faintly acrid scent and are most often collected from the remains of corprus-afflicted creatures—ash slaves, ash ghouls, and ash zombies. In alchemical practice, ash salts produce three distinct effects: Drain Agility, Resist Magicka, and Cure Blight Disease. Their curative property against blight is particularly valued, as few ingredients share this effect, making ash salts a vital component for healers and alchemists working in blight-affected regions.
topic_desc_basic: Ash salts are pale, gritty mineral crystals gathered from corprus creatures such as ash slaves, ash ghouls, and ash zombies in Morrowind's ash wastes. Alchemists prize them for their rare ability to cure blight disease, alongside effects that drain agility and resist magicka.

title: Ash Yam
topic_desc: Ash yam is a rough, tuberous root with dark, ash-gray skin and dense, pale flesh beneath a gnarled, uneven surface. This hardy vegetable grows commonly throughout the Ascadian Isles region, where it is frequently cultivated on farms. While occasionally consumed as food, its true value lies in practical alchemy. When prepared correctly, ash yam yields four distinct properties: Fortify Intelligence, Fortify Strength, Resist Common Disease, and Detect Key. These combined augmentative and restorative effects make it a staple ingredient for healers and alchemists seeking to enhance physical and mental attributes while providing disease resistance and utility.
topic_desc_basic: Ash yam is a tough, tuberous root vegetable with modest magical properties, characterized by its dark, ash-gray skin and dense, pale flesh. It grows commonly in the Ascadian Isles region, where farmers cultivate it readily. Healers and alchemists value the root for its beneficial properties.

title: Bear Pelt
topic_desc: A thick, brown bear hide with the head removed and the dark fur still attached to the supple leather skin. Harvested from bears native to colder regions such as Solstheim and Skyrim, the pelt serves practical alchemical purposes beyond its use in crafting. When prepared, it yields properties that Drain Fatigue and Fortify Strength, alongside providing Resist Common Disease and Night Eye effects, making it a versatile ingredient for enhancing physical resilience and sensory perception.
topic_desc_basic: A thick, brown bear hide with the dark fur still attached to the supple leather skin. Harvested from bears, it is a common ingredient in alchemy. When prepared, it can Drain Fatigue, Fortify Strength, Resist Common Disease, and grant Night Eye.

title: Bittergreen Petals
topic_desc: Crimson petals from the bittergreen plant curl inward along delicate, slightly translucent edges. The red-flowering bittergreen grows abundantly in the West Gash and in smaller quantities throughout the Ashlands and Red Mountain regions. Alchemists value these petals for their capacity to Restore Intelligence and grant Invisibility, though preparations must account for their detrimental properties, which Drain Endurance and Drain Magicka.
topic_desc_basic: Crimson petals curl inward along delicate, slightly translucent edges. Harvested from the red-flowering bittergreen plant found in the West Gash and Red Mountain regions, these petals are known to Restore Intelligence and grant Invisibility, while also carrying the risk to Drain Endurance and Drain Magicka.

title: Black Anther
topic_desc: Black anther is a dark-hued flower's reproductive part, consisting of a slender filament topped by small, pollen-bearing anthers. It is gathered from a flowering plant that grows along Azura's Coast and is also common in the Ascadian Isles. In alchemical preparation, black anther yields Drain Agility, Resist Fire, Drain Endurance, and Light. Its capacity to produce Light is notably rare, shared by only one other known ingredient, red lichen, making it valued among practitioners seeking illumination effects. The draining properties require careful combination to avoid unintended debilitation.
topic_desc_basic: Black anther is a dark-hued flower part gathered from flowering plants common in the Ascadian Isles and along Azura's Coast. Alchemists value it for its four properties: Drain Agility, Resist Fire, Drain Endurance, and Light. It is one of very few ingredients capable of producing a Light effect.

title: Black Lichen
topic_desc: Black lichen is a hardy primitive plant that thrives in the harsh conditions of Vvardenfell's Ashlands, Red Mountain, Molag Amur, and Azura's Coast. It manifests as a dark, leathery fungus growth forming flat, irregularly shaped clusters across rock surfaces. Alchemists value it for its distinctive properties: it can Drain Strength and Drain Speed, while also providing Resist Frost and Cure Poison. Its Resist Frost effect makes it particularly sought after for protective preparations against cold.
topic_desc_basic: Black lichen is a dark, leathery fungus that forms flat, irregular clusters on rocks. This hardy primitive plant grows in Vvardenfell's harsh Ashlands, Red Mountain, Molag Amur, and Azura's Coast regions. Alchemists prize it for its curative and protective properties.

title: Bloat
topic_desc: Bloat is the thick, pulpy-white tuber of the bloatspore plant, which grows in dark, damp locations. It presents as coarse, pale crystalline salts forming irregular clumps resembling ash residue within a small container. Alchemists value bloat for its diverse properties: it can Drain Magicka, Fortify Intelligence, Fortify Willpower, and Detect Animal. Despite its known botanical origin, the bloatspore is notoriously elusive, making the tuber a rare find often sourced only from specialized vendors or scattered loose samples rather than wild harvest.
topic_desc_basic: Bloat is a thick, pulpy-white tuber harvested from the bloatspore plant, which grows in dark, damp locations. It is a rare ingredient valued by alchemists for its potent properties, including the ability to fortify mental attributes and detect nearby creatures.

title: Blood of an Innocent
topic_desc: Blood of an Innocent is a small cluster of dark red lichen bearing viscous crimson fluid seeping from its rough, irregularly shaped fronds. Its natural source remains unverified by conventional botanical or creature taxonomy. In alchemical practice, the substance yields opposing properties: it provides Light and Cure Common Disease, while simultaneously imposing Drain Speed and Drain Magicka.
topic_desc_basic: Blood of an Innocent is a dark red lichen seeping viscous crimson fluid from rough, irregular fronds. Alchemists value its opposing properties, which provide Light and Cure Common Disease while inflicting Drain Speed and Drain Magicka.

title: Bonemeal
topic_desc: A coarse pale powder of finely ground bone, gathered in a small rough heap. Sourced primarily from the remains of bonewalkers guarding ancestral tombs, and from the bones of man-like races, bonemeal possesses modest magical properties valued in alchemical preparations. Its four recognized effects are Restore Agility, Telekinesis, Drain Fatigue, and Drain Personality. The powder's ready availability from undead remains makes it a staple reagent for practitioners seeking its beneficial properties, though care must be taken regarding its draining qualities.
topic_desc_basic: A coarse pale powder of finely ground bone, commonly harvested from bonewalkers and the bones of man-like races. This readily available reagent possesses modest magical properties valued by alchemists and healers for various preparations.

title: Bread
topic_desc: A rounded loaf with a golden-brown baked crust, a split crust, a pale flour-dusted surface, and a pale dense interior. This staple baked fare is ubiquitous across Vvardenfell and Solstheim, found on tables and in containers from taverns to private homes. While its culinary role is straightforward, alchemists value it as an easily acquired source of Restore Fatigue. Though this property is common among many ingredients, bread's sheer availability makes it a convenient and accessible reagent for restorative craft.
topic_desc_basic: A common golden-brown baked loaf with a pale, dense interior. Found throughout Vvardenfell in homes and taverns, it serves as a readily available culinary staple. In alchemy, it possesses the property to Restore Fatigue.

title: Bristleback Leather
topic_desc: A rough, bristly patch of tanned hide stripped from a wild boar, bearing sparse stiff hairs across its leathery surface. Harvested from the Bristleback herds roaming Solstheim's frozen wilderness, this durable pelt serves alchemists as a potent conduit for elemental and mystical properties. When prepared, the leather yields four distinct effects: Blind, Frost Damage, Resist Frost, and Recall. Its dual frost associations make it valuable for crafting protective elixirs against cold environments, while the destructive and transportive qualities require careful handling.
topic_desc_basic: A rough, bristly patch of tanned hide stripped from a wild boar, bearing sparse stiff hairs across its leathery surface. Solstheim's Bristleback herds provide this durable ingredient. Alchemists prize it for its frost-related properties and other magical qualities.

title: Bungler's Bane
topic_desc: A lumpy, brownish-orange shelf fungus with a spongy texture and irregular, bulbous protrusions, growing in clustered mounds on tree trunks and occasionally cave walls throughout the Bitter Coast region. It closely resembles Hypha Facia, which often grows in the same habitat. Alchemists value it sparingly; its properties are entirely detrimental or disruptive, yielding Drain Speed, Drain Endurance, Dispel, and Drain Strength. Healers and mages exercise caution, as its common name warns of the hazards of careless consumption.
topic_desc_basic: A brownish-orange shelf fungus growing on tree trunks in the Bitter Coast region. It resembles Hypha Facia but is less useful. Its alchemical properties are entirely harmful or disruptive, making it a hazardous ingredient for the unwary.

title: Chokeweed
topic_desc: A slender green herb with narrow leaves tightly clustered along its stiff, upright stems. This tough shrub thrives across the rocky highlands of the West Gash in great quantities, making it a common sight for regional foragers. In alchemical practice, chokeweed yields opposing properties: it can Restore Fatigue and Cure Common Disease, but also carries the detrimental effects to Drain Luck and Drain Willpower. Its reliable disease-curing virtue makes it a staple for healers despite its adverse attributes.
topic_desc_basic: A slender green herb with narrow leaves along stiff, upright stems. This tough shrub grows abundantly in the West Gash highlands. Healers value it as a common remedy that can cure common disease and restore fatigue, though it also carries harmful properties.

title: Coda Flower
topic_desc: A broad-petaled blossom with curling edges and a prominent central stamen cluster rising from its center. It is the fruiting body of the primitive draggle-tail plant, which roots in the shallow swamp waters of the Bitter Coast. The living plant emits a faint glow, though this luminosity fades once the bloom is harvested. Alchemists value the flower primarily for its Levitate property, though it also carries potent adverse qualities: Drain Personality, Drain Intelligence, and Drain Health.
topic_desc_basic: A broad-petaled blossom with curling edges and a prominent central stamen cluster. It grows as the fruiting body of the draggle-tail plant in the Bitter Coast swamps. Alchemists prize it for its Levitate property, though it also carries the harmful effects of Drain Personality, Drain Intelligence, and Drain Health.

title: Comberry
topic_desc: A cluster of small, round, purplish-red berries attached to a short, slender green stem. The bitter comberry grows on bushes cultivated throughout the Ascadian Isles and serves as the foundational ingredient for native Morrowind spirits, including comberry brandy, greef, and shein. In alchemy, the fruit yields four distinct properties: Drain Fatigue, Restore Magicka, Fire Shield, and Reflect. Its reliable availability makes it a staple for practitioners seeking accessible Restore Magicka effects.
topic_desc_basic: A cluster of small, round, purplish-red berries on a slender green stem. Comberry bushes grow in the Ascadian Isles and provide the bitter fruit used to brew native Morrowind brandy, greef, and shein. Alchemists value the berry for its Restore Magicka property.

title: Corkbulb Root
topic_desc: A thick, pale brown taproot tapers to a rounded tip, its rough surface marked by wiry rootlets and shallow ridges. Corkbulb trees are cultivated for these tough, fibrous roots, which serve as a substitute for wood across Vvardenfell, where proper trees cannot survive the harsh environment. The plant grows best in the Ascadian Isles, where plantation agriculture thrives. In alchemy, the root is valued for its modest magical properties, yielding Cure Paralyzation, Restore Health, Lightning Shield, and Fortify Luck. Its reliable first effect makes raw consumption a practical emergency measure against paralysis.
topic_desc_basic: Corkbulb root is a thick, pale brown taproot harvested from cultivated corkbulb trees. On Vvardenfell, these fibrous roots substitute for wood, which scarce trees cannot provide. The plant thrives in the Ascadian Isles. Healers and alchemists prize the root for its restorative and protective properties.

title: Crab Meat
topic_desc: Crab meat is a reddish chunk of raw crustacean flesh torn from a mudcrab, bearing a few remnants of shell. Mudcrabs are native to Vvardenfell and thrive wherever water is found, from coastal shallows to inland waterways. The flesh is prized for its sweet taste and modest magical properties. Alchemists value it for four confirmed effects: Restore Fatigue, Resist Shock, Lightning Shield, and Restore Luck. Its low cost and ready availability make it a staple reagent for novice and traveling practitioners.
topic_desc_basic: Crab meat is raw flesh taken from the mudcrabs that inhabit Vvardenfell's waters. It is valued as food and as a common alchemical reagent known to restore fatigue and confer resistance to shock among other properties.

title: Daedra Skin
topic_desc: A rough, leathery patch of mottled skin with a faintly translucent, reddish hue and a slick, rubbery texture. Daedra skin must be harvested from a specimen while its remains persist on the mortal plane following banishment, a dangerous and demanding task. Alchemists value the material for its diverse properties: it can Fortify Strength, Cure Common Disease, Paralyze, and grant Swift Swim. Though the skin possesses modest magical virtues, the peril of acquiring it from volatile Daedric remains ensures its scarcity and high commercial value among practitioners.
topic_desc_basic: A rough, leathery patch of mottled skin with a faintly translucent, reddish hue and a slick, rubbery texture. Harvested from Daedra remains before they return to Oblivion, this dangerous-to-collect ingredient is valued by alchemists for its varied magical properties.

title: Daedra's Heart
topic_desc: A dark, glistening organ with a rough, asymmetrical shape and faintly visible veins across its slick surface. This fleshy, ridged specimen must be harvested during a creature's brief appearance on the mortal plane, a process generally fatal to the entity, rendering the substance rare and expensive. Prized by alchemists, its properties yield Restore Magicka, Fortify Endurance, Drain Agility, and Night Eye effects. It is one of the very few known sources for the Night Eye property, making it exceptionally valuable for brews of darksight despite its debilitating effect on agility.
topic_desc_basic: A dark, glistening organ harvested from daedra during their brief appearance on the mortal plane. Because extraction is generally fatal to the specimen, the substance is rare and expensive. Alchemists value it for its notable magical properties, particularly its capacity to grant night vision, alongside effects that restore magicka and fortify endurance, though it impairs agility.

title: Diamond
topic_desc: A rare, transparent, extremely hard crystalline gemstone of great value, distinguished by its brilliant faceted octahedral shape and sharp angular faces. Prized as both a precious jewel and a potent alchemical reagent, diamonds are occasionally uncovered in Dwemer ruins or offered at Daedric shrines. In alchemy, diamond yields Drain Agility, Invisibility, Reflect, and Detect Key, making it highly sought after for crafting concealment and protective mixtures. Its Invisibility property is notably uncommon among known ingredients.
topic_desc_basic: A rare, transparent, extremely hard gemstone of great value, found occasionally in Dwemer ruins and Daedric shrines. In alchemy, it is prized for its useful properties, including the ability to grant Invisibility.

title: Dreugh Wax
topic_desc: A waxy, amber-yellow lump bearing the faint impression of segmented Dreugh shell along one curved side. This tough substance is scraped from the shells of Dreugh, powerful aquatic creatures whose hunting provides both hides and wax, a dangerous occupation. Alchemists value the wax for its restorative and fortifying properties, though it carries adverse side effects. Its exact alchemical effects are Fortify Strength, Restore Strength, Drain Luck, and Drain Willpower.
topic_desc_basic: A tough, waxy, amber-yellow substance scraped from the shells of dangerous aquatic Dreugh. It is valued by alchemists for its ability to restore and fortify a user's strength, though it also drains luck and willpower.

title: Durzog Meat
topic_desc: A rough slab of reddish meat cut from a durzog, bearing dark streaks of sinew and a slightly moist surface. Durzogs are fierce reptilian quadrupeds often kept by Goblin-ken for war and hunting, making their flesh a scarce commodity beyond the caverns of Mournhold. Alchemists value this coarse tissue for its potent mixture of beneficial and harmful properties. When prepared, the meat reliably yields preparations that Fortify Agility and Fortify Strength, enhancing physical capabilities. Conversely, improper mixtures inflict Blind and Damage Magicka, limiting sensory and arcane potential.
topic_desc_basic: A rough, sinew-streaked slab of reddish meat harvested from the fierce durzog quadrupeds used by Goblin-ken. Alchemists find this coarse flesh difficult to work with, as it can Fortify Strength and Fortify Agility alongside dangerous properties that Blind and Damage Magicka.

title: Ectoplasm
topic_desc: Ectoplasm is a translucent, gelatinous mass of pale substance exuding faint wisps of vaporous residue. It is the filmy residue that remains after a revenant spirit has been banished from the mortal plane, possessing modest magical properties. Alchemists value it for its capacity to Fortify Agility and grant Detect Animal, though it carries dangerous properties that Drain Strength and Drain Health.
topic_desc_basic: Ectoplasm is a translucent, gelatinous residue left behind when a revenant spirit is banished from the mortal plane. It possesses modest magical properties valued by alchemists and healers.

title: Emerald
topic_desc: A faceted, translucent green gemstone cut into a symmetrical hexagonal form with smooth, polished surfaces. This transparent green crystal is extremely rare and valuable, possessing modest innate magical properties. While no Vvardenfell mines yield emeralds and no creatures bear them, they are occasionally uncovered in Dwemer barrels or found as offerings at Daedric shrines, though shrine gems are sometimes cursed. In alchemy, emeralds are prized for their restorative and augmenting qualities, but carry debilitating side effects. Their exact alchemical effects are Fortify Magicka, Restore Health, Drain Agility, and Drain Endurance.
topic_desc_basic: A faceted, translucent green gemstone cut into a symmetrical hexagonal form with smooth, polished surfaces. This rare and valuable transparent green crystal possesses modest magical properties. Alchemists value it for its restorative and augmenting applications, though it carries debilitating side effects.

title: Fire Petal
topic_desc: A curled, flame-orange petal with a waxy surface and delicate, translucent edges radiating from a dark central vein. Fire petals are collected from the fire fern plant, which grows on Red Mountain, in Molag Mar, and along Azura's Coast. The plant thrives primarily in the Ashlands and Molag Amur regions. Alchemists value fire petals for four confirmed properties: Resist Fire, Drain Health, Spell Absorption, and Paralyze. The petal's protective and absorptive qualities make it useful to healers and mages preparing for fire or spell exposure, while its paralytic property appeals to practitioners of combat alchemy. Several apothecaries across Vvardenfell maintain restocking supplies.
topic_desc_basic: A curled, flame-orange petal with a waxy surface and translucent edges, gathered from fire fern plants growing on Red Mountain and in the Ashlands and Molag Amur regions. Alchemists prize it for properties including fire resistance and spell absorption.

title: Fire Salts
topic_desc: Crystalline reddish-orange granules gleam with an inner warmth, resembling coarse salt flecked with dark cinders. Fire salts are the crystalline compound that precipitates from elemental fire in solution. Such residues may be collected from the remains of fire atronachs that have been banished from the mortal plane. In alchemical practice, fire salts exhibit four distinct properties: Drain Health, Fortify Agility, Resist Frost, and Fire Shield. Their reliable Resist Frost effect makes them particularly valued among alchemists and healers for preparing protective elixirs against cold.
topic_desc_basic: Crystalline reddish-orange granules that gleam with inner warmth, resembling coarse salt flecked with dark cinders. Fire salts precipitate from elemental fire in solution and can be gathered from the remains of banished fire atronachs. Alchemists prize them for producing Resist Frost and Fire Shield preparations, alongside their Fortify Agility and Drain Health properties.

title: Flaming Eye of the Lightkeeper
topic_desc: A spherical eyeball emanating visible flames that flicker across its smooth, unblinking surface. This rare ingredient yields potent and volatile properties in synthesis. Alchemists value it for its capacity to bestow Resist Frost and Night Eye, alongside the physically enhancing Fortify Strength. However, practitioners must carefully manage its dangerous Drain Magicka effect. The exact creature from which this fiery organ originates remains a subject of uncertain speculation among healers and scholars.
topic_desc_basic: A spherical eyeball emanating visible flames across its smooth surface. This unusual ingredient is prized by alchemists and healers for its potent magical properties, though its exact natural origin remains uncertain.

title: Frost Salts
topic_desc: Frost salts are coarse, pale blue crystalline compounds clustered in rough, frosty aggregates that shimmer with a cold translucence. This substance precipitates from elemental frost in solution and can be gathered from the remains of frost atronachs banished from the mortal plane. In alchemical practice, the salts exhibit four distinct properties: they Drain Speed, Restore Magicka, provide a Frost Shield, and confer Resist Fire. These contrasting elemental qualities make the ingredient particularly valued by mages seeking magicka restoration alongside protective enchantments, despite the temporary reduction in mobility it imposes.
topic_desc_basic: Frost salts are pale blue, coarse crystalline aggregates shimmering with cold translucence. Gathered from the remains of banished frost atronachs, they are valued in alchemy for restoring magicka and providing frost or fire protection, though they slow the user.

title: Ghoul Heart
topic_desc: Ghoul heart is heart tissue harvested from the remains of an ash ghoul, a corprus-warped servant associated with Sixth House activity. The organ appears as a dark, fleshy mass with a shriveled, lopsided shape and coarse veins trailing across its surface. It is valued at one hundred fifty drakes and is notably rare in trade. Alchemists prize it for three confirmed properties: Paralyze, Cure Poison, and Fortify Attack Bonus. The Fortify Attack Bonus property is especially uncommon among known reagents, making ghoul heart sought after by practitioners seeking to enhance martial precision through alchemical preparation. Healers value its antitoxic properties, while the paralytic effect demands careful dosing.
topic_desc_basic: Ghoul heart is heart tissue taken from an ash ghoul, a creature warped by corprus. The organ is dark, shriveled, and lopsided with coarse veins. Alchemists prize it for its rare properties, which include Paralyze, Cure Poison, and Fortify Attack Bonus. It is scarce in trade and commands a high price among apothecaries.

title: Girith's Guar Hide
topic_desc: A rough, thick patch of mottled gray hide stripped from a guar, bearing sparse bristles. This specific guar hide yields a distinctive alchemical spectrum. Practitioners employ it to Drain Fatigue and Restore Personality, while also harnessing its properties to Fortify Endurance and Fortify Luck. Its enduring usefulness makes it a valued staple among healers and alchemists.
topic_desc_basic: A rough, thick patch of mottled gray guar hide bearing sparse bristles. Alchemists value it for its distinctive properties, which affect a subject's endurance, luck, personality, and fatigue in both beneficial and harmful ways.

title: Gold Kanet
topic_desc: A cluster of small golden flowers attached to slender green stems, with delicate petals radiating outward from pale centers. Gold kanet is a flowering plant commonly found in the Ascadian Isles and on Azura's Coast, typically growing near rocks. Its broad dark-green leaves are spiny and should be handled with care. In alchemy, the plant yields potent properties: Drain Health, Burden, Drain Luck, and Restore Strength.
topic_desc_basic: Gold kanet is a flowering plant with small golden petals and spiny dark-green leaves that grows near rocks in the Ascadian Isles and on Azura's Coast. Alchemists value it for its restorative and debilitating properties.

title: Golden Sedge Flowers
topic_desc: Golden sedge flowers are a loose cluster of small golden blooms attached to slender green sedge stalks. Alchemists value them for a distinctive combination of properties: they Drain Magicka while simultaneously providing Fortify Strength and Fortify Attack Bonus, alongside a Swift Swim effect that enhances aquatic movement. This unusual profile makes them useful to warriors and travelers who rely on physical prowess rather than magical aptitude.
topic_desc_basic: Golden sedge flowers consist of small golden blooms on slender green stalks. Alchemists prize them for properties that enhance physical combat and swimming speed while diminishing magical reserves.

title: Grahl Eyeball
topic_desc: A large, pale eyeball radiating an unnatural orange flame continuously burns across its veined surface. Harvested from the grahl, a fearsome ice-dwelling beast of Solstheim, this organ retains its eerie combustion even in isolation. Alchemists prize it for its potent and contradictory properties. When prepared, it grants Resist Frost and Night Eye, alongside Fortify Strength, though these benefits come at the cost of a Drain Magicka effect.
topic_desc_basic: A large, pale eyeball with an unnatural orange flame burning across its surface. Harvested from the grahl, a Solstheim ice-beast, it is valued by alchemists for granting frost resistance and night vision, though it drains magicka.

title: Gravedust
topic_desc: Gravedust is a small heap of pale, powdery ash composed of fine, gritty particles that clump together loosely. This spirit-affinitive substance is taken from remains buried in consecrated ground. It is somewhat rare, as it is harvested from no living creature or plant. Healers and alchemists value it for its potent restorative and curative properties, though it carries dangerous side effects. Its exact alchemical effects are Drain Intelligence, Cure Common Disease, Drain Magicka, and Restore Endurance.
topic_desc_basic: Gravedust is a pale, powdery ash taken from remains interred in consecrated ground. Valued by healers, this spirit-affinitive dust is somewhat rare and harvested from no living creature or plant. It can Cure Common Disease and Restore Endurance, though it also drains mental faculties.

title: Gravetar
topic_desc: Gravetar is a cluster of small, dark red berries with smooth, waxy skins and tiny green stems attached at the crown. Found in cold, northern regions, it is valued in alchemical practice for its potent but mixed properties. When prepared correctly, gravetar yields Resist Frost and Fortify Fatigue, making it useful for endurance in harsh climates. However, it carries significant risks: the same preparation also produces Drain Health and Drain Luck. Healers and alchemists must carefully balance its beneficial and harmful effects when crafting frost-resistant or stamina-enhancing concoctions.
topic_desc_basic: Gravetar consists of small, dark red berries with smooth, waxy skins and tiny green stems. Found in cold northern regions, these berries offer both beneficial and harmful alchemical properties. They can bolster stamina and protect against frost, but are dangerous to consume directly as they also drain health and diminish fortune.

title: Green Lichen
topic_desc: Green lichen is a hardy primitive plant with modest magical properties. It presents as a pale green, flat, leafy lichen with crinkled edges and a slightly powdery surface. It typically grows on rocks, primarily within the West Gash region, though some accounts also place it in the Ascadian Isles and Azura's Coast. In alchemy, it is valued for its beneficial properties: it can Fortify Personality and Cure Common Disease. However, preparations carry significant risks, as the lichen also imparts Drain Strength and Drain Health effects, requiring careful formulation to avoid debilitating the subject.
topic_desc_basic: Green lichen is a hardy primitive plant with modest magical properties. This pale green, flat, leafy growth features crinkled edges and a slightly powdery surface. It grows on rocks, mainly in the West Gash region. Alchemists use it to Fortify Personality and Cure Common Disease, though it also carries harmful Drain Strength and Drain Health properties.

title: Guar Hide
topic_desc: A rough, leathery patch of mottled grey-green skin stripped from a guar, bearing a sparse coating of coarse bristles. Guar hide is cured to make guar leather, a material widely used in native clothing, armors, and household goods throughout Morrowind. The hide trade is a notable commercial concern, with Great Houses Hlaalu and Redoran competing to supply alchemists and craftsmen. In alchemy, guar hide possesses four known properties: Drain Fatigue, Fortify Endurance, Restore Personality, and Fortify Luck.
topic_desc_basic: A rough, leathery patch of mottled grey-green skin stripped from a guar, bearing a sparse coating of coarse bristles. Cured guar hide yields guar leather, a staple material for Dunmer clothing, armor, and household goods. Alchemists value it for its restorative and fortifying properties.

title: Hackle-Lo Leaf
topic_desc: A broad, slightly curled green leaf with prominent veins running along its smooth surface. Hackle-lo is a tasty edible succulent leaf of the Grazelands, prized both for its taste and its roborative powers. Though it grows mainly in the Grazelands of northeastern Vvardenfell, it is commonly found in food larders throughout civilized areas of Morrowind. Alchemists value it for four distinct properties: Restore Fatigue, Paralyze, Water Breathing, and Restore Luck. Its combination of restorative and more exotic effects makes it a versatile reagent for both healing preparations and specialized mixtures.
topic_desc_basic: A broad, slightly curled green leaf with prominent veins. Hackle-lo is a tasty edible succulent prized for its flavor and restorative properties. It grows mainly in the Grazelands but is commonly kept in food larders throughout settled Morrowind.

title: Heart of an Innocent
topic_desc: Heart of an Innocent is a dark crimson organ with a smooth, glistening surface and thick, branching vessels extending from its asymmetrical, ventricle-like shape. It shares visual qualities with daedra hearts but is distinguished by its association with purity rather than daedric origin. Alchemists value it for four confirmed properties: it can Restore Magicka and Fortify Endurance, while also imposing Drain Agility and granting Night Eye. The combination of restorative and sensory effects makes it a sought-after but unsettling component, prized by healers and mages operating in Solstheim's harsh frontier.
topic_desc_basic: A dark crimson organ with a smooth, glistening surface and thick, branching vessels. Alchemists prize it for properties that Restore Magicka, Fortify Endurance, Drain Agility, and grant Night Eye. It is found in Solstheim and traded among healers and mages.

title: Heart of the Udyrfrykte
topic_desc: A dark, glistening organ with thick, fibrous veins and a dense, muscular texture suggesting a powerful, bestial origin. Harvested from the legendary Udyrfrykte of Solstheim, this heart is prized by alchemists for its potent and varied properties. When prepared correctly, it can Restore Magicka and Fortify Endurance, while also imparting Night Eye. However, its bestial nature carries a debilitating side effect that will Drain Agility, requiring careful formulation to mitigate.
topic_desc_basic: A dark, glistening organ with thick, fibrous veins and a dense, muscular texture suggesting a powerful, bestial origin. Sourced from the legendary Udyrfrykte, this rare ingredient is valued for its ability to Restore Magicka, Fortify Endurance, and grant Night Eye, though it also carries the hazardous effect to Drain Agility.

title: Heart of the Wolf
topic_desc: Heart of the Wolf is a rare alchemical reagent harvested from wolves, particularly those prowling the frozen wilds of Solstheim. It appears as a dark, muscular organ with a rough, fibrous surface and deep crimson coloration resembling a daedric heart. Alchemists prize it for a distinctive four-effect profile: it can Restore Magicka and Fortify Endurance, while also imposing Drain Agility and granting Night Eye. The combination of restorative, enhancing, and sensory properties makes it valuable to practitioners who can isolate beneficial effects while mitigating the agility penalty. Its substantial market value reflects both its potency and the danger of procurement from predatory beasts in harsh northern territories.
topic_desc_basic: A dark, muscular organ taken from wolves, deep crimson and fibrous, resembling a daedric heart. Found on Solstheim's wolves, it is valued by alchemists for restoring magicka, fortifying endurance, and granting night vision, though it also drains agility.

title: Heartwood
topic_desc: Heartwood is a rough, reddish-brown slab of dense interior wood bearing deep natural grain lines and jagged edges. Prized by alchemists for its potent magical resonance, it is a valuable and somewhat rare reagent. When consumed or distilled, its properties yield a mixture of enhancement and detriment. The precise effects it manifests are Restore Magicka, Fortify Agility, Drain Strength, and Weakness to Fire. Its capacity to Restore Magicka and Fortify Agility makes it sought after by mages and scouts, though practitioners must carefully account for the debilitating Drain Strength and the dangerous Weakness to Fire it simultaneously induces.
topic_desc_basic: Heartwood is a rough, reddish-brown slab of dense interior wood with deep grain lines and jagged edges. Alchemists value it for its mixed properties, which can Restore Magicka and Fortify Agility, though it also carries the detrimental effects of Drain Strength and Weakness to Fire.

title: Heather
topic_desc: Heather is a low evergreen shrub of the Ascadian Isles, characterized by delicate sprigs of small pink-purple bell-shaped flowers clustered along slender green stems with tiny narrow leaves. Though possessing modest magical properties, it holds recognized value in alchemical practice. Its preparations can Restore Personality and provide a Feather effect to lighten burdens. However, improper handling risks adverse consequences, as it can Drain Speed and Drain Personality. The plant's needle-like foliage draws comparison to northern trees, yet it thrives in Morrowind's temperate coastal regions rather than Skyrim's climate.
topic_desc_basic: Heather is a low evergreen shrub found throughout the Ascadian Isles, recognized by its small pink-purple bell-shaped flowers on slender stems. It possesses modest alchemical properties valued by healers and alchemists.

title: Holly Berries
topic_desc: A small cluster of round red berries attached to a few stiff green leaves. Holly berries grow on Solstheim's snowy shrubs and are valued by alchemists for their frost-aligned properties. When prepared properly, they yield Resist Frost, Frost Shield, Frost Damage, and Weakness to Fire. Healers favor them in northern regions where frostbite and exposure prove constant threats.
topic_desc_basic: Red berries gathered from holly shrubs in Solstheim's cold climate. Alchemists prize them for frost-related properties, including protection against cold and the capacity to inflict freezing harm upon those exposed to their essence.

title: Horker Tusk
topic_desc: A curved, pointed ivory tusk harvested from a horker, pale yellow in color with a smooth, slightly ridged surface. Horkers are large tusked marine mammals native to the icy coastal waters of Solstheim and northern Tamriel. The tusks are valued by alchemists for their distinctive magical properties: Drain Alteration, Fortify Intelligence, Fortify Maximum Magicka, and Detect Animal. This combination makes the tusk particularly sought by mages seeking to expand their arcane capacity and mental acuity, while its ability to Detect Animal proves useful for hunters traversing Solstheim's wilderness. The tusk is relatively lightweight and modest in commercial value.
topic_desc_basic: A curved ivory tusk harvested from horkers, large marine mammals found along Solstheim's icy coasts. The pale yellow tusk is smooth with slight ridging. Alchemists prize it for properties that Fortify Intelligence, Fortify Maximum Magicka, Detect Animal, and Drain Alteration, making it valued by mages and hunters alike.

title: Horn Lily Bulb
topic_desc: A pale, tapered bulb with a slightly curved horn-like shape and thin, papery outer layers covering its firm surface. Harvested from the horn lily, a flower found predominantly in the Mournhold region, this ingredient holds recognized alchemical value. When prepared, it yields four distinct properties: Resist Paralysis, Drain Health, Restore Strength, and Restore Endurance. Its capacity to fortify physical vigor and ward off paralytic afflictions makes it sought by healers and poisoners alike, though the Drain Health effect demands careful formulation to avoid self-harm.
topic_desc_basic: A pale, tapered bulb with a slightly curved horn-like shape and thin, papery outer layers covering its firm surface. Harvested from the horn lily plant of the Mournhold region, it possesses notable alchemical properties that can both restore bodily vigor and inflict harm depending on preparation.

title: Hound Meat
topic_desc: A rough slab of reddish meat cut from a nix-hound, bearing a few intact tendons and marbled with pale fat. This sweet, tender flesh is a common foodstuff throughout Vvardenfell, readily harvested from the ubiquitous nix-hounds that roam the island. Beyond its culinary uses, hound meat possesses modest magical properties valued in alchemy. When prepared correctly, it yields preparations that Restore Fatigue and Fortify Fatigue, while rarer applications can induce Reflect and Detect Enchantment effects.
topic_desc_basic: A rough slab of reddish meat cut from a nix-hound, marbled with pale fat. This sweet, tender flesh is a common food found throughout Vvardenfell. It also possesses modest magical properties of use to alchemists and healers.

title: Human Flesh
topic_desc: A thick, raw slab of reddish meat with pale sinew still clinging to the unevenly cut surface. Human flesh cannot be harvested from living subjects and is exceptionally rare, with only a handful of known samples existing in Vvardenfell and Solstheim. Alchemically, it carries potent but contradictory properties: it can Fortify Health, yet simultaneously Drain Intelligence and Drain Personality. These severe cognitive and social detriments make it a dangerous reagent, valued primarily by those willing to risk mental degradation for physical vitality.
topic_desc_basic: A thick, raw slab of reddish meat with pale sinew clinging to its uneven surface. This rare ingredient cannot be harvested from living people. Alchemically, it Fortify Health but also Drain Intelligence and Drain Personality, making it a dangerous and controversial reagent.

title: Hypha Facia
topic_desc: Hypha Facia is a pale, shelf-like fungal growth with a rounded, irregularly lobed cap and a short, stubby central stem. Found on tree trunks and occasionally cave walls throughout the Bitter Coast region, it is often confused with the similar-looking Bungler's Bane, though Hypha Facia is safe to eat. In alchemy, it carries the effects Drain Luck, Drain Agility, Drain Fatigue, and Detect Enchantment.
topic_desc_basic: Hypha Facia is a pale, shelf-like fungus that grows on tree trunks in the Bitter Coast region. It is safe to eat and resembles the similar Bungler's Bane. Alchemists value it for its detection and debilitating properties.

title: Kagouti Hide
topic_desc: A thick, rough patch of mottled brown and gray hide stripped from a kagouti, with coarse bristles protruding along the edges. Harvested from the aggressive, tusked kagouti roaming the Morrowind wilderness, the hide serves common crafters as a durable leather for clothing and household goods. In alchemy, it offers a distinctive spectrum of properties: Drain Fatigue, Fortify Speed, Resist Common Disease, and Night Eye. This rare Night Eye property makes the hide particularly valued by potion-makers seeking to enhance vision in darkness.
topic_desc_basic: A thick, rough patch of mottled brown and gray hide with coarse bristles, stripped from a wild kagouti. Commonly tanned into durable leather for clothing and household goods, it also sees use in alchemy for its notable properties, including a rare ability to grant enhanced vision in darkness.

title: Kresh Fiber
topic_desc: A coarse bundle of pale plant fibers gathered from the kresh weed, twisted into a rough, spool-like shape. This resinous fiber is harvested from kreshweed, a coarse grass thriving near salt water across the Grazelands, Azura's Coast, and the West Gash. Alchemists value it for its modest magical properties, which include the ability to Restore Luck and Fortify Personality, alongside detrimental qualities that Drain Magicka and Drain Speed.
topic_desc_basic: A coarse, resinous plant fiber gathered from kreshweed, a coarse grass growing near saltwater in the Grazelands and Azura's Coast. Alchemists prize it for properties that Restore Luck and Fortify Personality, though it also Drain Magicka and Drain Speed.

title: Kwama Cuttle
topic_desc: Kwama cuttle is a pale, squarish slab of resilient, waxy substance harvested from the beaks of kwama beasts, bearing a rough, fibrous texture and faintly mottled surface patterns. Foragers, workers, warriors, and queens all yield this material, which possesses modest magical properties valued in alchemy. When prepared, it exhibits the effects Resist Poison and Drain Fatigue, alongside the aquatic virtues Water Walking and Water Breathing.
topic_desc_basic: Kwama cuttle is a tough, waxy substance taken from the beaks of kwama beasts. It possesses modest magical properties useful to alchemists, offering Resist Poison and Drain Fatigue effects, alongside Water Walking and Water Breathing virtues.

title: Large Kwama Egg
topic_desc: A large, oval kwama egg with a pale, smooth shell and subtle surface mottling. Harvested from kwama egg sacs within Vvardenfell's worked mines, these nutritious staples are widely consumed throughout the Empire and remain fresh for extended periods. In alchemy, the egg yields Restore Fatigue, Paralyze, Frost Shield, and Fortify Health. Its ready availability makes it a practical base for restorative and protective preparations, though the paralytic property demands measured handling.
topic_desc_basic: A large, oval kwama egg with a pale, smooth shell and subtle surface mottling. Harvested from kwama egg sacs in Vvardenfell's mines, this common, nutritious foodstuff is widely eaten across the Empire. Alchemists value it for its Restore Fatigue, Paralyze, Frost Shield, and Fortify Health properties.

title: Corprusmeat
topic_desc: Corprusmeat is diseased flesh harvested from victims of the Divine Disease. It appears as irregular, swollen hunks bearing mottled discoloration, knobby protrusions, or weeping yellowish fluid. Specimens are often bound tightly in coarse, bloodstained cloth to conceal their corrupted surfaces. Found in abundance throughout Sixth House strongholds—hanging from altar strings or filling troughs—the material holds no curative value. Its alchemical properties are uniformly harmful, manifesting as Drain Fatigue, Drain Health, and Drain Magicka. Consequently, healers consider it entirely worthless for medicinal preparation, though its sheer abundance ensures it remains a recognized, if dangerous, subject of blight pathology.
topic_desc_basic: Corprusmeat is diseased flesh from corprus victims, appearing as swollen, discolored hunks sometimes wrapped in coarse cloth. Found abundantly in Sixth House strongholds, it possesses no beneficial properties. Its alchemical effects are entirely harmful: Drain Fatigue, Drain Health, and Drain Magicka.

title: Lloramor Spines
topic_desc: Lloramor Spines are a cluster of pale, sharp spines radiating from a dark, dried base segment. Alchemists value these peculiar growths for their diverse magical and toxic properties. When prepared correctly, they yield Spell Absorption and Invisibility, alongside Poison and Detect Enchantment. Their exact natural origin remains uncertain, though the dried base suggests they are harvested from a specialized organism or rare fungal growth rather than a common flora.
topic_desc_basic: Lloramor Spines consist of pale, sharp spines radiating from a dark, dried base segment. Alchemists prize them for yielding Spell Absorption, Invisibility, Poison, and Detect Enchantment. Their precise natural source remains uncertain.

title: Luminous Russula
topic_desc: Luminous russula is a squat, mottled-brown-and-green toadstool mushroom native to the Bitter Coast region, also found in regional caves and mines. It bears a broad-capped fungus with pale, seemingly phosphorescent coloring and thick, sturdy white gills beneath the rounded cap. Living specimens emit a visible glow, and even harvested samples retain enough luminosity to serve as markers in dark environments. Alchemists value the fungus for its distinct properties: it grants Water Breathing, imposes Drain Fatigue, and delivers Poison. Its Water Breathing effect is notably accessible, manifesting as the primary property, while the Poison effect remains comparatively rare in standard ingredient compounding.
topic_desc_basic: Luminous russula is a squat, mottled-brown-and-green toadstool mushroom of the Bitter Coast region. This broad-capped fungus displays pale, seemingly phosphorescent coloring and thick, sturdy white gills. It naturally glows in the dark, and alchemists employ it for its Water Breathing, Drain Fatigue, and Poison properties.

title: Marshmerrow
topic_desc: A cluster of pale, reedy stalks topped with small, rounded, golden flower heads. Marshmerrow is an important cash crop cultivated in the Ascadian Isles and found wild in the Grazelands and on Azura's Coast. Its sweet pulp is a delectable foodstuff with modest restorative properties. In alchemy, it yields Restore Health and Detect Enchantment alongside the detrimental Drain Willpower and Drain Fatigue effects.
topic_desc_basic: A cluster of pale, reedy stalks topped with small, rounded, golden flower heads. This sweet-pulped reed is an important cash crop of the Ascadian Isles and grows wild along Azura's Coast and the Grazelands. It is widely used in healing potions.

title: Marsus' Guar Hide
topic_desc: Marsus' Guar Hide is a coarse, shaggy pelt of mottled greenish hide scraped from a guar, bearing irregular patches of darker fur. Guar are domesticated pack beasts widespread across Morrowind, valued for their labor and occasionally for their pelts. When prepared alchemically, this hide exhibits four distinct properties: Drain Fatigue, Fortify Endurance, Restore Personality, and Fortify Luck. The blend of fortifying and restorative virtues makes it a noteworthy ingredient for bolstering resilience and temperament, though the fatigue-draining quality demands careful formulation by experienced alchemists.
topic_desc_basic: A coarse, shaggy pelt of mottled greenish hide with darker fur patches, scraped from a guar. These domesticated pack beasts are common throughout Morrowind, and their hides occasionally find use in alchemical preparations, where they are known to influence both physical and mental attributes.

title: Meadow Rye
topic_desc: A slender stalk of golden grain topped with a bristly, whiskered head of clustered kernels. Meadow rye is a common cereal grass cultivated across temperate reaches. In alchemical practice, the grain yields opposing properties regarding bodily velocity: it can Fortify Speed and Restore Speed, yet paradoxically also induces Drain Speed. Additionally, it carries the hazardous capacity to Damage Health, demanding careful formulation by practitioners.
topic_desc_basic: A slender stalk of golden grain topped with a bristly, whiskered head of clustered kernels. This common cereal grass is valued by alchemists for its contradictory effects on bodily velocity and its harmful properties.

title: Meteor Slime
topic_desc: Meteor Slime is a viscous, dark-hued gelatinous mass extracted from a scrib, exhibiting a faintly iridescent sheen. Prized by alchemists and healers for its potent curative and restorative properties, this distinctive exudate offers reliable therapeutic applications. When prepared correctly, it can Fortify Willpower and Restore Willpower, while also providing the capacity to Cure Poison and Cure Blight Disease. Its efficacy against blight makes it particularly valuable in Morrowind's afflicted regions.
topic_desc_basic: Meteor Slime is a viscous, dark-hued gelatinous mass extracted from a scrib, notable for its faintly iridescent sheen. Healers and alchemists value this ingredient for its restorative and curative properties, particularly its usefulness in treating poisons and blight diseases.

title: Muck
topic_desc: A dark, amorphous clump of viscous organic matter with a faintly glistening, uneven surface. This damp, fibrous slime is harvested from the crushed muckspunge plants that grow in the West Gash and on Azura's Coast. Unless properly prepared in the native manner, the substance is mildly toxic. Healers and alchemists value it for its curative properties, and it is commonly used in potions of cure disease. Its alchemical effects are Drain Intelligence, Detect Key, Drain Personality, and Cure Common Disease.
topic_desc_basic: A dark, amorphous clump of viscous organic matter with a faintly glistening, uneven surface. This damp, fibrous slime is harvested from muckspunge plants growing in the West Gash and on Azura's Coast. It is mildly toxic unless properly prepared, but widely valued by healers for its Cure Common Disease property.

title: Muffin
topic_desc: A small, rounded, golden-brown baked muffin with a slightly domed, cracked top and a pale, floury crust. Though commonly prepared and consumed as simple baked food throughout Vvardenfell, it possesses modest alchemical properties. When subjected to proper preparation, the muffin yields only a single confirmed effect: Restore Fatigue. Its widespread availability and low weight make it a readily accessible component for alchemists and healers seeking to brew basic restorative mixtures.
topic_desc_basic: A small, rounded, golden-brown baked muffin with a slightly domed, cracked top and a pale, floury crust. Often eaten as a simple food, it can also be used in alchemy to Restore Fatigue.

title: Netch Leather
topic_desc: A rough, thick strip of tanned hide with a pebbled surface texture and a deep amber hue. Harvested from the native netch of Vvardenfell, particularly in the Bitter Coast and Ascadian Isles, this prepared skin is a significant export product. Cured netch skin is valued throughout the Empire for its durability and flexibility, featuring prominently in garments, light armor, household goods, and furnishings. In alchemy, netch leather possesses potent properties: it can Fortify Endurance, Fortify Intelligence, and Cure Paralyzation, though it also carries the adverse effect to Drain Personality.
topic_desc_basic: A rough, thick strip of tanned hide with a pebbled surface and deep amber hue, harvested from Vvardenfell's netch. This durable, flexible skin is an important export used throughout the Empire for garments, armor, and furnishings. Alchemically, it can Fortify Endurance, Fortify Intelligence, and Cure Paralyzation, but will Drain Personality.

title: Nirthfly Stalks
topic_desc: Nirthfly stalks consist of several slender, pale green stalks bundled together, each topped with a small, rounded seed pod. In alchemical practice, the specimen yields contradictory properties regarding agility, simultaneously offering Restore Speed and Fortify Speed alongside Drain Speed. Additionally, it carries a Damage Health effect. These opposing qualities make it a delicate reagent requiring careful formulation to isolate beneficial aspects from its harmful and debilitating potentials.
topic_desc_basic: Nirthfly stalks are slender, pale green stalks bundled together, each topped with a small, rounded seed pod. Alchemists value them for properties that affect agility and vitality, though their effects can be contradictory and harmful if mishandled.

title: Noble Sedge Flowers
topic_desc: Noble sedge flowers are delicate pale golden flower clusters with slender green stems and narrow blade-like leaves. Prized by alchemists for their contradictory properties, they offer both restoration and fortification of agility alongside harmful effects. When consumed or prepared, they Damage Health, Restore Agility, cause Poison, and Fortify Agility. This unusual duality makes them valuable in crafting potions that enhance physical grace, though their toxicity demands careful handling.
topic_desc_basic: Noble sedge flowers are delicate pale golden flower clusters with slender green stems and narrow blade-like leaves. Alchemists value them despite their toxicity, as they can Restore Agility and Fortify Agility, alongside their harmful properties.

title: Pearl
topic_desc: A lustrous, palely iridescent sphere formed from concentric nacre layers within a bivalve mollusk. These small, irregularly spherical gems with smooth surfaces and subtle pinkish overtones are occasionally produced by the cave kollop and other native Morrowind mollusks. Their natural scarcity makes them highly valued for ornamental and alchemical purposes. In practical alchemy, pearl yields Drain Agility, Dispel, Water Breathing, and Resist Common Disease. Its properties make it particularly sought after for underwater exploration and protective concoctions, though care must be taken with its debilitating effect on agility.
topic_desc_basic: A small, smooth, lustrous bead with pale iridescence and subtle pinkish overtones. Produced rarely by Morrowind mollusks like the cave kollop, pearls are scarce and prized as ornaments. Alchemists value them for their magical properties, especially those aiding underwater travel and resisting disease.

title: Pinetear
topic_desc: A small, pale green crystalline shard shaped like a pine needle with a sharp tip and faceted surface. Pinetear is a rare mineral ingredient valued for its potent magical resonance. In alchemical preparations, it provides the beneficial properties to Fortify Magicka and Restore Health, making it sought after by mages and healers. However, its crystalline structure also carries detrimental qualities that Drain Agility and Drain Endurance, requiring careful formulation to mitigate these debilitations. Its sharp, needle-like form and emerald-like appearance suggest a crystallized mineral origin rather than a botanical one.
topic_desc_basic: A small, pale green crystalline shard shaped like a pine needle with a sharp tip and faceted surface. This rare mineral ingredient is valued by alchemists for its capacity to Fortify Magicka and Restore Health, though it also carries the detrimental effects to Drain Agility and Drain Endurance.

title: Poison
topic_desc: A viscous, sickly greenish puddle of gelatinous substance seeps slowly from an unseen organic source. This rare and dangerous material is virtually useless in conventional alchemy, as its properties are entirely detrimental. Its four known effects—Weakness to Poison, Damage Health, Damage Fatigue, and Poison—are uniquely harmful, with most shared by no other known reagent, preventing the brewing of any beneficial concoction. Only two confirmed samples exist in all Vvardenfell, making it a morbid curiosity rather than a practical component.
topic_desc_basic: A viscous, sickly greenish puddle of gelatinous substance seeping from an unknown organic source. This extremely rare material is entirely harmful, possessing no beneficial alchemical properties. It serves as a morbid curiosity rather than a practical reagent.

title: Racer Plumes
topic_desc: Three slender, tapering plumes display fading hues of bluish-purple with sparse, pale central vanes. These are harvested from the cliff racer, a ubiquitous winged creature native to Vvardenfell whose plumes are widely used throughout Morrowind and the Empire as decorative trim for garments and household goods. In alchemical practice, racer plumes are prized for yielding two distinct effects: Drain Willpower and Levitate. The Levitate property makes them especially valued by alchemists and healers who prepare aerial mobility mixtures, a critical necessity for navigating Morrowind's vertical terrain and Telvanni towers.
topic_desc_basic: Plumes taken from the cliff racer, a common winged creature of Vvardenfell. They are widely used as decorative trim for garments and household goods throughout Morrowind and the Empire. Alchemists value them for their Levitate and Drain Willpower properties.

title: Rat Meat
topic_desc: A rough slab of raw, reddish meat cut from a rat, bearing irregular edges and visible sinew. Tough, greasy, and malodorous, it remains cheap, abundant sustenance when heavily spiced in stews. Alchemically, rat meat yields Drain Magicka and Paralyze, alongside the curative and protective properties Cure Poison and Resist Poison, making it a surprisingly versatile staple for healers despite its humble origin.
topic_desc_basic: A rough slab of raw, reddish meat cut from a rat, bearing irregular edges and visible sinew. Though tough and unpleasant raw, it is cheap, abundant food when stewed with spices. Alchemically, it provides Drain Magicka, Paralyze, Cure Poison, and Resist Poison.

title: Raw Ebony
topic_desc: A dense, dark shard of raw ebony exhibiting a glassy black surface with irregular, jagged edges. This extremely hard, obsidian-like substance is said to be the crystallized blood of the gods and ranks among the Empire's most precious materials. Vvardenfell holds the continent's primary deposits, heavily guarded in Imperial mines; extraction or export without a charter is illegal, making ebony smuggling a dangerous but profitable underworld trade. Cursed variants occasionally appear as Daedric shrine offerings. In alchemy, raw ebony yields Drain Agility, Cure Poison, Frost Shield, and Restore Speed.
topic_desc_basic: A dense, dark, irregularly shaped chunk of raw ebony ore with a faintly glossy, obsidian-like surface. This extremely hard, black glass-like substance is considered the crystallized blood of the gods. Vvardenfell holds most of the continent's deposits, and Imperial law strictly forbids unchartered mining or export, fueling a lucrative smuggling trade.

title: Raw Glass
topic_desc: A rough, translucent shard of pale green glass with jagged edges and an uneven, naturally fractured surface. Raw glass is less renowned than raw ebony but remains a prized commodity, valued for its light weight and flexibility. It serves as the primary material for the distinctive, elegant glass armors and weapons of High Elven design. The mineral is chiefly extracted from heavily guarded mines, with occasional specimens recovered from Dwemer ruins. In alchemical preparation, raw glass yields Drain Intelligence, Drain Strength, Drain Speed, and Fire Shield, demanding careful formulation to mitigate its debilitating properties while exploiting its protective quality.
topic_desc_basic: A rough, translucent mineral shard displaying faint greenish hues and jagged, unworked edges. Less well-known than raw ebony, this pale green glass is primarily smelted for High Elven armor and weaponry. Alchemists value it for its Fire Shield property, though its preparations also inflict Drain Intelligence, Drain Strength, and Drain Speed.

title: Raw Stalhrim
topic_desc: A jagged, translucent shard of pale blue crystalline ice, compacted into a dense, unyielding mineral block. Raw Stalhrim is a rare and enigmatic substance primarily found in the frozen barrows of Solstheim, where ancient Nordic dead are entombed within it as a sacred and enduring preservation. This peculiar material is notoriously difficult to harvest, requiring specialized tools to chip away even small fragments. In alchemy, it is highly prized for its potent and contradictory properties. When prepared correctly, it yields Resist Frost, Frost Damage, Paralyze, and Restore Health. Its enduring mystical chill and connection to preservation make it sought after by both healers and mages.
topic_desc_basic: A jagged, translucent shard of pale blue crystalline ice compacted into a dense, unyielding mineral block. Found primarily in Solstheim's Nordic barrows as an enduring burial preservative, it is exceptionally difficult to harvest. Alchemists prize it for yielding Resist Frost, Frost Damage, Paralyze, and Restore Health.

title: Red Lichen
topic_desc: A small, rough cluster of reddish fungal growth with curled, leafy lobes spreading from a central base. This hardy primitive plant endures the harsh conditions of Red Mountain, Molag Amur, and the Ashlands, where it grows on rocks. Alchemists value it for its distinctive properties: it imposes Drain Speed and Drain Magicka, while providing Light and Cure Common Disease.
topic_desc_basic: A small, rough cluster of reddish fungal growth with curled, leafy lobes. This hardy primitive plant grows on rocks in the harsh Ashlands, Molag Amur, and around Red Mountain. Healers and alchemists prize it for its curative and illuminating properties.

title: Resin
topic_desc: A translucent, amber-hued chunk of hardened resin with rough, irregular edges and a glossy surface. This vegetable-sourced substance is essential to Dunmer craftsmanship, serving as a glue and stiffener in the manufacture of their distinctive chitin and bonemold armors and weapons. In alchemy, resin yields the properties Restore Health, Restore Speed, Burden, and Resist Common Disease. It is notably one of the rare ingredients capable of conferring Restore Speed.
topic_desc_basic: A translucent, amber-hued chunk of hardened resin. This vegetable substance is used by the Dunmer as a glue and stiffener for crafting chitin and bonemold armors. Alchemists value it for its restorative and protective properties.

title: Ripened Belladonna Berries
topic_desc: A small cluster of dark purple-black berries with smooth, glossy skins and tiny green calyxes still attached. Ripened belladonna berries are harvested from the belladonna bush, a plant commonly found growing in the harsh, cold environments of Solstheim. Prized by alchemists and healers for their potent magical properties, these berries offer a complex spectrum of arcane effects. When prepared correctly, they can Resist Magicka, Restore Magicka, and Fortify Magicka, though their volatile nature also introduces the risk of a Drain Magicka effect. This paradoxical quality demands careful handling in any alchemical formulation.
topic_desc_basic: Dark purple-black berries with smooth, glossy skins and tiny green calyxes, harvested from belladonna bushes in cold northern regions. Healers and alchemists value them for their arcane properties, which can Resist Magicka, Restore Magicka, and Fortify Magicka, though they carry the risk of a Drain Magicka effect.

title: Roland's Tear
topic_desc: Roland's Tear is a rare golden-petaled flower with delicate, teardrop-shaped blossoms and slender green stems, closely resembling the common Gold Kanet in appearance. It is found growing among ordinary Gold Kanet plants, particularly near the Daedric ruin of Ald Sotha east of Vivec. Alchemists value it for its distinctive properties: Drain Health, Burden, Drain Luck, and Restore Strength. Its combination of restorative and debilitating effects makes it a noteworthy specimen in advanced alchemical practice.
topic_desc_basic: Roland's Tear is a rare golden flower nearly identical in appearance to the common Gold Kanet. It grows among ordinary Gold Kanet plants near the Daedric ruin of Ald Sotha east of Vivec. Alchemists prize it for its unusual properties, which include both restorative and debilitating effects.

title: Roobrush
topic_desc: Roobrush is a small, pale green shrub with slender, woody stems and clusters of tiny, rounded leaves. This tough, low, wiry plant thrives in the arid, poor, ashy soils of the West Gash region, where it is commonly gathered. In alchemical practice, roobrush yields contradictory properties; it can Drain Willpower and Drain Health, yet simultaneously Fortify Agility and Cure Poison. These mixed effects make it a staple for healers treating specific poisons and a hazardous component for unskilled alchemists.
topic_desc_basic: Roobrush is a small, pale green shrub with slender, woody stems and tiny, rounded leaves. This tough, wiry plant commonly grows in the arid, ashy soils of the West Gash region. Alchemists value it for its Cure Poison and Fortify Agility properties, though it also carries harmful Drain Health and Drain Willpower effects.

title: Ruby
topic_desc: A faceted, deep crimson gemstone cut into a symmetrical shape with smooth, polished faces and a pointed base. These transparent red crystals appear occasionally on the surface and more often in subterranean deposits on Vvardenfell, and are frequently encountered as offerings at Daedric shrines or within Dwemer ruins. In alchemical practice, ruby yields contradictory properties, simultaneously offering the restorative benefit of Restore Intelligence and the encumbering relief of Feather while inflicting the harmful effects of Drain Health and Drain Agility. Skilled practitioners carefully balance these opposing qualities when formulating mixtures.
topic_desc_basic: A faceted, deep red crystalline gemstone with a smooth, polished surface and angular, symmetrical cut. Rubies are transparent red gems found occasionally on the surface and more often in subterranean deposits across Vvardenfell. Alchemists value them despite their mixed properties, as they provide both beneficial and harmful effects.

title: Saltrice
topic_desc: A cluster of pale, elongated grain kernels arranged along a slender, greenish stalk. A staple crop and major export of Morrowind, saltrice is widely cultivated on southeastern plantations—historically enriching House Dres—and more recently in the Ascadian Isles, while also growing wild along the shores of the Grazelands and Azura's Coast. Commonly fermented into mazte or used as kwama feed, it also possesses modest alchemical utility. When prepared in a potion, saltrice exhibits the effects Restore Fatigue, Fortify Magicka, Drain Strength, and Restore Health, making it a familiar component in restorative mixtures despite its debilitating property.
topic_desc_basic: A cluster of pale, elongated grain kernels arranged along a slender, greenish stalk. Saltrice is a nutritious staple grain and major export crop cultivated across Morrowind's southeastern plantations, the Ascadian Isles, and growing wild along the coasts. Beyond its dietary role, it provides modest restorative alchemical properties.

title: Scales
topic_desc: Scales are small, overlapping translucent scales forming a thin, flexible patch of iridescent skin shed from some aquatic creature. Locals consider dried slaughterfish scales a crunchy treat, though foreigners are cautioned against them. In alchemy, they exhibit four distinct properties: Drain Personality, Water Walking, Restore Endurance, and Swift Swim. Their reliable Restore Endurance effect makes them particularly valued by practitioners, as few ingredients share this property.
topic_desc_basic: Scales are thin, flexible patches of iridescent skin shed from aquatic creatures, likely slaughterfish. While dried slaughterfish scales are eaten locally as a crunchy treat, foreigners are warned to avoid them. Alchemists value them for their Water Walking and Swift Swim properties.

title: Scamp Skin
topic_desc: A rough, leathery hide stripped from a scamp, bearing a wrinkled texture and mottled reddish-brown hue. The skin must be harvested while the creature remains bound to the mortal plane, a difficult process that keeps the substance scarce in alchemical stocks. When prepared, it exhibits the properties to Drain Magicka, Cure Paralyzation, Restore Personality, and Restore Strength, making it a valued curative for both physical and spiritual afflictions despite its unpleasant harvesting.
topic_desc_basic: A rough, leathery hide with a wrinkled texture and mottled reddish-brown hue, harvested from scamps. It must be taken while the creature is bound to the mortal plane. Alchemists prize it for its varied curative properties, though its difficult extraction keeps supplies limited.

title: Scathecraw
topic_desc: Scathecraw is the soft inner flesh of long, tough reddish grasses growing in the thermal ash regions of the Ashlands, Molag Amur, and Red Mountain. It appears as a cluster of dark reddish leaves gathered around a tough central stem, with curling pointed tips. Alchemists value scathecraw for its varied properties, though its harmful aspects require careful handling. When prepared, it can Cure Poison and Restore Willpower, but simultaneously inflicts Drain Health and Drain Strength upon the subject.
topic_desc_basic: Scathecraw is the soft inner flesh of tough reddish grasses found in the Ashlands, Molag Amur, and Red Mountain regions. It appears as dark reddish leaves with curling tips around a central stem. Healers value it for its ability to Cure Poison and Restore Willpower, despite its harmful Drain Health and Drain Strength properties.

title: Scrap Metal
topic_desc: Irregular shards of dark, corroded ferrous metal are jumbled together in a rough, unrefined aggregate mass. This exotic material is salvaged from the remains of animated Dwemer constructs, such as centurions, rather than being common iron or steel scrap. Found within Dwemer ruins, it is prized by collectors of antiquities and scholars of metals and enchantments. Imperial law restricts the sale and export of such Dwemer artifacts, though enforcement in Morrowind remains lax. Its considerable weight relative to market value makes it unappealing for general trade, but it retains significant alchemical utility. When prepared, it yields the effects Drain Health, Lightning Shield, Resist Shock, and Restore Intelligence.
topic_desc_basic: Irregular shards of dark, corroded ferrous metal are jumbled together in a rough, unrefined aggregate mass. This exotic material is salvaged from the remains of animated Dwemer constructs, rather than being common iron or steel scrap. Found within Dwemer ruins, it is valued by scholars and enchanters despite Imperial trade restrictions. In alchemy, scrap metal produces Drain Health, Lightning Shield, Resist Shock, and Restore Intelligence.

title: Scrib Cabbage
topic_desc: Scrib cabbage is a small, dense head of thick, tightly overlapping leaves forming a compact, rounded mass of vegetable matter. Despite its name, it is a plant rather than a product of the scrib creature. The leaves yield a complex spectrum of alchemical properties: Drain Intelligence and Damage Health make it hazardous in crude preparations, while Restore Agility and Fortify Agility render it valuable to practitioners seeking to enhance physical coordination. Healers and alchemists in Mournhold and surrounding regions prize it for these restorative and strengthening qualities, though its toxic aspects demand careful formulation.
topic_desc_basic: Scrib cabbage is a small, dense head of thick, tightly overlapping leaves forming a compact, rounded vegetable mass. Alchemists value it for properties that Restore Agility and Fortify Agility, though it also carries adverse effects including Drain Intelligence and Damage Health, requiring careful preparation.

title: Scrib Jelly
topic_desc: A translucent, pale blue gelatinous mass of thick, sticky jelly harvested from the scrib insect. Scribs are the larval form of the kwama, and this jelly is produced by crushing their flesh. Dunmer eat it readily as a nutritious if sour-tasting food, and it is commonly gathered from kwama egg mines where scribs are plentiful. Alchemists value it for its broad restorative properties: it can Fortify Willpower, Cure Poison, Cure Blight Disease, and Restore Willpower. Notably, it is one of only two commonly available ingredients that can cure blight disease, making it indispensable to healers throughout Morrowind. Its complete absence of adverse side effects further simplifies its use in potion-making.
topic_desc_basic: A pale blue jelly harvested from the scrib, the larval form of the kwama. Dunmer eat it as a nutritious food despite its sour taste.
